name: A Song of Ice and Fire/Game of Thrones Lorebook
description: A comprehensive lorebook for the A Song of Ice and Fire universe. Covers the Dawn Age, Age of Heroes, Targaryen Dynasty (House of the Dragon), Blackfyre Rebellions, and the Main Series. Includes detailed entries for Characters, Great Houses, Castles, Battles, Artifacts, Magic, etc. Formatted in JSON for SillyTavern with recursive scanning in mind.

1.content: History of Westeros: A timeline spanning over twelve thousand years, beginning with the Dawn Age. It is categorized by major shifts in power and migration, including the arrival of the First Men, the Andal invasion, and the three-century reign of the Targaryen dynasty. Much of the early record is surviving runes or later histories compiled by septons and maesters, the accuracy of which is often debated at the Citadel.
1.name: Lore: Overview of Westerosi History

2.content: Dawn Age: An indeterminate era before the coming of man when Westeros was inhabited solely by the Children of the Forest and giants. The Children worshipped nameless gods of forest and stone. It ended approximately 12,000 years ago when the First Men invaded from Essos via the Arm of Dorne, leading to two thousand years of warfare until the signing of the Pact at the Isle of Faces.
2.name: Lore: The Dawn Age

3.content: Age of Heroes: A legendary era following the Pact, characterized by four thousand years of peace and prosperity between the First Men and the Children of the Forest. This period saw the foundation of the Great Houses, including the Starks, Lannisters, and Durrandons. It was punctuated by the Long Night, a generation-long winter and invasion by the Others, eventually repelled by the first members of the Night's Watch.
3.name: Lore: The Age of Heroes

4.content: Andal Invasion: A massive migration of the Andal people from Essos to Westeros, occurring between 6,000 and 2,000 years ago. Driven by the vision of the Seven, the Andals utilized steel weapons to conquer the southern kingdoms of the First Men, destroying weirwoods and establishing the Faith of the Seven. The North remained the only region to successfully resist the invasion due to the defenses of Moat Cailin.
4.name: Lore: The Andal Invasion

5.content: Valyrian Freehold: An advanced civilization in Essos that became the dominant military and cultural power of the known world for five millennia. Ruled by forty noble families of dragonlords, the Freehold utilized dragons and blood magic to conquer the Old Empire of Ghis and the Rhoynar. It was characterized by topless towers, Valyrian steel, and the practice of slavery and incest to preserve blood purity.
5.name: Lore: Valyrian Freehold

6.content: Doom of Valyria: A cataclysmic event in 102 BC that destroyed the Valyrian peninsula and caused the collapse of the Freehold. The eruption of the Fourteen Flames filled the air with ash and smoke, killing dragons and shattering the land into the Smoking Sea. Spells, knowledge, and history were largely lost, leaving House Targaryen of Dragonstone as the only surviving dragonlords.
6.name: Lore: The Doom of Valyria

7.content: War of Conquest: The military campaign (2 BC – 1 AC) led by Aegon I Targaryen and his sister-wives, Visenya and Rhaenys, to unite the Seven Kingdoms. Utilizing three dragons—Balerion, Vhagar, and Meraxes—the Targaryens extinguished House Hoare and House Gardener, forced the submission of the North and the Vale, and established the Iron Throne. Dorne remained the only kingdom to successfully resist.
7.name: Lore: Aegon's Conquest

8.content: Faith Militant Uprising: A bloody rebellion (41–48 AC) by the military orders of the Faith against Targaryen rule, sparked by the incestuous marriage of Aenys I's children. King Maegor the Cruel responded with brutal suppression, burning the Sept of Remembrance and placing bounties on the faithful. The conflict was finally resolved by Jaehaerys I, who granted amnesty in exchange for the dissolution of the orders.
8.name: Lore: Faith Militant Uprising

9.content: Dance of the Dragons: A catastrophic civil war of succession (129–131 AC) between Rhaenyra Targaryen (the Blacks) and her half-brother Aegon II (the Greens). The conflict divided the realm and resulted in the deaths of both claimants and the near-extinction of the dragons. It concluded with the coronation of Rhaenyra’s son, Aegon III, and a permanent change to Targaryen inheritance laws favoring male heirs.
9.name: Lore: Dance of the Dragons

10.content: Conquest of Dorne: A war initiated by the fourteen-year-old King Daeron I Targaryen in 157 AC to 'complete the Conquest.' Despite initial success and the Submission of Sunspear, a massive Dornish rebellion erupted, leading to the death of Daeron I under a peace banner in 161 AC. The war cost the Iron Throne approximately sixty thousand men and ended with Dorne regaining independence until a later marriage alliance.
10.name: Lore: Conquest of Dorne

11.content: Blackfyre Rebellions: A series of five civil wars sparked by Aegon IV’s deathbed legitimization of his Great Bastards. The First Rebellion (196 AC) saw Daemon I Blackfyre challenge Daeron II for the Iron Throne. Subsequent attempts were led by Daemon's descendants and Aegor 'Bittersteel' Rivers, continuing until the male line was extinguished in the Stepstones.
11.name: Lore: Blackfyre Rebellions

12.comment: Lore: War of the Ninepenny Kings
12.content: War of the Ninepenny Kings: A conflict in 260 AC between the Band of Nine—an alliance of Essosi merchants and pirates—and the Seven Kingdoms. The alliance sought to place Maelys the Monstrous on the Iron Throne. King Jaehaerys II dispatched a host to the Stepstones, where Barristan Selmy ended the threat by slaying Maelys in single combat, finally extinguishing the Blackfyre male line.
12.name: Lore: War of the Ninepenny Kings

13.content: Robert's Rebellion: A realm-wide revolt (282–283 AC) triggered by Rhaegar Targaryen's abduction of Lyanna Stark and the execution of Rickard and Brandon Stark by Aerys II. Led by Robert Baratheon, Eddard Stark, and Jon Arryn, the rebels overthrew the Targaryen dynasty. The war ended with the Sack of King's Landing and Robert's coronation, establishing the Baratheon dynasty.
13.name: Lore: Robert's Rebellion

14.content: Greyjoy's Rebellion: An uprising in 289 AC where Balon Greyjoy declared himself King of the Iron Islands in an attempt to restore the 'Old Way.' The Iron Fleet burned the Lannister fleet at Lannisport, but the rebellion was crushed by the combined strength of Robert I and Eddard Stark. Balon was forced to kneel, and his son Theon was taken as a hostage to Winterfell.
14.name: Lore: Greyjoy's Rebellion

15.comment: Lore: War of the Five Kings
15.content: War of the Five Kings: A massive multi-theater conflict (298–300 AC) sparked by the death of Robert I and the execution of Eddard Stark. Claimants included Joffrey, Stannis, and Renly Baratheon for the Iron Throne, while Robb Stark and Balon Greyjoy fought for secession. The war devastated the Riverlands and North, resulting in the fall of Houses Stark and Tully and the rise of House Bolton.
15.name: Lore: War of the Five Kings

16.content: Battle of the Trident: The decisive engagement of Robert's Rebellion fought in 283 AC at the ruby ford. Robert Baratheon slew Prince Rhaegar Targaryen in single combat, crushing the crown prince’s chest with his warhammer. The loss of their commander caused the royalist army to break and flee, effectively deciding the fate of the Targaryen dynasty.
16.name: Event: Battle of the Trident

17.content: Field of Fire: The only battle during Aegon's Conquest where all three Targaryen dragons—Balerion, Vhagar, and Meraxes—were unleashed simultaneously. The combined dragonflame immolated over four thousand men, including King Mern IX and the entire Gardener line. King Loren I Lannister survived and surrendered the following day, leading to the submission of the Westerlands.
17.name: Event: Field of Fire

18.comment: Event: Battle of the Redgrass Field
18.content: Battle of the Redgrass Field: The final, bloodiest conflict of the First Blackfyre Rebellion (196 AC). Named for the blood-soaked terrain, it saw the deaths of Daemon I Blackfyre and his twin sons, Aegon and Aemon, at the hands of Brynden 'Bloodraven' Rivers and his Raven's Teeth. The battle was won by the 'hammer and anvil' strategy of Baelor Breakspear and Maekar Targaryen.
18.name: Event: Battle of the Redgrass Field

19.content: Battle of the Bells: A fierce street battle in Robert's Rebellion fought at Stoney Sept (283 AC). Named for the sept bells rung to warn the populace, it saw rebel forces under Eddard Stark and Hoster Tully rescue Robert Baratheon from the pursuing royalist army. The defeat led to the exile of the King's Hand, Jon Connington.
19.name: Event: Battle of the Bells

20.content: Sack of King's Landing: The final major battle of Robert's Rebellion (283 AC). Tywin Lannister's host feigned loyalty to enter the gates before turning to pillage the city. Ser Jaime Lannister slew King Aerys II to prevent the wildfire plot, while Gregor Clegane and Amory Lorch murdered Princess Elia Martell and her children, Rhaenys and Aegon.
20.name: Event: Sack of King's Landing

21.content: Red Wedding: A horrific massacre in 299 AC orchestrated by Walder Frey, Roose Bolton, and Tywin Lannister. Violating the sacred laws of hospitality, the Freys slaughtered King Robb Stark, Catelyn Stark, and thousands of northern soldiers during the wedding feast of Edmure Tully and Roslin Frey. The event effectively ended the northern rebellion.
21.name: Event: Red Wedding

22.content: Purple Wedding: The royal wedding feast of Joffrey I Baratheon and Margaery Tyrell on the first day of 300 AC. The celebration ended in the public assassination of King Joffrey, who choked to death on poisoned wine. Orchestrated by Petyr Baelish and Olenna Tyrell, the event led to the arrest of Tyrion Lannister and the flight of Sansa Stark.
22.name: Event: Purple Wedding

23.content: Aegon I Targaryen: The first Lord of the Seven Kingdoms and founder of the Targaryen dynasty. [Appearance]: Tall, broad-shouldered, and powerful, with Valyrian purple eyes and short-cut silver-gold hair. [Personality]: A charismatic but solitary warrior-king, respected by friends and foes alike. [Key History]: He conquered six of the Seven Kingdoms using his dragon Balerion and forged the Iron Throne from the swords of his enemies. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, husband to Visenya and Rhaenys.
23.name: Character: Aegon I Targaryen

24.content: Aerys II Targaryen: The last Targaryen king to sit the Iron Throne. [Appearance]: In his youth, handsome and quick-witted; in old age, skeletal and gaunt with long yellowed nails and a tangled silver beard reaching his waist. [Personality]: Initially ambitious and charming, he descended into paranoia, cruelty, and a pathological obsession with wildfire. [Key History]: His erratic behavior and execution of the Starks triggered Robert's Rebellion; he was slain by Jaime Lannister during the Sack of King's Landing. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
24.name: Character: Aerys II Targaryen

25.content: Robert I Baratheon: The first king of the Baratheon dynasty. [Appearance]: Once a towering, muscled warrior with a mane of black hair and a beard; as king, he became morbidly obese and red-faced from heavy drinking. [Personality]: Boisterous, gregarious, and a formidable commander, though he proved a disinterested and debt-ridden ruler. [Key History]: He led the rebellion to avenge Lyanna Stark and killed Rhaegar Targaryen at the Trident. [Affiliations]: House Baratheon, husband to Cersei Lannister.
25.name: Character: Robert I Baratheon

26.content: Eddard Stark: Lord of Winterfell and Warden of the North. [Appearance]: Long face, brown hair, and somber grey eyes. [Personality]: Dour, honorable, and intensely loyal to his family and duty. [Key History]: A primary leader of Robert's Rebellion, he returned North after the war to rule Winterfell until being named Hand of the King by Robert I. [Affiliations]: House Stark, husband to Catelyn Tully.
26.name: Character: Eddard Stark

27.content: Essos: The largest of the three known continents, located east of Westeros across the narrow sea. Its vast landscape includes the independent Nine Free Cities in the west, the central Dothraki sea grasslands, and the Ghiscari slaver cities of the south. The continent is home to diverse cultures and ancient ruins, including the remnants of the Valyrian Freehold and the mysterious Further East. Unlike the unified Westeros, Essos is divided into numerous sovereign city-states and regions. Its climate varies from temperate coastlines to the sweltering jungles of Yi Ti and the arid Red Waste.
27.name: Location: Essos

28.content: The North: The largest province of the Seven Kingdoms, a sparsely populated wilderness of forests, pine-covered hills, and snowcapped mountains. It is ruled by House Stark from Winterfell, an ancient line that reigned as Kings of Winter for eight thousand years before submitting to the Iron Throne. The region is defined by a harsh, cold climate where it may snow even in summer, and its people primarily follow the old gods of the forest. Natural defenses include the marshy isthmus of the Neck to the south and the Wall to the far north. Inhabitants are known for traits such as long faces and grey eyes, and noble bastards born here take the surname Snow.
28.name: Location: The North

29.content: The Reach: The second largest and most fertile region of Westeros, serving as the realm's agricultural heart. It is ruled by House Tyrell of Highgarden, who formerly served as hereditary stewards to the extinct House Gardener. The region is the center of chivalry in the Seven Kingdoms and is home to Oldtown, the oldest city and the seat of the Maesters' Citadel. Its military power is significant, capable of fielding the largest armies and commanding the massive Redwyne fleet. Noble bastards of the Reach are given the surname Flowers.
29.name: Location: The Reach

30.content: The Westerlands: A hilly and mountainous region west of the riverlands, known for possessing the richest gold and silver mines on the continent. It is ruled by House Lannister from Casterly Rock, a colossal stronghold carved into a stone hill overlooking the Sunset Sea. The region's principal port is the city of Lannisport, famous for its goldsmiths. The Lannisters traditionally hold the title of Warden of the West and are recognized as the wealthiest of the Great Houses. Bastards of noble birth in this region take the surname Hill.
30.name: Location: The Westerlands

31.content: The Riverlands: A fertile and central region of Westeros defined by the multiple forks of the Trident river. It is ruled by House Tully from Riverrun, a three-sided castle situated at the confluence of the Tumblestone and the Red Fork. Historically, the region lacked a unified crown and was often contested or ruled by ironmen and storm kings. The area is known for its many large towns, such as Maidenpool and Fairmarket, but contains no major cities. Noble bastards born in the riverlands are given the surname Rivers.
31.name: Location: The Riverlands

32.content: The Stormlands: A region located south of King's Landing, characterized by harsh mountains, verdant forests like the rainwood, and stony shores. It is ruled by House Baratheon from Storm's End, a legendary fortress on Shipbreaker Bay said to be protected by ancient magic. The region includes the Dornish Marches, a historically war-torn border zone between the Reach and Dorne. Its people are known for mercurial tempers and powerful builds. Noble bastards in the stormlands take the surname Storm.
32.name: Location: The Stormlands

33.content: The Vale of Arryn: A mountainous region on the eastern coast of Westeros, almost entirely surrounded by the jagged Mountains of the Moon. It is ruled by House Arryn from the Eyrie, an unassailable castle perched high atop the Giant's Lance. The Arryns claim to be the oldest and purest line of Andal nobility, tracing their descent to the first King of Mountain and Vale, Artys Arryn. The region's primary port is Gulltown, the largest settlement in the Vale. Noble bastards of the Vale are given the surname Stone.
33.name: Location: The Vale of Arryn

34.content: Dorne: The southernmost and hottest region of Westeros, featuring the continent's only desert. It is ruled by House Martell from Sunspear, with the lords uniquely styling themselves as 'Prince' or 'Princess' in the Rhoynish fashion. The Dornish are culturally and ethnically distinct from other Westerosi due to the mass migration of the Rhoynar under Queen Nymeria. Dorne was the only kingdom to successfully resist the Targaryen conquest, eventually joining the Seven Kingdoms through marriage. Noble bastards in this region take the surname Sand.
34.name: Location: Dorne

35.content: Iron Islands: An archipelago of seven major, barely-fertile islands off the western coast of Westeros. They are inhabited by the ironborn, a fierce seafaring people who follow the Old Way of reaving and the religion of the Drowned God. Ruled by House Greyjoy from the castle of Pyke, they once held dominion over much of the western coast and the riverlands. The islands are characterized by a cold, grey, and stormy climate. Noble bastards of the Iron Islands take the surname Pyke.
35.name: Location: Iron Islands

36.content: The Crownlands: A region on the east coast of Westeros ruled directly by the Iron Throne. It centers on the capital city of King's Landing and includes surrounding areas such as Duskendale, Rosby, and the islands of Dragonstone and Driftmark. The province was established after Aegon's Conquest, serving as the royal seat for the Targaryen and later Baratheon dynasties. It is characterized by its proximity to Blackwater Bay and the narrow sea. Noble bastards in the crownlands take the surname Waters.
36.name: Location: The Crownlands

37.content: Beyond the Wall: A wild and uncharted territory in the extreme north of Westeros, separated from the Seven Kingdoms by the Wall. It is home to the free folk (wildlings) and legendary creatures such as giants and the Others. The geography includes the massive haunted forest, the Frostfangs mountain range, and the frozen Lands of Always Winter. The climate is perpetually harsh and bitter, with only small, settled communities surviving in the wilderness. It is a lawless land where strength is the only authority recognized.
37.name: Location: Beyond the Wall

38.content: King's Landing: The capital of the Seven Kingdoms, a sprawling walled city located at the mouth of the Blackwater Rush. It houses the Red Keep, the royal residence containing the Iron Throne, situated atop Aegon's High Hill. The city is the most populous in Westeros, home to approximately 500,000 residents, and is known for its unsightly conditions and pervasive stench. Notable locations include the Great Sept of Baelor on Visenya's Hill and the ruinous Dragonpit on the Hill of Rhaenys. It is policed by the City Watch, distinguished by their golden cloaks.
38.name: Location: King's Landing

39.content: Winterfell: The ancient seat of House Stark and the regional capital of the North. Built by Brandon the Builder in the Age of Heroes, the massive castle complex is situated over natural hot springs that heat its walls through a system of pipes. It contains a three-acre ancient godswood and cavernous underground crypts housing the statues of previous Stark kings and lords. The castle is protected by two massive granite walls and a wide moat. Outside its gates lies the winter town, which fills with smallfolk during the long winters.
39.name: Location: Winterfell

40.content: Oldtown: The oldest and richest city in Westeros, located at the mouth of the Honeywine in the Reach. It is ruled by House Hightower from the Hightower, a massive stepped lighthouse that serves as the tallest tower in the world. The city is the intellectual and religious heart of the realm, housing the Citadel of the maesters and the Starry Sept. Its streets are cobbled and its architecture is largely stone, smelling of flowers and perfume. Despite its wealth, it has been surpassed in population by King's Landing.
40.name: Location: Oldtown

41.content: Braavos: The wealthiest and most powerful of the Free Cities, built across a hundred islands in a vast northern lagoon. It was founded by escaped slaves fleeing the Valyrian Freehold and is ruled by an elected Sealord. The city is guarded by the massive stone Titan of Braavos and is home to the powerful Iron Bank and the guild of the Faceless Men. Braavos is characterized by its stone architecture, lack of trees, and a culture of dueling bravos and refined water dancers. Slavery is strictly forbidden by the First Law of Braavos.
41.name: Location: Braavos

42.content: Valyria: The ruined capital of the Valyrian Freehold, once the greatest civilization in the known world. At its peak, it featured topless towers, dragons, and sorcery rooted in blood and fire. The city and its freehold were destroyed in a single day by the cataclysmic Doom of Valyria in 102 BC, which shattered the peninsula into islands and created the Smoking Sea. The area is now considered demon-haunted and accursed, though it reportedly still contains treasures like Valyrian steel and glass candles. It is the ancestral home of House Targaryen.
42.name: Location: Valyria

43.content: Asshai: A massive and mysterious port city in the far southeast of Essos, situated where the Ash river meets the Jade Sea. Its buildings and walls are constructed of greasy, light-drinking black stone, giving the city a dark and gloomy atmosphere. Asshai is a center for arcane knowledge, where shadowbinders, necromancers, and warlocks practice forbidden arts without restraint. There are no children in the city, and the inhabitants all wear masks or veils. It is the alleged origin point of both dragons and the prophecy of Azor Ahai.
43.name: Location: Asshai

key: Shield of the realms of men
44.content: The Wall: A monumental fortification of ice, stone, and ancient magic stretching 100 leagues across the northern border of the Seven Kingdoms. It stands seven hundred feet tall and was raised by Brandon the Builder during the Age of Heroes to protect the realms of men from the Others. The Wall is guarded by the Night's Watch, who maintain nineteen castles along its southern base, though only three remain manned. It is said that the Wall can only be brought down by the legendary Horn of Winter.
keys: Shield of the realms of men
44.name: Lore: The Wall

45.content: Night's Watch: An ancient military order dedicated to guarding the Wall and defending the Seven Kingdoms from threats beyond. Its members, known as 'black brothers,' take lifelong vows to hold no lands, marry no wives, and father no children. The Watch is divided into three orders: rangers (warriors), builders (maintainers), and stewards (support). Once a powerful force of ten thousand, its numbers have dwindled to fewer than a thousand, largely composed of criminals and outcasts. They remain neutral in the wars of the realm, honoring all kings but obeying none.
45.name: Organization: Night's Watch

46.content: Kingsguard: An elite order of seven sworn knights dedicated to the lifelong protection of the monarch and the royal family. Founded by Aegon I and Visenya Targaryen, their vows are modeled on those of the Night's Watch, forbidding them from marriage, titles, or land. They are distinguished by their all-white armor, cloaks, and unblazoned white shields. The Lord Commander of the Kingsguard serves as a key member of the small council. Their history and deeds are recorded in the White Book, kept within the White Sword Tower of the Red Keep.
46.name: Organization: Kingsguard

47.content: Maesters: A secular order of scholars, healers, and advisors who serve the nobility of Westeros. They are trained at the Citadel in Oldtown, where they earn metal links for a collar that signifies their mastery of various subjects, such as healing, history, and ravenry. Upon taking their vows, they renounce their house names and commit to a life of service and celibacy. They serve as the primary source of scientific and historical knowledge in the Seven Kingdoms, having largely supplanted the Alchemists' Guild. The order is led by Archmaesters who sit on the Conclave.
47.name: Organization: Maesters

48.content: The Citadel: A massive complex of buildings in Oldtown that serves as the headquarters and training center for the Order of Maesters. It is considered the greatest repository of knowledge in the known world, housing a vast library and the Ravenry. The institution is funded by taxes from Oldtown and payments from lords for maester services. It contains four glass candles brought from Valyria, used in the final vigil of acolytes. The Citadel's Conclave of archmaesters determines the changing of the seasons and elects the Grand Maester.
48.name: Location: The Citadel

49.content: Faith of the Seven: The dominant religion of the Seven Kingdoms, brought to Westeros by the Andal invaders. It teaches that there is one god with seven aspects: the Father (justice), Mother (mercy), Warrior (courage), Smith (labor), Maiden (innocence), Crone (wisdom), and Stranger (death). Worshippers pray in seven-walled buildings called septs, led by septons and septas. The religion is headed by the High Septon and a council of high-ranking clergy known as the Most Devout. Its military branch, the Faith Militant, consists of the Warrior's Sons and the Poor Fellows.
49.name: Religion: Faith of the Seven

50.content: Old Gods of the Forest: An ancient, nameless religion practiced by the Children of the Forest and later the First Men. It is centered on the worship of the gods of forest, stream, and stone, particularly through weirwood trees with carved faces known as heart trees. Worship typically occurs in godswoods, where followers believe the gods watch through the eyes of the trees. The religion has no priests, holy books, or formal ceremonies, though it is used to witness oaths and marriages. It remains the dominant faith in the North and among the free folk beyond the Wall.
50.name: Religion: Old Gods

key: What is dead may never die
He Who Dwells Beneath the Waves
51.content: Drowned God: The primary deity of the ironborn, whose worship justifies their culture of reaving and the 'Old Way'. He is believed to have created the ironborn in his image to hold dominion over the seas. Priests of the order, who wear mottled robes and carry waterskins of seawater, perform ritual drowning and resuscitation using the 'kiss of life'. The religion is defined by its struggle against the Storm God, who dwells in the sky and sends lashing rains. Its central mantra is 'What is dead may never die, but rises again, harder and stronger'.
keys: What is dead may never die
He Who Dwells Beneath the Waves
51.name: Religion: Drowned God

52.content: Lord of Light: A dualistic religion centered on R'hllor, the god of fire, light, and life, and his nemesis, the Great Other. Popular in Essos but rare in Westeros, its priests are known for wearing red robes and seeing visions in the flames of nightfires. The faith emphasizes that 'the night is dark and full of terrors' and prophesies the return of the hero Azor Ahai. Worshippers often use blood sacrifice and burning to appease their god, believing fire to be a cleansing force. It is associated with magical feats such as raising the dead and birthing shadow assassins.
52.name: Religion: Lord of Light

53.content: Faceless Men: A religious society of elite assassins based in the House of Black and White in Braavos. They worship the Many-Faced God, whom they believe to be the singular god of death present in all religions. For a high price, they grant the 'gift' of death to any marked target, often making the killing appear accidental. Members undergo rigorous training to discard their identities and become 'no one,' utilizing magical masks made from the cured faces of the dead. They are associated with the High Valyrian phrases 'valar morghulis' and 'valar dohaeris'.
53.name: Organization: Faceless Men

54.content: Magic: A potent but little-understood supernatural force rooted in blood and fire. Often dismissed as myth or 'higher mysteries' by the Citadel, its power faded significantly after the Doom of Valyria and the death of the last dragons. Forms include elemental control (pyromancy, water magic), divination (greensight, dragon dreams), and the rare ability of skinchanging. Practitioners such as warlocks, red priests, and shadowbinders inhabit the lands of the Jade Sea and Asshai. The recent hatching of Daenerys Targaryen’s dragons is linked to a resurgence of magical potency across the world.

55.content: Dragons: Ferocious, magical reptilian creatures used as weapons of war by the dragonlords of the Valyrian Freehold. They possess scales harder than horn and breathe devastating fire that can melt steel and stone. Dragons never stop growing as long as they are free and well-fed, reaching sizes capable of swallowing mammoths whole. Though thought extinct for over a century following the death of the last sickly specimen during the reign of Aegon III, three new dragons were hatched by Daenerys Targaryen in the Dothraki sea. They are the source of House Targaryen’s historical power and are intrinsically tied to the resurgence of magic.
55.name: Lore: Dragons

56.content: Others: A malevolent race of humanoid beings from the polar Lands of Always Winter beyond the Wall. Tall and gaunt, they have milk-white flesh and eyes of burning blue fire. They wear reflective, camouflaging armor that shifts color and wield thin crystal swords of ice so cold they can shatter steel. They move silently, leave no prints in the snow, and bring a white mist and extreme cold with them. Through necromancy, they reanimate dead men and animals as blue-eyed thralls known as wights. They are vulnerable only to weapons made of obsidian (dragonglass) or dragonsteel (Valyrian steel).
56.name: Lore: The Others

57.content: Children of the Forest: The original, diminutive non-human inhabitants of Westeros, known to themselves as 'the singers.' Dark and beautiful with nut-brown skin, they possessed supernatural powers over nature, dreams, and the ability to look through the eyes of weirwood heart trees. They worked no metal, instead using obsidian weapons and woven leaf clothing. After a two-thousand-year war with the First Men, they signed the Pact at the Isle of Faces, ceding the open lands to man while keeping the deep forests. They were thought extinct for millennia but a small group survives in a cave beneath a great weirwood north of the Wall.
57.name: Lore: Children of the Forest

58.content: Giants: A dwindling race of sentient, shaggy humanoids standing ten to fourteen feet tall. They possess massive strength, squat faces with tiny eyes, and bodies covered in thick fur that turns grey with age. Lacking advanced technology, they wield logs as clubs and stone axes. They are a shy folk who ride mammoths into battle and speak the Old Tongue of the First Men. Though considered extinct in the Seven Kingdoms, several hundred remained to join Mance Rayder’s host beyond the Wall. Notable individuals include Mag the Mighty and Wun Weg Wun Dar Wun.
58.name: Lore: Giants

59.content: Direwolves: Massive and powerful relatives of the wolf, growing to the size of ponies when fully matured. They have heavier builds and longer legs than standard wolves and are almost never seen south of the Wall. They are the sigil of House Stark and possess a spiritual bond with the Stark children, many of whom are skinchangers capable of entering their direwolves' minds. The current known litter was discovered as pups in the snow near Winterfell.
59.name: Lore: Direwolves

60.content: Valyrian Steel: A rare and magical metal spell-forged with dragonflame in the Valyrian Freehold. It is lighter, stronger, and sharper than any other steel, recognizable by its dark grey color and distinctive rippled patterns. The secret of its creation was lost during the Doom, though the smiths of Qohor maintain the ability to reforge existing blades through blood sacrifice. In Westeros, there are only 227 recorded Valyrian steel weapons, mostly held as priceless ancestral heirlooms by noble houses. It is one of the few substances capable of killing the Others.
60.name: Lore: Valyrian Steel

61.content: Wildfire: A volatile, flammable liquid created by the Alchemists' Guild in King's Landing. Known to the pyromancers as 'the substance,' it is a murky green liquid that burns with a brilliant emerald flame and cannot be extinguished by water. It is extremely unstable, becoming more dangerous as it ages, and can seep into materials like cloth, wood, and steel to ignite them. It burns until exhausted and is hot enough to melt knightly armor. Its creation involves secret magical rituals that have become more effective since the return of dragons.
61.name: Lore: Wildfire

62.content: Greyscale: A virulent disease that calcifies flesh, leaving it stiff, cracked, and stone-like to the touch. It primarily affects children in cold, damp climates; while often disfiguring, survivors are immune to the fatal 'Grey Plague.' In its mortal form, it begins at the extremities and slowly creeps inward, eventually causing blindness and madness as the internal organs turn to stone. It is associated with the 'stone men' who dwell in the ruins of Chroyane, said to be cursed by Prince Garin the Great against the Valyrian conquerors.
62.name: Lore: Greyscale

63.content: Aegon I Targaryen: The first Lord of the Seven Kingdoms and founder of the Targaryen dynasty. [Appearance]: Tall, powerful, and broad-shouldered with purple eyes and short silver-gold hair. [Personality]: A solitary, charismatic enigma who took no pleasure in battle despite his martial prowess; he was harsh to those who defied him but generous to those who knelt. [Key History]: He led the War of Conquest with his dragons, Balerion, Vhagar, and Meraxes, forged the Iron Throne from the swords of his enemies, and established King's Landing. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, husband to his sisters Visenya and Rhaenys.
63.name: Character: Aegon I Targaryen

64.content: Visenya Targaryen: Elder sister and wife to Aegon the Conqueror. [Appearance]: A voluptuous woman of austere beauty with silver-gold hair often braided or bound in rings and purple eyes. [Personality]: Stern, serious, and unforgiving; she was a skilled warrior rumored to dabble in dark sorceries and poisons. [Key History]: She rode the dragon Vhagar during the Conquest, wielded the Valyrian steel blade Dark Sister, and was responsible for establishing the Kingsguard to protect the royal bloodline. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
64.name: Character: Visenya Targaryen

65.content: Rhaenys Targaryen: Younger sister and wife to Aegon the Conqueror. [Appearance]: Slender, graceful, and beautiful with long, loose silver-gold hair and purple eyes. [Personality]: Playful, curious, and kindhearted; she loved music, poetry, and flying above all else. [Key History]: A dragonrider of Meraxes, she spent more time in the air than her siblings combined; she died in 10 AC at Hellholt when a Dornish scorpion bolt pierced her dragon’s eye. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
65.name: Character: Rhaenys Targaryen

66.content: Maegor I Targaryen: The third Targaryen king, known as 'the Cruel.' [Appearance]: Fearsomely strong, bull-like, with massive shoulders and a thick neck; he kept his hair short and his beard trimmed to his jaw. [Personality]: Savage, brutal, and rigid; he craved absolute mastery and showed a pathological love for violence and death from childhood. [Key History]: He usurped the throne from his nephew, brutally suppressed the Faith Militant uprising, and completed the Red Keep before executing all its builders; he was found dead on the Iron Throne. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, son of Aegon I and Visenya, rider of Balerion.
66.name: Character: Maegor I Targaryen

67.content: Jaehaerys I Targaryen: The fourth Targaryen king, whose reign lasted fifty-five years. [Appearance]: In old age, he had white hair and a long beard, appearing wise and dignified. [Personality]: Wise, fair-spoken, and open-handed; he was as learned as a maester and as pious as a septon. [Key History]: Known as the Conciliator, he ended the war with the Faith, codified the laws of the realm, and built the kingsroad; his reign is remembered as an era of unprecedented peace and prosperity. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, husband to Alysanne, rider of Vermithor.
67.name: Character: Jaehaerys I Targaryen

68.content: Viserys I Targaryen: The fifth Targaryen king, grandson of Jaehaerys I. [Appearance]: Plump and round-faced with a bushy silver-gold mustache; in later life, his girth nearly prevented him from climbing the steps of the throne. [Personality]: Amiable, peaceful, and eager to please; he hated conflict and was known for his legendary generosity. [Key History]: He presided over the height of Targaryen power; his refusal to alter the succession away from his daughter Rhaenyra set the stage for the Dance of the Dragons following his death. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, father of Rhaenyra and Aegon II, rider of Balerion.
68.name: Character: Viserys I Targaryen

69.content: Rhaenyra Targaryen: The self-proclaimed Queen of Westeros during the Dance of the Dragons. [Appearance]: Valyrian features with silver-gold hair and purple eyes; known as the 'Realm's Delight' in her youth, though she grew stout after several childbeds. [Personality]: Grasping, proud, and increasingly vindictive; she was fiercely protective of her children's claims. [Key History]: Designated heir of Viserys I, she fought her half-brother Aegon II for the Iron Throne; she briefly held King's Landing before being forced to flee and was ultimately executed by her brother's dragon. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, rider of Syrax.
69.name: Character: Rhaenyra Targaryen

70.content: Aemond Targaryen: A fierce prince of the Greens during the Dance of the Dragons. [Appearance]: Proficient swordsman who lost his right eye as a child, replacing it with a sapphire and often wearing an eye patch. [Personality]: Bold, wild, willful, hot-tempered, and unforgiving. [Key History]: He claimed the legendary dragon Vhagar, served as Prince Regent and Protector of the Realm for his brother Aegon II, and was labeled a kinslayer after killing Lucerys Velaryon. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, second son of Viserys I and Alicent Hightower.
70.name: Character: Aemond Targaryen

71.content: Corlys Velaryon: The fabled Lord of the Tides and greatest seafarer in the history of the Seven Kingdoms. [Appearance]: A Valyrian nobleman of storied heritage. [Personality]: Brilliant, restless, adventurous, and intensely ambitious. [Key History]: He made nine great voyages to the Far East, accumulating enough wealth to make House Velaryon the richest in the realm. He served as Hand of the Queen to Rhaenyra Targaryen and later as a regent for Aegon III. [Affiliations]: House Velaryon, husband to Rhaenys Targaryen.
71.name: Character: Corlys Velaryon

72.content: Criston Cole: The Lord Commander of the Kingsguard whose actions precipitated the Dance of the Dragons. [Appearance]: Had coal-black hair and pale green eyes; described as exceptionally charming by the ladies of the court. [Personality]: A formidable warrior known for his mastery of the morningstar. [Key History]: Originally Rhaenyra Targaryen's champion, he became her bitterest foe, eventually crowning Aegon II in defiance of Viserys I's will. [Affiliations]: House Cole, Kingsguard, the Greens.
72.name: Character: Criston Cole

73.content: Aegon IV Targaryen: The eleventh Targaryen king, widely considered the worst to sit the Iron Throne. [Appearance]: Began as a handsome youth but ended his reign as a bloated, morbidly obese man with eyes lost in the fat of his face. [Personality]: Decadent and corrupt; his lusts and gluttony ruled him entirely. [Key History]: He sired scores of bastards and legitimized them on his deathbed, sparking generations of Blackfyre Rebellions. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, husband to Naerys Targaryen.
73.name: Character: Aegon IV Targaryen

74.content: Daemon I Blackfyre: The first Blackfyre Pretender and founder of House Blackfyre. [Appearance]: Tall and powerful with silver-gold hair and deep purple eyes, possessing an almost inhuman beauty. [Personality]: A peerless warrior who many felt was the true image of the Conqueror. [Key History]: He was gifted the sword Blackfyre by his father Aegon IV, eventually leading a massive rebellion against his half-brother Daeron II. [Affiliations]: House Blackfyre, legitimized son of Aegon IV and Daena Targaryen.
74.name: Character: Daemon I Blackfyre

75.content: Aegor Rivers: A legitimized Great Bastard of Aegon IV and the founder of the Golden Company. [Appearance]: Had the purple eyes of the dragon and the black hair of House Bracken; a lean, muscular warrior who never smiled. [Personality]: Angry, hard, and easily offended; he lived only for war. [Key History]: He championed the Blackfyre cause, dueled his rival Bloodraven at the Redgrass Field, and maintained the exile of the Blackfyres in Essos. [Affiliations]: House Bracken, Golden Company.
75.name: Character: Aegor Rivers

76.content: Brynden Rivers: A sorcerous Great Bastard who served as Hand of the King and Lord Commander of the Night's Watch. [Appearance]: An albino with milk-white skin, long white hair, and one red eye; he bore a raven-shaped winestain birthmark on his cheek. [Personality]: Cunning, sinister, and enigmatic; he effectively ruled with spies and spells. [Key History]: He commanded the Raven's Teeth, slew Daemon Blackfyre, and eventually became the last greenseer. [Affiliations]: House Blackwood, Night's Watch.
76.name: Character: Brynden Rivers

77.content: Shiera Seastar: The last of the Great Bastards and the most beautiful woman of her age. [Appearance]: Heart-shaped face with long, curly silver-gold hair and mismatched eyes of blue and green. [Personality]: A renowned seductress and polyglot reputed to practice the dark arts. [Key History]: The longtime paramour of Bloodraven, she was also the focus of intense rivalry between him and Bittersteel. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, daughter of Aegon IV and Serenei of Lys.
77.name: Character: Shiera Seastar

78.content: Aerys II Targaryen: The seventeenth and final Targaryen king to sit the Iron Throne. [Appearance]: In his madness, he became skeletal and gaunt, with matted waist-length hair and nine-inch yellow fingernails. [Personality]: Initially charming but descended into paranoia, cruelty, and an obsession with wildfire and execution by fire. [Key History]: His reign collapsed after the Defiance of Duskendale and the execution of the Starks, leading to Robert's Rebellion. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
78.name: Character: Aerys II Targaryen

79.content: Rhaegar Targaryen: The last Prince of Dragonstone and heir to the Iron Throne. [Appearance]: Tall and beautiful with dark purple eyes and silver hair; he wore night-black plate armor encrusted with rubies. [Personality]: Intelligent, bookish, and a skilled musician, though he was marked by a deep-seated melancholy. [Key History]: He believed himself to be the Prince That Was Promised, won the Tourney at Harrenhal, and died at the Trident. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, husband to Elia Martell.
79.name: Character: Rhaegar Targaryen

80.content: Arthur Dayne: A legendary Kingsguard knight and Rhaegar Targaryen's closest friend. [Appearance]: Often depicted with the pale greatsword Dawn. [Personality]: Remembered as the most chivalrous warrior and finest knight of his generation. [Key History]: He defeated the Smiling Knight, won various tourneys, and died at the tower of joy defending Rhaegar's secrets. [Affiliations]: House Dayne, Kingsguard.
80.name: Character: Arthur Dayne

81.content: Barristan Selmy: A celebrated hero and veteran of the Kingsguard across multiple reigns. [Appearance]: Tall with pale blue eyes; in old age, he has white hair but remains as strong and graceful as in his youth. [Personality]: Determining, dutiful, and single-minded in his pursuit of knightly honor. [Key History]: He slew Maelys the Monstrous, rescued Aerys II from Duskendale, and later joined Daenerys Targaryen in exile. [Affiliations]: House Selmy, Kingsguard, Queensguard.
81.name: Character: Barristan Selmy

82.content: Tywin Lannister: The calculating Lord of Casterly Rock and former Hand of the King. [Appearance]: Tall with golden hair and emerald eyes; he remained imposing and powerful well into his later years. [Personality]: Cold, brilliant, and ruthless, valuing the legacy of House Lannister above all else. [Key History]: He restored Lannister power by crushing the Reyne-Tarbeck revolt and sacked King's Landing to end Robert's Rebellion. [Affiliations]: House Lannister.
82.name: Character: Tywin Lannister

83.content: Robert I Baratheon: The first king of the Baratheon dynasty and a formidable warrior. [Appearance]: In his youth, a towering giant with coal-black hair and blue eyes; in age, he grew red-faced and morbidly obese. [Personality]: Gregarious, boisterous, and a natural leader on the battlefield, but a disinterested and debt-ridden ruler. [Key History]: He led the rebellion to avenge Lyanna Stark and personally slew Rhaegar Targaryen at the Trident. [Affiliations]: House Baratheon, husband to Cersei Lannister.
83.name: Character: Robert I Baratheon

84.content: Jon Arryn: The Lord of the Eyrie and the foster-father of Robert Baratheon and Eddard Stark. [Appearance]: Broad-shouldered with blue eyes and blond hair as a younger man. [Personality]: A wise mentor and stabilizing influence who was considered the soul of the realm. [Key History]: He raised his banners in rebellion to protect his wards and served as Hand of the King for fourteen years before being poisoned. [Affiliations]: House Arryn, husband to Lysa Tully.
84.name: Character: Jon Arryn

85.content: Hoster Tully: The proud and former active Lord of Riverrun and Lord Paramount of the Trident. [Appearance]: In his youth, tall and broad with auburn hair and blue eyes; in old age, he grew thin and white-haired from illness. [Personality]: Restless and ambitious, he spent his life securing the future of his House through marriage alliances. [Key History]: He sided with the rebels in Robert's Rebellion and later suffered a long, terminal illness. [Affiliations]: House Tully, father to Catelyn, Lysa, and Edmure.
85.name: Character: Hoster Tully

86.content: Mace Tyrell: The Lord of Highgarden and Warden of the South. [Appearance]: A handsome man who has turned fat, with curly brown hair and a triangular beard. [Personality]: Amiable but often seen as an oafish figure who claims the military successes of his bannermen. [Key History]: He besieged Storm's End during Robert's Rebellion and later sought to make his daughter Margaery a queen. [Affiliations]: House Tyrell, father to Willas, Garlan, Loras, and Margaery.
86.name: Character: Mace Tyrell

87.content: Doran Martell: The patient and calculating Prince of Dorne and Lord of Sunspear. [Appearance]: Body is soft and shapeless, his joints severely swollen and reddened by gout, leaving him unable to walk. [Personality]: Complaisant and sweet-smelling on the outside, but hiding a lethal and vengeful nature beneath. [Key History]: He has spent years working for the downfall of Tywin Lannister to avenge his sister Elia. [Affiliations]: House Martell, father to Arianne, Quentyn, and Trystane.
87.name: Character: Doran Martell

88.content: Balon Greyjoy: The hard and bitter Lord of the Iron Islands who sought to restore the Old Way. [Appearance]: Gaunt with a hard face, hard black eyes, and long grey hair flecked with white. [Personality]: Fierce, fearless, and stubborn; he paid the iron price for his crowns. [Key History]: He led two rebellions against the Iron Throne, the first crushed by Robert Baratheon and the second during the War of the Five Kings. [Affiliations]: House Greyjoy, father to Rodrik, Maron, Asha, and Theon.
88.name: Character: Balon Greyjoy

89.content: Jon Snow: The acknowledged bastard of Eddard Stark and 998th Lord Commander of the Night's Watch. [Appearance]: Slender and graceful with long face, dark hair, and grey eyes; he looks more like a Stark than any of his half-siblings. [Personality]: Solemn, guarded, and observant, he resented his bastardy but remained dedicated to honor. [Key History]: He joined the Night's Watch, infiltrated the wildlings, and was elected Lord Commander to defend the Wall. [Affiliations]: House Stark, Night's Watch.
89.name: Character: Jon Snow

90.content: Daenerys Targaryen: The last legitimate scion of House Targaryen and Queen of Meereen. [Appearance]: Classic Valyrian features with violet eyes and long silver-gold hair; slender and beautiful. [Personality]: Proud, strong, and fierce; she survived exile and hatched three dragons. [Key History]: She rose from an impoverished exile to become the Mother of Dragons, conqueror of Slaver's Bay, and claimant to the Iron Throne. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, widow of Khal Drogo.
90.name: Character: Daenerys Targaryen

91.content: Tyrion Lannister: The sharp-witted dwarf son of Tywin Lannister. [Appearance]: Stunted legs, mismatched eyes of green and black, and fair flaxen hair. [Personality]: Highly intelligent, cynical, and amoral, yet capable of surprising kindness and loyalty. [Key History]: He served as acting Hand of the King during the Battle of the Blackwater, was falsely accused of regicide, and escaped into exile. [Affiliations]: House Lannister, Second Sons.
91.name: Character: Tyrion Lannister

92.content: Cersei Lannister: The strikingly beautiful and ambitious Queen Dowager. [Appearance]: Golden hair and emerald green eyes with a slender, graceful figure. [Personality]: Fiercely protective of her children, proud, and increasingly paranoid. [Key History]: She orchestrated the downfall of several rivals to secure her power as Queen Regent after Robert's death. [Affiliations]: House Lannister, House Baratheon, widow of Robert I.
92.name: Character: Cersei Lannister

93.content: Jaime Lannister: A legendary and amoral knight of the Kingsguard. [Appearance]: Tall and handsome with golden hair and flashing cat-green eyes. [Personality]: Arrogant and amoral born warrior who only feels truly alive when fighting or making love. [Key History]: He earned his nickname by slaying the Mad King Aerys II and later lost his sword hand during the War of the Five Kings. [Affiliations]: House Lannister, Kingsguard.
93.name: Character: Jaime Lannister

94.content: Arya Stark: The headstrong younger daughter of Eddard Stark. [Appearance]: Long face, brown hair, and grey eyes; often mistaken for a boy in her travels. [Personality]: Fierce, independent, and vengeful. [Key History]: After fleeing the purge in King's Landing, she wandered the Riverlands before traveling to Braavos to train as an assassin with the Faceless Men. [Affiliations]: House Stark, Faceless Men.
94.name: Character: Arya Stark

95.content: Sansa Stark: The beautiful and courtly eldest daughter of Eddard Stark. [Appearance]: Aubun hair and blue eyes, taking after her mother's Tully lineage. [Personality]: Initially naive and infatuated with songs, she became a resilient survivor of political intrigue. [Key History]: Held hostage by the Lannisters, she eventually escaped King's Landing with Petyr Baelish and hid in the Vale under an alias. [Affiliations]: House Stark, House Lannister (by marriage).
95.name: Character: Sansa Stark

96.content: Bran Stark: The second son of Eddard Stark and a powerful greenseer. [Appearance]: Auburn hair and deep blue eyes. [Personality]: Serious and inquisitive, he dreamt of being a knight before being crippled. [Key History]: Pushed from a tower by Jaime Lannister, he later fled north of the Wall to become the apprentice of the Three-Eyed Crow. [Affiliations]: House Stark.
96.name: Character: Bran Stark

97.content: Robb Stark: The eldest son of Eddard Stark and King in the North. [Appearance]: Auburn hair, blue eyes, and fair skin; powerfully built like a Tully. [Personality]: A bold and brilliant military commander who was eventually undone by political missteps. [Key History]: He led the northern rebellion to avenge his father but was murdered by his own bannermen at the Red Wedding. [Affiliations]: House Stark, husband to Jeyne Westerling.
97.name: Character: Robb Stark

98.content: Catelyn Stark: The fierce and protective Lady of Winterfell. [Appearance]: Auburn hair, blue eyes, and high cheekbones; as Lady Stoneheart, she has greyish-flesh and a slit throat. [Personality]: Deeply devoted to her family, her grief eventually transformed her into a vengeful undead leader. [Key History]: She supported her son Robb's war until their murder at the Red Wedding, after which she was resurrected by Beric Dondarrion. [Affiliations]: House Tully, House Stark, Brotherhood Without Banners.
98.name: Character: Catelyn Stark

key: The King in the Narrow Sea
99.content: Stannis Baratheon: The Lord of Dragonstone and head of House Baratheon of Dragonstone. He is a tall, broad-shouldered man with hollow cheeks, dark blue eyes, and a fringe of black hair. He is characterized by an unyielding sense of duty, justice, and a stubborn, humorless nature. After the death of his brother Robert I, he declared himself the rightful heir to the Iron Throne upon discovering the illegitimacy of Cersei Lannister's children. He adopted the faith of R'hllor under the influence of Melisandre and led his forces to the Wall to defend the Night's Watch against the wildling host.
keys: The King in the Narrow Sea
99.name: Character: Stannis Baratheon

100.content: Renly Baratheon: The youngest brother of King Robert I and the Lord of Storm's End. He is a handsome, charismatic man who strongly resembles a younger version of Robert, with coal-black hair and blue-green eyes. He served as Master of Laws on the small council before crowning himself king with the support of House Tyrell and the Reach. Though popular with the smallfolk, he was eventually assassinated by a shadow creature conjured by Melisandre. He was known for his love of fine clothing and maintained a secret romantic relationship with Ser Loras Tyrell.
100.name: Character: Renly Baratheon

key: The King on the Iron Throne
101.content: Joffrey Baratheon: The ostensible eldest son of Robert I and Cersei Lannister, actually fathered by Jaime Lannister. He is a handsome boy with blond curly hair and green eyes, possessing a cruel, arrogant, and sadistic temperament. His reign was marked by the execution of Eddard Stark, which catalyzed the War of the Five Kings. He enjoyed tormenting his betrothed, Sansa Stark, and ruled with unpredictable whim until his assassination by poison at his own wedding feast. He wielded the Valyrian steel sword Widow's Wail.
keys: The King on the Iron Throne
101.name: Character: Joffrey Baratheon

102.content: Sandor Clegane: A formidable warrior and the younger brother of Gregor Clegane. He is a massive, muscled man with a face that is gaunt on one side and a burned ruin of scars on the other, an injury inflicted by his brother. Cynical and embittered, he loathes fire and the hypocrisy of knighthood, refusing to take knightly vows even after joining Joffrey's Kingsguard. He developed a complex, protective relationship with Sansa Stark before deserting during the Battle of the Blackwater. He eventually traveled with Arya Stark before being left for dead in the riverlands.
102.name: Character: Sandor Clegane

103.content: Gregor Clegane: The Knight of Clegane's Keep and a monstrously huge primary bannerman for House Lannister. Standing near eight feet tall and weighing over thirty stone, he possesses inhuman strength and a reputation for extreme cruelty and violence. He is infamous for the murders of Elia Martell and Aegon Targaryen during the Sack of King's Landing. During the War of the Five Kings, he led the Mountain's men in pillaging the riverlands. He was mortally wounded by Oberyn Martell's poisoned spear but was seemingly resurrected by Qyburn as the silent giant Ser Robert Strong.
103.name: Character: Gregor Clegane

104.content: Brienne of Tarth: The only daughter of Lord Selwyn Tarth and a skilled warrior seeking acceptance in a society that mocks her appearance. She is over six feet tall, heavily built, with straw-colored hair and large blue eyes. Driven by a naively idealized concept of knighthood, she is intensely loyal and determined. She served in Renly Baratheon's Rainbow Guard before entering the service of Catelyn Stark. Tasked with returning Jaime Lannister to King's Landing, she was later gifted the Valyrian steel sword Oathkeeper to find the missing Stark daughters.
104.name: Character: Brienne of Tarth

105.content: Davos Seaworth: A former smuggler from Flea Bottom who became Stannis Baratheon's most loyal and honest supporter. He is a slight man with thinning brown hair and is missing the first joints of the fingers on his left hand, a punishment he accepted from Stannis for past crimes. Known for his unvarnished honesty and practical wisdom, he was elevated to Ser, Lord of the Rainwood, and Hand of the King. He famously resupplied Storm's End during Robert's Rebellion and later rescued Edric Storm from sacrifice.
105.name: Character: Davos Seaworth

106.content: Melisandre: A red priestess of R'hllor and a shadowbinder from Asshai. She is a strikingly beautiful woman with burnished copper hair, red eyes, and a heart-shaped face, always dressing in red. She wields powerful fire and shadow magic, including the ability to birth shadow assassins and see visions in the flames. Convinced that Stannis Baratheon is the messianic hero Azor Ahai reborn, she serves as his influential adviser. Her methods include the burning of idols and blood sacrifice to empower her deity.
106.name: Character: Melisandre

107.content: Mance Rayder: A former ranger of the Night's Watch who deserted to become the King-Beyond-the-Wall. He is a man of middling height with sharp eyes and long hair that has turned grey. Driven by a love for the wild and freedom, he united the disparate clans of the free folk to lead an invasion of the Seven Kingdoms to escape the Others. He is a skilled musician and used the alias Abel to infiltrate Winterfell. He was purportedly burned at the Wall, though Melisandre secretly used a glamor to disguise him.
107.name: Character: Mance Rayder

108.content: Theon Greyjoy: The heir to the Iron Islands and a former hostage and ward of Eddard Stark. Originally a lean, arrogant, and promiscuous youth with a cocky smile, he was broken physically and mentally by Ramsay Bolton's tortures. Forced to take the guise of 'Reek,' he suffered the loss of several fingers, toes, and teeth, causing him to look decades older. After betraying the Starks to seize Winterfell, he was captured by Ramsay and eventually helped Jeyne Poole escape the castle's ruins.
108.name: Character: Theon Greyjoy

109.content: Asha Greyjoy: The headstrong daughter of Balon Greyjoy and captain of the Black Wind. She is a bold, wild woman with a sharp wit and short black hair who defies traditional gender roles in Westeros. Raised by her father as his heir, she is a capable fighter and sailor who commanded the ironborn during the invasion of the North. She unsuccessfully challenged her uncle Euron for the Seastone Chair during the kingsmoot and was later taken captive by Stannis Baratheon.
109.name: Character: Asha Greyjoy

110.content: Euron Greyjoy: The King of the Isles and the North and captain of the Silence. He is a handsome man with a neat dark beard and blue lips from drinking shade of the evening, wearing a patch over a 'black eye shining with malice'. Known for his cunning, mockery, and godless reputation, he claims to have sailed the Smoking Sea to the ruins of Valyria. He seized power after the death of his brother Balon, using the magical dragon horn Dragonbinder to cement his authority during the kingsmoot.
110.name: Character: Euron Greyjoy

key: Lord Captain of the Iron Fleet
111.content: Victarion Greyjoy: The Lord Captain of the Iron Fleet and master of the Iron Victory. He is a large, powerful man with a bull's chest and grey-flecked hair, known for being a fierce warrior who wears full plate armor at sea. Though a capable commander, he is often considered dim-witted and unimaginative by his siblings. A devout follower of the Drowned God, he harbor deep resentment toward his brother Euron for the seduction of his third wife. He was dispatched by Euron to Slaver's Bay to bring Daenerys Targaryen to the Iron Islands.
keys: Lord Captain of the Iron Fleet
111.name: Character: Victarion Greyjoy

112.content: Oberyn Martell: A prince of Dorne and a formidable warrior known for his knowledge of poisons and his notorious reputation. He is a tall, slender man with a saturnine face, black 'viper' eyes, and a sharp nose. Driven by a lifelong desire to avenge the murder of his sister Elia, he traveled to King's Landing to claim a seat on the small council. He fought as Tyrion Lannister's champion in a trial by combat, mortally wounding Gregor Clegane before being killed by the Mountain in his final moments.
112.name: Character: Oberyn Martell

113.content: Arianne Martell: The heiress to Sunspear and the eldest child of Doran Martell. She is a buxom, beautiful woman with olive skin, large dark eyes, and thick black hair. Proud and ambitious, she resented her father's apparent preference for her brother Quentyn, leading her to orchestrate a failed plot to crown Myrcella Baratheon. She eventually discovered her father's long-term secret plans for vengeance against House Lannister. She is a skilled player of cyvasse and has had multiple highborn lovers.
113.name: Character: Arianne Martell

114.content: Jorah Mormont: An exiled knight and the former Lord of Bear Island. He is a burly, middle-aged man who is swarthy and balding, with a body covered in coarse black hair. He fled Westeros to escape execution by Eddard Stark for trading in slaves and later became a spy for Varys while serving Daenerys Targaryen. Despite his initial betrayal, he became a fierce protector and adviser to Daenerys, falling deeply in love with her before his eventual exile from her service.
114.name: Character: Jorah Mormont

115.content: Jeor Mormont: The 997th Lord Commander of the Night's Watch and the former Lord of Bear Island. He is an immense man with a bald, spotted head and a shaggy grey beard, possessing the strength and gruff manner of a bear. He abdicated his lordship to his son Jorah to serve at the Wall. He led the great ranging beyond the Wall to investigate the threat of the Others and was eventually murdered by his own men during the mutiny at Craster's Keep.
115.name: Character: Jeor Mormont

116.content: Samwell Tarly: A novice of the Citadel and a brother of the Night's Watch. He is a morbidly obese, dark-haired youth with a moon-shaped face and a timid, scholarly nature. Disowned by his father Randyll Tarly for his lack of martial prowess, he became the closest friend and adviser to Jon Snow. He earned the nickname 'Sam the Slayer' after killing an Other with a dragonglass dagger during the retreat from the Fist of the First Men.
116.name: Character: Samwell Tarly

117.content: Gendry: A blacksmith's apprentice and an unacknowledged bastard son of King Robert I. He is a tall, muscled youth with thick black hair and blue eyes, bearing a striking resemblance to a young Renly Baratheon. He fled King's Landing to escape the purge of Robert's bastards and traveled with Yoren toward the Wall. He later joined the brotherhood without banners and was knighted by Beric Dondarrion as the 'knight of the hollow hill'. He is stubborn, suspicious, and skilled in smithing.
117.name: Character: Gendry

118.content: Bronn: A skilled sellsword who rose to becomes the Lord of Stokeworth. He is a tall, thin man with black hair, black eyes, and a wolfish smile, noted for being as quick as a cat in combat. Pragmatic and amoral, he entered Tyrion Lannister's service after championing him in a trial by combat at the Eyrie. He was knighted for his heroism during the Battle of the Blackwater and later secured his lordship by marrying Lollys Stokeworth and eliminating potential rivals.
118.name: Character: Bronn

119.content: Ramsay Bolton: The legitimized bastard son of Roose Bolton and the self-proclaimed Lord of Winterfell. He is a big-boned man with sloped shoulders, fleshy lips, and pale eyes that mirror his father's. Notorious for his extreme sadism and cruelty, he enjoys flaying his enemies and transformed Theon Greyjoy into the broken servant 'Reek'. He forcibly married Donella Hornwood and later Jeyne Poole, who was disguised as Arya Stark, to cement his claim to the North.
119.name: Character: Ramsay Bolton

120.content: Roose Bolton: The Lord of the Dreadfort and the current Warden of the North. He is an unremarkable-looking man with pasty skin and strange, pale 'ghost grey' eyes, possessing a soft voice and a cold, remorseless nature. He is a practitioner of regular leeching and adheres to the rule of 'a peaceful land, a quiet people' through fear and discipline. He betrayed House Stark at the Red Wedding to secure his family's dominance, eventually moving the Bolton seat to Winterfell.
120.name: Character: Roose Bolton

121.content: Walder Frey: The nonagenarian Lord of the Crossing and head of House Frey. He is a bald, vulture-like man with a snot-nosed appearance, troubled by gout and a prickly, irascible temperament. Infamous for his fertility, he has sired scores of descendants across eight wives. He orchestrated the Red Wedding massacre in retaliation for Robb Stark's broken marriage pact, violating the sacred laws of guest right. He is widely considered ambitious, envious, and untrustworthy.
121.name: Character: Walder Frey

122.content: High Sparrow: The leader of the sparrows and the current High Septon of the Faith of the Seven. He is a small, scrawny man with a heavily lined face, grey hair, and callused bare feet, known for his iron will and extreme piety. Formerly a traveling septon, he rose to power by championing the smallfolk devastated by war. He negotiated the rearming of the Faith Militant with Cersei Lannister and subsequently arrested her and Margaery Tyrell for their alleged crimes.
122.name: Character: High Sparrow

123.content: House Dayne: An ancient Dornish house of First Men origin, famous for their ancestral sword, Dawn. [Seat]: Starfall. [Words]: None provided. [Sigil]: A white sword and falling star crossed on a lilac field. [Traits]: Distinctive features include violet or purple eyes and pale blond or dark hair. [History]: Founded when a meteor was followed to the site of Starfall; they formerly ruled as Kings of the Torrentine. [Affiliations]: House Martell.
123.name: House: Dayne of Starfall

124.content: House Blackwood: An ancient house of First Men origin in the riverlands that remains loyal to the old gods. [Seat]: Raventree Hall. [Words]: None provided. [Sigil]: A flock of black ravens on scarlet surrounding a dead weirwood. [Traits]: Known for their historical feud with House Bracken. [History]: They once ruled the wolfswood in the North before being driven south by the Starks. [Affiliations]: House Tully, House Stark.
124.name: House: Blackwood of Raventree Hall

125.content: House Bracken: An old house of First Men descent from the riverlands, perpetual rivals of House Blackwood. [Seat]: Stone Hedge. [Words]: None provided. [Sigil]: A red stallion on a golden escutcheon on a brown field. [Traits]: Often characterized by a choleric and easily offended temperament. [History]: They ruled the riverlands as kings during the Age of Heroes. [Affiliations]: House Tully.
125.name: House: Bracken of Stone Hedge

126.content: House Frey: A relatively young but wealthy and powerful house that controls the crossing of the Green Fork. [Seat]: The Twins. [Words]: None provided. [Sigil]: Two blue towers on a silver-grey field. [Traits]: Noted for their large family size and reputation as upstarts. [History]: Founded six centuries ago by an ennobled lord who built a bridge across the Trident. [Affiliations]: House Tully (formerly), House Lannister.
126.name: House: Frey of the Crossing

127.content: House Redwyne: A wealthy naval house from the Reach, masters of the Arbor and its world-famous vineyards. [Seat]: The Arbor. [Words]: None provided. [Sigil]: A burgundy grape cluster on a blue field. [Traits]: Frequently described as orange-haired and freckled. [History]: Claim descent from Gilbert of the Vines; they once ruled as Kings of the Arbor. [Affiliations]: House Tyrell.
127.name: House: Redwyne of the Arbor

128.content: House Cole: A minor noble house from the Dornish Marches in the stormlands. [Seat]: None provided. [Words]: None provided. [Sigil]: Ten black pellets on scarlet, representing lumps of coal. [Traits]: Produced one of the most controversial figures in history, Ser Criston the Kingmaker. [History]: Served as stewards to House Dondarrion before rising to prominence. [Affiliations]: House Dondarrion.
128.name: House: Cole (Dornish Marches)

129.content: House Strong: An extinct noble house of First Men origin that once held Harrenhal. [Seat]: Harrenhal (formerly). [Words]: None provided. [Sigil]: A tripartite pale of blue, red, and green on a white field. [Traits]: Known for producing men of immense physical strength. [History]: They were awarded Harrenhal by Jaehaerys I before being extinguished during the Dance of the Dragons. [Affiliations]: House Tully (formerly).
129.name: House: Strong of Harrenhal

130.content: House Reyne: An extinct noble house of the Westerlands, formerly the second most powerful house in the region. [Seat]: Castamere. [Words]: None provided. [Sigil]: A red lion rampant regardant on a silver field. [Traits]: Known for their pride and ultimate downfall. [History]: They were utterly destroyed by Tywin Lannister following a failed rebellion against Casterly Rock. [Affiliations]: House Lannister (formerly).
130.name: House: Reyne of Castamere

131.content: House Tarbeck: An extinct noble house of the Westerlands that shared a common fate with House Reyne. [Seat]: Tarbeck Hall. [Words]: None provided. [Sigil]: A seven-pointed star countercharged on gyronny silver and blue. [Traits]: Remembered as an ancient and formerly honorable house. [History]: They were extinguished root and branch by Tywin Lannister during the Reyne-Tarbeck revolt. [Affiliations]: House Lannister (formerly).
131.name: House: Tarbeck of Tarbeck Hall

132.content: House Blackfyre: An extinct cadet branch of House Targaryen founded by the Great Bastard Daemon Blackfyre. [Seat]: Tyrosh (in exile). [Words]: None provided. [Sigil]: A black three-headed dragon breathing black fire on a red field. [Traits]: Shared the Valyrian features of their Targaryen ancestors. [History]: They contested the Iron Throne through five rebellions until the male line was extinguished in 260 AC. [Affiliations]: Golden Company, House Bracken.
132.name: House: Blackfyre (Great Bastards)

133.content: House Seaworth: A newly made noble house of the stormlands, founded after Robert's Rebellion. [Seat]: Cape Wrath. [Words]: None provided. [Sigil]: A black ship with an onion on its sail on a pale grey field. [Traits]: Characterized by unvarnished honesty and lowborn pragmatism. [History]: Founded by the former smuggler Davos Seaworth, who was knighted for resupplying Storm's End. [Affiliations]: House Baratheon of Dragonstone.
133.name: House: Seaworth of Cape Wrath

134.content: House Clegane: A house of landed knights in the Westerlands, serving as primary bannermen to the Lannisters. [Seat]: Clegane's Keep. [Words]: None provided. [Sigil]: Three black dogs running on a yellow field. [Traits]: Produce warriors of immense size and terrifying reputation. [History]: Founded by a kennelmaster who was knighted after saving Lord Tytos Lannister from a lioness. [Affiliations]: House Lannister.
134.name: House: Clegane (Landed Knights)

135.content: Vhagar: A great she-dragon of House Targaryen, the last survivor from the days of the Conquest. [Appearance]: Bronze with greenish-blue highlights and bright green eyes; by the time of the Dance of the Dragons, she was nearly as large as Balerion had been. [Personality]: Hoary and fierce, with a roar that could shake castle foundations. [Key History]: Ridden by Queen Visenya, Prince Baelon the Brave, Laena Velaryon, and Prince Aemond Targaryen; she perished in the Battle Above the Gods Eye in 130 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
135.name: Dragon: Vhagar

136.content: Meraxes: A formidable she-dragon utilized during Aegon's Conquest. [Appearance]: Massive enough to swallow horses whole; possessed golden eyes. [Personality]: Playful yet devastating in battle. [Key History]: Ridden by Queen Rhaenys Targaryen, who spent more time in the air than her siblings combined; Meraxes was killed in 10 AC at Hellholt when a Dornish scorpion bolt pierced her eye. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
136.name: Dragon: Meraxes

137.content: Sunfyre: A magnificent male dragon known as 'the Golden.' [Appearance]: Gleaming gold scales, pale pink wing membranes, and golden flames. [Personality]: Formidable and aggressive fighter despite his relative youth. [Key History]: The mount of King Aegon II, he was severely injured at Rook's Rest, later hid at Crackclaw Point, and eventually killed the dragons Grey Ghost and Moondancer; he executed Queen Rhaenyra before dying of his wounds in late 130 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
137.name: Dragon: Sunfyre

138.content: Syrax: A large she-dragon of House Targaryen named after a Valyrian goddess. [Appearance]: Yellow scales; described as huge and formidable, though less experienced in battle than Caraxes. [Personality]: Heavily fed and kept in chains, she had not hunted for years by the time of the civil war. [Key History]: The sole mount of Queen Rhaenyra Targaryen; she was slain by a mob during the Storming of the Dragonpit in 130 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
138.name: Dragon: Syrax

139.content: Caraxes: A fierce and experienced dragon known as 'the Blood Wyrm.' [Appearance]: Blood-red, huge, and lean. [Personality]: Old, cunning, and formidable in combat. [Key History]: Originally ridden by Prince Aemon Targaryen and later by Prince Daemon Targaryen; he led the assault on Harrenhal and died in 130 AC during the Battle Above the Gods Eye while killing Vhagar. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
139.name: Dragon: Caraxes

140.content: Meleys: A swift and powerful she-dragon called 'the Red Queen.' [Appearance]: Scarlet scales and pink wing membranes. [Personality]: Extremely fast, easily outspeeding Caraxes or Vhagar in her prime. [Key History]: Ridden by Princess Alyssa Targaryen and later by Princess Rhaenys Targaryen; she was killed in 129 AC at the Battle of Rook's Rest by the combined efforts of Sunfyre and Vhagar. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
140.name: Dragon: Meleys

141.content: Vermithor: A massive male dragon known as 'the Bronze Fury.' [Appearance]: Bronze and tan scales with great wings; the largest living dragon after Balerion and Vhagar. [Personality]: Fearsome but accustomed to men. [Key History]: The mount of King Jaehaerys I, later claimed by the dragonseed Hugh Hammer; he fought at the Battle of the Gullet and died at the Second Battle of Tumbleton in 130 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
141.name: Dragon: Vermithor

142.content: Silverwing: A silvery she-dragon often paired with Vermithor. [Appearance]: Silvery scales; fire possibly blue in hue. [Personality]: Docile and relatively friendly to strangers. [Key History]: The mount of Queen Alysanne Targaryen, later ridden by the dragonseed Ulf White; she survived the Dance of the Dragons and eventually went wild in the Reach. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
142.name: Dragon: Silverwing

143.content: Tessarion: A beautiful and swift she-dragon known as 'the Blue Queen.' [Appearance]: Deep cobalt scales with copper claws, belly scales, and wing membranes; her dragonflame was also cobalt. [Personality]: Notably nimble in the air. [Key History]: Ridden by Prince Daeron the Daring; she was a major asset for the Greens during the Dance until she was put out of her misery after being mangled at the Second Battle of Tumbleton. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
143.name: Dragon: Tessarion

144.content: Seasmoke: A pale, silver-grey dragon native to Driftmark. [Appearance]: Silver-grey scales. [Personality]: Pride and passion of its first rider. [Key History]: Ridden by Ser Laenor Velaryon and later by the dragonseed Addam of Hull; he was killed at the Second Battle of Tumbleton in 130 AC while fighting Vermithor. [Affiliations]: House Velaryon, House Targaryen.
144.name: Dragon: Seasmoke

145.content: Sheepstealer: A wild male dragon with a notorious taste for mutton. [Appearance]: Muddy brown scales; an ugly and plain creature. [Personality]: Wild, skittish, and dangerous to those who approached him without offerings. [Key History]: Lived wild on Dragonstone for over seventy years before being tamed by the dragonseed Nettles; the pair disappeared together toward the end of the Dance of the Dragons. [Affiliations]: Nettles.
145.name: Dragon: Sheepstealer

146.content: Arrax: A young dragon who grew quickly during the reign of Viserys I. [Appearance]: Pearlescent white scales with a golden chest and eyes; dragonflame was yellow. [Personality]: Thriving and energetic. [Key History]: Ridden by Prince Lucerys Velaryon; he was overwhelmed and killed by Vhagar above Shipbreaker Bay in 129 AC. [Affiliations]: House Velaryon, House Targaryen.
146.name: Dragon: Arrax

147.content: Vermax: A green and orange dragon that hatched on Dragonstone. [Appearance]: Green scales and orange wing membranes. [Personality]: Growled at the sight of snow and ice. [Key History]: Ridden by Prince Jacaerys Velaryon to treat with the North and the Vale; he was killed during the Battle of the Gullet in 130 AC after being struck by a grapple. [Affiliations]: House Velaryon, House Targaryen.
147.name: Dragon: Vermax

148.content: Tyraxes: A dragon used primarily for transport during the Dance of the Dragons. [Appearance]: Pale violet scales with dark purple horns and purple flame. [Personality]: Smaller than his brothers' dragons but swift. [Key History]: Ridden by Prince Joffrey Velaryon; he was slain by a mob in the Dragonpit in 130 AC after burning scores of people. [Affiliations]: House Velaryon, House Targaryen.
148.name: Dragon: Tyraxes

149.content: Stormcloud: A young dragon who saved the life of Prince Aegon the Younger. [Appearance]: Not explicitly described, but known for his speed. [Personality]: Brave and loyal. [Key History]: When the Triarchy attacked the Gay Abandon in 130 AC, Aegon escaped on Stormcloud; the dragon delivered his rider back to Dragonstone despite being riddled with arrows and bolts, dying shortly after. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
149.name: Dragon: Stormcloud
