150.content: Morghul: A young dragon that was never ridden. [Appearance]: Black scales. [Personality]: Bound to Princess Jaehaera Targaryen. [Key History]: Kept in the Dragonpit; he was slain by the Burning Knight during the Storming of the Dragonpit in 130 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
150.name: Dragon: Morghul

151.content: Shrykos: A young dragon bound to Prince Jaehaerys Targaryen. [Appearance]: Not described. [Personality]: Never ridden. [Key History]: Kept in the Dragonpit; she was killed by a woodsman named Hobb the Hewer during the Dragonpit riots in 130 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
151.name: Dragon: Shrykos

152.content: Dreamfyre: A slender and elegant she-dragon. [Appearance]: Pale blue scales with silver markings, silver crests, and pale blue wings. [Personality]: More used to human presence than wild dragons. [Key History]: Originally ridden by Princess Rhaena, and later by Queen Helaena; she broke her chains during the Storming of the Dragonpit and died when the dome collapsed on her in 130 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
152.name: Dragon: Dreamfyre

153.content: Quicksilver: A slender she-dragon of House Targaryen. [Appearance]: Presumably silver or pale in color. [Personality]: Loyal to her riders. [Key History]: Ridden by King Aenys I and later by Prince Aegon the Uncrowned; she was killed by Balerion during the Battle Beneath the Gods Eye in 43 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
153.name: Dragon: Quicksilver

154.content: Drogon: The largest and most aggressive of Daenerys Targaryen's dragons, often compared to Balerion the Black Dread. [Appearance]: Black scales with red streaks; red eyes, horns, and spinal plates; flame is black shot with red. [Personality]: Fierce and willful. [Key History]: Hatched on the Dothraki sea from the funeral pyre of Khal Drogo; he serves as the primary mount for Daenerys Targaryen. [Affiliations]: Daenerys Targaryen.
154.name: Dragon: Drogon

155.content: Rhaegal: One of the three dragons hatched by Daenerys Targaryen. [Appearance]: Jade-green scales with bronze flecks; bronze eyes; dragonflame is orange-and-yellow shot through with veins of green. [Personality]: Strong and powerful. [Key History]: Hatched on the Dothraki sea; named in honor of Prince Rhaegar Targaryen. [Affiliations]: Daenerys Targaryen.
155.name: Dragon: Rhaegal

156.content: Viserion: One of the three dragons hatched by Daenerys Targaryen. [Appearance]: Cream-colored scales with gold horns, wing bones, and spinal crest; eyes are molten gold; flame is pale gold shot with red and orange. [Personality]: Generally the most docile of the trio. [Key History]: Hatched on the Dothraki sea; named in honor of Prince Viserys Targaryen. [Affiliations]: Daenerys Targaryen.
156.name: Dragon: Viserion

157.content: Aenys I Targaryen: The second Lord of the Seven Kingdoms. [Appearance]: Taller than his father but slender; comely with a ringed beard and curly hair. [Personality]: Amiable and kindhearted, he desired to be loved and was indecisive in the face of conflict. [Key History]: His reign was plagued by rebellions and the beginning of the Faith Militant uprising; he died on Dragonstone in 42 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, husband to Alyssa Velaryon.
157.name: Character: Aenys I Targaryen

158.content: Aegon III Targaryen: The seventh Lord of the Seven Kingdoms. [Appearance]: Tall and lean with a short beard; always dressed in black. [Personality]: Sullen, melancholic, and joyless; haunted by witnessing his mother's death. [Key History]: His reign followed the Dance of the Dragons and saw the death of the last Targaryen dragons; he focused on maintaining peace and the unity of the realm. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, husband to Jaehaera Targaryen and later Daenaera Velaryon.
158.name: Character: Aegon III Targaryen

159.content: Daeron I Targaryen: The eighth Lord of the Seven Kingdoms. [Appearance]: Handsome and clean-shaven with long hair. [Personality]: Charismatic, bold, and a brilliant military commander. [Key History]: He successfully conquered Dorne at the age of fourteen but was killed in 161 AC while discussing peace terms with the Dornish. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
159.name: Character: Daeron I Targaryen

160.content: Baelor I Targaryen: The ninth Lord of the Seven Kingdoms. [Appearance]: Ascetic and gaunt from frequent fasting; wore a crown of vines and flowers. [Personality]: Pious, holy, and fanatically dedicated to the Faith of the Seven. [Key History]: He forged a permanent peace with Dorne and built the Great Sept of Baelor, but also imprisoned his sisters in the Maidenvault; he starved himself to death in 171 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
160.name: Character: Baelor I Targaryen

161.content: Viserys II Targaryen: The tenth Lord of the Seven Kingdoms. [Appearance]: Resembled his brother Aegon III but with a more prominent nose. [Personality]: Wise, calculating, and an efficient administrator. [Key History]: Served as Hand of the King to his brother and two nephews for fifteen years, effectively ruling the realm; his own reign lasted only a single year before his death in 172 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, husband to Larra Rogare.
161.name: Character: Viserys II Targaryen

162.content: Daeron II Targaryen: The twelfth Lord of the Seven Kingdoms. [Appearance]: Spindly and round-shouldered with a slight belly. [Personality]: Scholarly, cultured, and dedicated to peaceful governance. [Key History]: He successfully brought Dorne into the realm through marriage and defeated the First Blackfyre Rebellion; he died during the Great Spring Sickness in 209 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, husband to Myriah Martell.
162.name: Character: Daeron II Targaryen

163.content: Aerys I Targaryen: The thirteenth Lord of the Seven Kingdoms. [Appearance]: Tall and thin with a long face and long, thin hair. [Personality]: Bookish and detached; more interested in scrolls and prophecy than ruling. [Key History]: He left the governance of the realm entirely to his Hand, Brynden Rivers, and failed to produce an heir before his death in 221 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, husband to Aelinor Penrose.
163.name: Character: Aerys I Targaryen

164.content: Maekar I Targaryen: The fourteenth Lord of the Seven Kingdoms. [Appearance]: Powerfully built with a square-cut beard of silver and gold. [Personality]: Stern, prickly, and a formidable warrior. [Key History]: He spent much of his life in the shadow of his brothers; he fell in battle at Starpike during the Peake Uprising in 233 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, husband to Dyanna Dayne.
164.name: Character: Maekar I Targaryen

165.content: Aegon V Targaryen: The fifteenth Lord of the Seven Kingdoms. [Appearance]: Typical Targaryen features; often kept his head shaved as a youth. [Personality]: Empathetic toward the smallfolk and determined to reform the realm. [Key History]: Traveled the realm as 'Egg' with Ser Duncan the Tall; his reign ended in the Tragedy at Summerhall in 259 AC while attempting to hatch dragon eggs. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, husband to Betha Blackwood.
165.name: Character: Aegon V Targaryen

166.content: Dark Sister: A famous longsword made of Valyrian steel. [Appearance details]: Slender blade designed specifically for a woman's hand. [Personality/Traits]: The second of two ancestral blades of House Targaryen, known for its extreme sharpness. [Key History]: Possessed by the house since before the Conquest, it was wielded by Visenya Targaryen, Prince Aemon the Dragonknight, and Brynden 'Bloodraven' Rivers before being lost. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
166.name: Item: Ancestral Targaryen Sword

167.content: Ice: The ancient, two-handed greatsword of House Stark. [Appearance details]: A massive blade of rippled Valyrian steel. [Personality/Traits]: A weapon of war and justice, described as possessing a unique, dark beauty. [Key History]: Used by Eddard Stark for executions until his arrest; after his death, it was taken by Tywin Lannister and melted down to create two new longswords, Oathkeeper and Widow's Wail. [Affiliations]: House Stark.
167.name: Item: Ancestral Stark Sword

168.content: Longclaw: The ancestral Valyrian steel bastard sword of House Mormont. [Appearance details]: A hand-and-a-half blade, half a foot longer than a standard longsword, with a pommel fashioned into a snarling wolf's head of pale stone with garnet eyes. [Personality/Traits]: Carried by the family for five centuries, it is light, old, and deadly sharp. [Key History]: Returned to Jeor Mormont by his sister after Jorah Mormont fled into exile; Jeor later gifted it to Jon Snow for saving his life from a wight. [Affiliations]: House Mormont, Night's Watch.
168.name: Item: Ancestral Mormont Sword

169.content: Dawn: The legendary ancestral greatsword of House Dayne. [Appearance details]: Forged from the heart of a fallen star, the blade is pale as milkglass and glows with a light of its own. [Personality/Traits]: Possesses the properties of Valyrian steel but is unique in origin; only a knight deemed worthy is permitted to wield it as the 'Sword of the Morning'. [Key History]: Wielded by Ser Arthur Dayne until his death at the tower of joy; it was returned to Starfall by Eddard Stark where it remains until another worthy knight arises. [Affiliations]: House Dayne.
169.name: Item: Ancestral Dayne Sword

170.content: Heartsbane: The ancestral Valyrian steel greatsword of House Tarly. [Appearance details]: A massive two-handed blade. [Personality/Traits]: An heirloom of a house old in honor, passed from father to son for near five hundred years. [Key History]: Traditionally carried by the Lords of Horn Hill; currently wielded by Lord Randyll Tarly during his campaigns. [Affiliations]: House Tarly.
170.name: Item: Ancestral Tarly Sword

171.content: Brightroar: The ancient Valyrian steel greatsword belonging to House Lannister. [Appearance details]: A storied blade of Valyrian craftsmanship. [Personality/Traits]: Symbol of the wealth and power of the Kings of the Rock. [Key History]: Lost to history when King Tommen II Lannister led an expedition to Valyria and never returned; subsequent attempts to recover it have failed. [Affiliations]: House Lannister.
171.name: Item: Lost Ancestral Lannister Sword

172.content: Lady Forlorn: The ancestral Valyrian steel longsword of House Corbray. [Appearance details]: Smoke-grey steel with a heart-shaped ruby set in its pommel. [Personality/Traits]: An ancient blade whose name predates the current steel version, originating from the Andal invasion. [Key History]: Wielded by Ser Gwayne Corbray at the Redgrass Field and currently held by Ser Lyn Corbray. [Affiliations]: House Corbray.
172.name: Item: Ancestral Corbray Sword

173.content: Red Rain: A Valyrian steel sword belonging to House Drumm. [Appearance details]: Crafted from rippled Valyrian metal. [Personality/Traits]: Implied to have been stolen by the Drumms during a raid, potentially from House Reyne given its name and coloring. [Key History]: Currently held by the Lord of Old Wyk, Dunstan Drumm. [Affiliations]: House Drumm.
173.name: Item: Ancestral Drumm Sword

174.content: Nightfall: A storied Valyrian steel longsword belonging to House Harlaw. [Appearance details]: Dark, rippled steel. [Personality/Traits]: An ancestral weapon of the most powerful house on Harlaw. [Key History]: Currently wielded by Ser Harras Harlaw, the Knight of Grey Garden. [Affiliations]: House Harlaw.
174.name: Item: Ancestral Harlaw Sword

175.content: Vigilance: A Valyrian steel longsword belonging to House Hightower. [Appearance details]: Finely crafted Valyrian metal. [Personality/Traits]: Ancestral blade of one of the oldest and richest houses in the Reach. [Key History]: Historically wielded by the Lords of Oldtown, including Lord Ormund Hightower during the Dance of the Dragons. [Affiliations]: House Hightower.
175.name: Item: Ancestral Hightower Sword

176.content: Lamentation: A Valyrian steel sword that once belonged to House Royce. [Appearance details]: Forged of rippled Valyrian steel. [Personality/Traits]: Ancestral weapon of the Bronze Kings of Runestone. [Key History]: The sword was lost during the chaos of the Storming of the Dragonpit in King's Landing during the Dance of the Dragons. [Affiliations]: House Royce.
176.name: Item: Lost Ancestral Royce Sword

177.content: Oathkeeper: A Valyrian steel longsword forged from the melted remains of the Stark blade Ice. [Appearance details]: Features grey-black and red ripples throughout the steel; the pommel is a golden lion's head with ruby eyes. [Personality/Traits]: Created to be a Lannister heirloom but gifted away to fulfill a debt of honor. [Key History]: Reforged by Tobho Mott under Tywin Lannister's orders; Ser Jaime Lannister gave it to Brienne of Tarth to aid in her quest to find the Stark daughters. [Affiliations]: House Lannister, House Stark (by origin).
177.name: Item: Lannister Longsword

178.content: Widow's Wail: A Valyrian steel longsword forged from the melted remains of the Stark blade Ice. [Appearance details]: The blade has red and black ripples; the scabbard is decorated with gold, cherrywood, and ruby-eyed lions. [Personality/Traits]: Slightly smaller than its twin, Oathkeeper, but equally sharp and deadly. [Key History]: Given to Joffrey Baratheon as a wedding gift by Tywin Lannister; following Joffrey's death, it passed to King Tommen I. [Affiliations]: House Baratheon of King's Landing, House Lannister.
178.name: Item: Lannister Longsword

179.content: Dragonbinder: A massive six-foot-long dragon horn bound with red gold and Valyrian steel. [Appearance details]: Inscribed with Valyrian glyphs that glow white-hot when the horn is sounded. [Personality/Traits]: A sorcerous artifact said to bind dragons to the horn's master, though the blower's lungs are burned to ash by its sound. [Key History]: Euron Greyjoy claims to have recovered it from the smoking ruins of Valyria; it was sounded at the kingsmoot to establish his claim. [Affiliations]: House Greyjoy, Valyria.
179.name: Item: Magical Dragon Horn

180.content: Old Empire of Ghis: An ancient and powerful empire that dominated much of Essos thousands of years before the rise of Valyria. Its capital, Old Ghis, was protected by formidable lockstep legions. The empire fought five great wars against the Valyrian Freehold but was eventually obliterated by dragonflame. Following its destruction, the Valyrians adopted the practice of slavery from the conquered Ghiscari. The surviving colonies of Slaver's Bay—Astapor, Yunkai, and Meereen—remain as remnants of its architectural and cultural legacy.
180.name: Location: Old Empire of Ghis

181.content: Kingdom of Sarnor: A region of northern Essos inhabited by the Sarnori, who styled themselves the 'Tall Men'. The kingdom consisted of a series of independent city-states, such as Sarnath and Sallosh, centered around the river Sarne. At its height, Sarnor was a major trading partner with Valyria and Yi Ti, known for using chariot teams in battle. The realm was almost entirely destroyed by the Dothraki during the Century of Blood following the Doom of Valyria. Saath remains the only surviving Sarnori settlement.
181.name: Location: Kingdom of Sarnor

182.content: Yi Ti: An ancient and legendarily wealthy nation in far eastern Essos, bordered by the Jade Sea and the Bone Mountains. It is ruled by the Golden Empire of Yi Ti, a civilization that claims descent from the mythic Great Empire of the Dawn. The land is characterized by sweltering jungles, thick farmlands, and a vast network of stone roads. Yi Ti contains more cities than any other land, many of which are significantly larger and more splendid than those in the west. Major exports include saffron, silk, and spices, which are traded as far as Pentos and Qarth.
182.name: Location: Yi Ti

183.content: Leng: A large, forested island in the Jade Sea off the southern coast of Essos, rich in spices and gemstones. The island is ruled by god-empresses who traditionally take two husbands—one of YiTish descent and one of native Lengii descent. The northern two-thirds of the island are occupied by descendants of YiTish invaders, while the native Lengii inhabit the southern third. In the depths of the island's jungles lie ruined subterranean cities inhabited by 'Old Ones'. It is strictly forbidden to enter these ruins under penalty of death.
183.name: Location: Island of Leng

184.content: Asshai: A vast and mysterious port city in the far southeast of Essos, where the Ash river meets the Jade Sea. Its buildings and walls are constructed from a light-drinking black stone that is greasy to the touch. The city is a center for arcane knowledge, where shadowbinders, bloodmages, and warlocks practice their arts without restraint. Despite its massive physical size, the population is small, and no children are ever seen in the city. All food and freshwater must be brought in by ship, as the river Ash is corrupted and black.
184.name: Location: Asshai

185.content: Shadow Lands: A mountainous and ominous region in the far east of Essos beyond the city of Asshai. It is characterized by the presence of ghost grass and the deep, narrow Vale of Shadows. Ancient tales suggest that dragons first originated in the Shadow. The native inhabitants, known as Shadow Men, cover their bodies in tattoos and wear red lacquer masks. The region is reputed to be home to demons and other twisted creatures.
185.name: Location: Shadow Lands

186.content: Stygai: A haunted corpse city located at the heart of the Shadow Lands within the Vale of Shadows. It is known as the 'City of the Night' because it only receives sunlight for a brief period around noon each day. The ruins are avoided even by shadowbinders due to the presence of demons and twisted creatures.
186.name: Location: Stygai

187.content: Qarth: An ancient and opulent port city on the southern coast of Essos, serving as the gateway between the east and west. It is the sole surviving city of the Qaathi people, protected from the Dothraki by a triple wall of engraved stone. The city is ruled by the Pureborn from the Hall of a Thousand Thrones, though powerful merchant guilds like the Thirteen and the Ancient Guild of Spicers hold significant sway. Qarth is home to the Warlocks and their seat of power, the House of the Undying. Its residents are pale-skinned and known for their extreme politeness and sophisticated culture.
187.name: Location: Qarth

188.content: Free Cities: A group of nine independent city-states in western Essos that interact frequently with the Seven Kingdoms. Eight of the cities were founded as colonies of the Valyrian Freehold, while Braavos was founded by escaped slaves. The cities are more mercantile and developed than those in Westeros. They include coastal ports like Pentos and Volantis, island cities like Lys and Tyrosh, and inland cities like Norvos and Qohor. The cities often engage in shifting alliances and conflicts over the control of the Disputed Lands.
188.name: Location: The Free Cities

189.content: Volantis: The oldest and most populous of the Free Cities, situated at the mouth of the Rhoyne. It is ruled by an elected triarchy of the Tiger or Elephant parties. The city is divided into two halves by the massive Long Bridge, with the oldest district protected by the 200-foot-high Black Walls. Only those of 'Old Blood' who can trace their lineage to Valyria may live within the Black Walls. Volantis is a center of the slave trade, with slaves outnumbering free men five to one.
189.name: Location: Volantis

190.content: Pentos: A major trading port on the western coast of Essos, largely composed of descendants of Andals and Valyrians. It is ruled by a council of magisters who choose a ceremonial Prince of Pentos. The city avoids Dothraki sackings by paying lavish tributes to passing khalasars. Although slavery is technically outlawed by treaty with Braavos, the Pentoshi keep 'servants' who are effectively slaves. It is a city of square brick towers and large red temples.
190.name: Location: Pentos

191.content: Myr: A coastal Free City renowned for its master artisans, particularly lenscrafters and lace-makers. It is considered one of the most advanced Free Cities, producing high-quality glass, carpets, and telescopes known as 'Myrish eyes'. The inhabitants often have olive skin and dark hair, leading some to suspect Rhoynish ancestry. Myr is frequently involved in wars over the Disputed Lands and is a known center for the worship of R'hllor.
191.name: Location: Myr

192.content: Lys: An island Free City known as 'Lys the Lovely,' where the blood of Old Valyria remains strong among the populace. The city is famous for its pillow houses, where slaves are trained in the erotic arts. Lys is a merchantile society where trade is esteemed over arms, and it frequently employs sellsword companies for its defense. It is a producer of fine wines, perfumes, and potent poisons such as the 'tears of Lys'.
192.name: Location: Lys

193.content: Tyrosh: A fortress harbor city in the Stepstones, ruled by an elected Archon. The Tyroshi are known for their flamboyant culture, frequently dyeing their hair and beards in bright, vivid colors. The city grew wealthy from a unique variety of sea snail used to produce high-quality dyes. Tyrosh is a major player in the slave trade and is famous for the construction of ornate armor and ingenious torture devices.
193.name: Location: Tyrosh

194.content: Norvos: An inland Free City situated in the Hills of Norvos, split between a high city on a hill and a low city beside the river Noyne. It is effectively a theocracy ruled by the bearded priests, who maintain a strict religious life governed by the ringing of three massive bells. Norvoshi culture is characterized by its sweltering summers, bitter winters, and a yearly festival featuring dancing bears. The city is known for its fine tapestries and fermented goat's milk.
194.name: Location: Norvos

195.content: Qohor: The easternmost Free City, located on the edge of a vast forest and serving as the gateway to the Dothraki sea. It is known as the 'City of Sorcerers' due to the reputed practice of dark arts. The city's smiths possess the rare ability to reforge Valyrian steel through magical spells. Qohor is famously defended by Unsullied slave soldiers, a tradition dating back to the victory of the Three Thousand of Qohor. The city's primary deity is the Black Goat.
195.name: Location: Qohor

196.content: Lorath: The smallest, poorest, and most isolated of the Free Cities, located on an archipelago in the Shivering Sea. It was founded by Valyrian worshippers of the blind god Boash, whose cult practiced extreme self-abnegation and equality. This religious legacy persists in the Lorathi habit of using indefinite pronouns rather than personal names. The islands are dotted with ancient stone mazes built by the extinct Mazemakers. Its economy relies primarily on salt cod, walrus tusks, and whale oil.
196.name: Location: Lorath

197.content: Braavos: The wealthiest and most powerful Free City, built on a hundred islands in a foggy lagoon. Founded by escaped slaves, it is the home of the Iron Bank and the Faceless Men. The city is guarded by the Titan of Braavos, a massive stone and bronze fortress that serves as a lighthouse. Braavos is a center of tolerance where all gods are honored, though the Moonsingers are given special prominence for leading the founders to safety. Slavery is strictly forbidden within its domains by the First Law.
197.name: Location: Braavos

198.content: Summer Isles: An archipelago in the Summer Sea south of Westeros. The islands are inhabited by a brown-skinned people known as Summer Islanders, who are famed as explorers and master shipbuilders. They are rumored to have extensively mapped the southern coasts of Sothoryos. Their warriors often utilize feathered cloaks and powerful bows made of goldenheart.
198.name: Location: Summer Isles

199.content: Naath: A fertile island off the northwestern coast of Sothoryos, known as the 'Isle of Butterflies'. It is home to the Naathi, a peaceful people who refuse to kill any living creature. The island is protected by 'butterfly fever,' a fatal disease carried by local butterflies that kills all outsiders who remain on the island for more than a year. Despite this defense, Naath is frequently raided by slavers from the Basilisk Isles.
199.name: Location: Naath

200.content: Basilisk Isles: A group of islands off the northern coast of Sothoryos, named for the basilisks that once infested them. For centuries, the isles have served as a lawless nest for pirates, corsairs, and slavers. Captives are often held in pens on the islands of Talon or the Isle of Tears before being sold in Slaver's Bay. Notable locations include Skull Isle, where corsairs deliver skulls to a dark god, and the ruins of the Valyrian penal colony Gogossos.
200.name: Location: Basilisk Isles

201.content: Sothoryos: A massive, jungle-covered continent south of Essos, largely unexplored and plagued by deadly diseases. Its interior, known as the 'Green Hell,' is home to basilisks, wyverns, and vampire bats. The continent is inhabited by the Brindled Men (Sothoryi), a muscled, thick-skinned race known for savagery and cannibalism. Ancient ruined cities like Yeen, built of oily black stone, are found in the jungles and are said to be haunted.
201.name: Location: Sothoryos

202.content: Ulthos: A mysterious landmass in the far east, south of Asshai and separated from the Shadow Lands by the Saffron Straits. It is covered in dense jungle, and its true extent as either a continent or a large island remains unknown to Westerosi scholars.
202.name: Location: Ulthos

203.content: R'hllor: A dualistic deity of fire, light, and life, primarily worshipped in Essos. The faith is centered on an eternal struggle between R'hllor and the Great Other, the god of ice and death. Red priests lead worship at nightfires and interpret visions in the flames. The religion prophesies the return of Azor Ahai, a messianic figure who will wield the flaming sword Lightbringer to defeat the darkness.
203.name: Religion: R'hllor

204.content: The Great Other: The antithesis of R'hllor in the dualistic faith of the Lord of Light. He is regarded as the god of ice, darkness, and death. His true name is never spoken, and he is believed to be the power behind the Others and the cold shadows of the north.
204.name: Religion: The Great Other

205.content: The Seven: The dominant religion of the Seven Kingdoms, centered on one deity with seven aspects: Father, Mother, Warrior, Smith, Maiden, Crone, and Stranger. Brought to Westeros by the Andals, it utilizes septs as places of worship and is led by the High Septon. The faith preaches against bastardy, incest, and polygamy, and historically maintained a military arm known as the Faith Militant.
205.name: Religion: The Seven

key: He Who Dwells Beneath the Waves
206.content: Drowned God: The primary deity of the ironborn, whose faith justifies their culture of reaving and piracy. He is believed to have made the ironborn in his own likeness to hold dominion over the waters. His eternal enemy is the Storm God. Rituals involve drowning and resuscitation, and the faith's central mantra is 'What is dead may never die'.
keys: He Who Dwells Beneath the Waves
206.name: Religion: Drowned God

207.content: Storm God: The malevolent deity of the ironborn and the eternal enemy of the Drowned God. He is said to dwell in a cloudy hall, utilizing ravens as his creatures and sending storms to lure ironmen to their destruction. Legend states he snuffed out the living fire of Nagga's bones upon the Grey King's death.
207.name: Religion: Storm God

208.content: Old Gods: An ancient, nameless religion practiced by the Children of the Forest and the First Men. It centers on the worship of nature gods through weirwood trees with carved faces, known as heart trees. The faith has no priests or holy texts, and it is most strongly observed in the North and beyond the Wall.
208.name: Religion: Old Gods

209.content: Many-Faced God: The deity of death worshipped by the Faceless Men of Braavos. The cult believes that all religions essentially worship the same god of death, known by various names such as the Black Goat of Qohor or the Stranger. Followers grant the 'gift' of death as a holy sacrament.
209.name: Religion: Many-Faced God

210.content: Great Shepherd: The deity of the Lhazareen, who teaches that all of humanity is one flock. His clergy are known as godswives. The Dothraki derisively refer to the Lhazareen as 'Lamb Men' and frequently plunder their temples.
210.name: Religion: Great Shepherd

211.content: Lion of Night: A prominent god in Yi Ti, often associated with death and the darkness of the Long Night. Legend states he came forth in wroth to punish the wickedness of mankind during the Blood Betrayal. He is represented in the House of Black and White by an ebony statue of a man with a lion's head.
211.name: Religion: Lion of Night

212.content: Merling King: A deity of the sea whose statues are found in the House of Black and White. According to legend, he concluded a pact with House Velaryon and gifted them the Driftwood Throne. The name is also shared by a Braavosi trading galley with a figurehead of a golden-crowned merman.
212.name: Lore/Object: Merling King

213.content: Moon-Pale Maiden: A goddess whose statue resides in the House of Black and White in Braavos. Her shrine is most commonly visited by sailors seeking her favor.
213.name: Religion: Moon-Pale Maiden

214.content: Stone Men: Afflicted individuals suffering from the terminal stages of greyscale who have been exiled to the ruins of Chroyane. They roam the foggy ruins of the Sorrows and are said to be ruled by the Shrouded Lord. The triarchs of Volantis occasionally send mercy galleys with food to the colony.
214.name: Lore: Stone Men

215.content: Greyscale: A dreaded disease that leaves the flesh stiff, dead, and stone-like to the touch. It is believed to have originated from a curse called down by Prince Garin the Great upon the Valyrian conquerors of Chroyane. While often non-fatal in children, it results in a disfiguring calcification of the skin.
215.name: Lore: Greyscale

216.content: Long Night: A generation-long winter and darkness that occurred approximately eight thousand years ago. During this time, the Others first emerged from the far north, invading Westeros and raising the dead to serve as wights. The darkness was eventually ended after the Battle for the Dawn, though legends from across the world credit various heroes with restoring the sun.
216.name: Event: The Long Night

217.content: Battle for the Dawn: A legendary conflict during the Age of Heroes that marked the end of the Long Night. The first members of the Night's Watch, along with the First Men and Children of the Forest, utilized dragonglass to defeat the Others and drive them back to the far north.
217.name: Event: Battle for the Dawn

218.content: Pact: A peaceful agreement signed on the Isle of Faces that ended the war between the First Men and the Children of the Forest. Under the terms, the First Men took dominion over the open lands while the Children kept the deep forests. This event inaugurated the Age of Heroes and led to the First Men adopting the worship of the old gods.
218.name: Event: The Pact

219.content: Hammer of the Waters: A cataclysmic magical event wrought by the greenseers of the Children of the Forest during the Dawn Age. It was an attempt to shatter the land bridge of the Arm of Dorne and later the Neck to halt the advance of the First Men. While the Arm was shattered into the Stepstones, the attempt on the Neck only succeeded in turning it into a swamp.
219.name: Event: Hammer of the Waters

220.content: Doom of Valyria: A massive volcanic and seismic cataclysm in 102 BC that destroyed the Valyrian peninsula and the capital city of Valyria. The eruption of the Fourteen Flames filled the air with ash and smoke, killing dragons and sinking parts of the Freehold into the Smoking Sea. Spells, knowledge, and recorded history were largely lost, and the Valyrian Freehold collapsed.
220.name: Event: Doom of Valyria

221.content: Century of Blood: A chaotic period in Essos following the Doom of Valyria, characterized by a massive power vacuum. During this time, Volantis attempted to reclaim the Valyrian empire through war, while the Dothraki emerged from the east to sack and destroy numerous cities, including the Kingdom of Sarnor. It ended with the Rise of the Free Cities as independent entities.
221.name: Event: Century of Blood

222.content: Defiance of Duskendale: A landmark rebellion in 277 AC led by Lord Denys Darklyn against King Aerys II Targaryen. [Key History]: Sparked by Tywin Lannister's refusal of a new charter for Duskendale, Denys withheld taxes and eventually took the King prisoner for six months. The crisis was resolved when Ser Barristan Selmy performed a daring solo rescue of the King. In his subsequent madness, Aerys executed Denys, his family, and House Hollard, sparing only young Dontos Hollard. The event caused a permanent rift between Aerys and his Hand, Tywin Lannister. [Affiliations]: House Darklyn, House Hollard, House Targaryen.
222.name: Event: Defiance of Duskendale

223.content: Tourney at Harrenhal: A grand tournament held in 281 AC during the Year of the False Spring, hosted by Lord Walter Whent. [Key History]: It was the largest gathering of nobility in recent history, rumored to be secretly funded by Prince Rhaegar Targaryen to gather lords for a Great Council. Notable events included the appearance of the mystery Knight of the Laughing Tree and Jaime Lannister’s induction into the Kingsguard. The tourney ended with Rhaegar winning the joust and crowning Lyanna Stark the Queen of Love and Beauty, an act that catalyzed Robert's Rebellion. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, House Whent, House Stark.
223.name: Event: Tourney at Harrenhal

224.comment: Event: War of the Ninepenny Kings
224.content: War of the Ninepenny Kings: A massive conflict in 260 AC between the Seven Kingdoms and the Band of Nine, an alliance of Essosi merchants, pirates, and mercenaries. [Key History]: The Band sought to place the last Blackfyre Pretender, Maelys the Monstrous, on the Iron Throne. King Jaehaerys II Targaryen dispatched an army to the Stepstones, where the threat was ended when Ser Barristan Selmy slew Maelys in single combat, extinguishing the Blackfyre male line. Many future Great Lords, including Jon Arryn, Hoster Tully, and Tywin Lannister, forged lifelong bonds during this campaign. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, Band of Nine, Golden Company.
224.name: Event: War of the Ninepenny Kings

225.content: Peake Uprising: A brief but significant rebellion in 233 AC by House Peake against the Iron Throne. [Key History]: King Maekar I Targaryen led the assault on Starpike personally. He was killed during the siege, crushed by a rock hurled from the battlements. The uprising was eventually suppressed by loyalist forces, including Aegon V and Ser Duncan the Tall. The conflict resulted in the death of Tion Lannister’s twin, Tywald. [Affiliations]: House Peake, House Targaryen, House Lannister.
225.name: Event: Peake Uprising

226.content: Reyne-Tarbeck revolt: A brutal 261 AC rebellion in the Westerlands where Houses Reyne and Tarbeck defied their overlord, Tytos Lannister. [Key History]: Frustrated by his father's weakness, Ser Tywin Lannister led his own host to obliterate the rebels. He put Tarbeck Hall to the torch and diverted a nearby stream to flood the mines of Castamere, drowning the remaining Reynes. Both houses were extinguished root and branch, immortalized in the song 'The Rains of Castamere' as a warning against Lannister wrath. [Affiliations]: House Lannister, House Reyne, House Tarbeck.
226.name: Event: Reyne-Tarbeck revolt

227.content: First Blackfyre Rebellion: A massive civil war in 196 AC sparked by the legitimation of Aegon IV's Great Bastards. [Key History]: Daemon I Blackfyre, bearing the Targaryen ancestral sword, claimed the Iron Throne from his half-brother Daeron II. The realm split between the Red Dragon and the Black. The rebellion culminated in the Battle of the Redgrass Field, where Daemon and his twin sons were killed by Bloodraven’s archers. Bittersteel fled to Essos with Daemon’s surviving sons and the sword Blackfyre. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, House Blackfyre.
227.name: Event: First Blackfyre Rebellion

228.content: Second Blackfyre Rebellion: A failed 212 AC conspiracy to crown Daemon II Blackfyre under the guise of a wedding tourney at Whitewalls. [Key History]: Daemon II, disguised as the hedge knight 'John the Fiddler,' hoped a dragon egg would hatch to validate his claim. The plot was undermined by the absence of Bittersteel and the intervention of Lord Brynden 'Bloodraven' Rivers, whose spies had infiltrated the wedding. The rebellion was crushed with almost no blood spilled; Whitewalls was razed and salted. [Affiliations]: House Blackfyre, House Butterwell, House Targaryen.
228.name: Event: Second Blackfyre Rebellion

229.content: Third Blackfyre Rebellion: A significant attempt by Haegon I Blackfyre and Aegor 'Bittersteel' Rivers to claim the Iron Throne. [Key History]: Launched from Essos with the support of the Golden Company, the rebels were met in battle by House Targaryen. Bittersteel and Bloodraven dueled once again. The rebellion ended with Haegon's death and Bittersteel's capture and subsequent escape back to the Free Cities. [Affiliations]: House Blackfyre, House Targaryen, Golden Company.
229.name: Event: Third Blackfyre Rebellion

230.content: Fourth Blackfyre Rebellion: A 236 AC invasion led by Daemon III Blackfyre and Aegor Rivers. [Key History]: The rebels landed at Massey's Hook with the Golden Company but found little support from the lords of Westeros. They were intercepted at the Battle of Wendwater Bridge by King Aegon V and his sons. The rebellion ended when Ser Duncan the Tall slew Daemon III in single combat. Bittersteel escaped across the narrow sea once more. [Affiliations]: House Blackfyre, House Targaryen, Golden Company.
230.name: Event: Fourth Blackfyre Rebellion

231.content: Fifth Blackfyre Rebellion: Also known as the War of the Ninepenny Kings (260 AC). [Key History]: Led by Maelys I Blackfyre, who had seized control of the Golden Company by killing his cousin. The conflict took place in the Stepstones. The death of Maelys at the hands of Ser Barristan Selmy ended the male line of House Blackfyre, terminating their attempts to claim the Iron Throne. [Affiliations]: House Blackfyre, Band of Nine, House Targaryen.
231.name: Event: Fifth Blackfyre Rebellion

232.content: Great Council: A formal assembly of the lords and nobles of the Seven Kingdoms convened to resolve questions of succession. [Key History]: The Great Council of 101 AC at Harrenhal chose Viserys I over Laenor Velaryon, establishing the precedent that the Iron Throne could not pass to a woman or through a woman. The Great Council of 233 AC elected Aegon V 'the Unlikely' after the deaths of Maekar I’s elder sons. A 136 AC gathering is also considered a Great Council by some to determine the Regency for Aegon III. [Affiliations]: Iron Throne, Citadel.
232.name: Lore: Great Councils of Westeros

233.content: Hand of the King: The highest-ranking official in the Seven Kingdoms and chief advisor to the monarch. [Description]: The Hand is the executor of the King’s command, authorized to sit the Iron Throne and lead the small council in the sovereign's absence. [Traits]: Symbolized by a brooch or chain of linked gold hands. The office is associated with the proverb, 'What the King dreams, the Hand builds.' Historically, hands have ranged from pious septons like Barth to ruthless lords like Tywin Lannister. [Affiliations]: Iron Throne, Small Council.
233.name: Office: Hand of the King

234.content: Small Council: A body of senior advisors tasked with assisting the monarch in governance. [Description]: The council typically meets in a richly furnished chamber in the Red Keep, often led by the Hand. [Key History]: Formalized during the reign of Jaehaerys I, the council consists of seven standard members: the Hand, the Grand Maester, the Master of Coin, the Master of Laws, the Master of Ships, the Master of Whisperers, and the Lord Commander of the Kingsguard. At times, the monarch may appoint additional advisors or regents to the board.
234.name: Office: The Small Council

235.content: Master of Whisperers: The crown's spymaster and head of intelligence. [Description]: Responsible for gathering secrets and maintaining a network of informants both within Westeros and across the narrow sea. [Key History]: The role became highly prominent under Varys, who utilized his 'little birds' to monitor threats to the realm. The office is situated in the Red Keep, often with access to secret passages and tunnels used for clandestine surveillance. [Affiliations]: Small Council, Iron Throne.
235.name: Office: Master of Whisperers

236.content: Master of Ships: The supreme commander of the royal fleet and naval operations. [Description]: Oversees the building, maintenance, and strategic deployment of the King's warships. [Key History]: The office was held as a hereditary position by House Velaryon of Driftmark for nearly a century due to their Valyrian ties and naval power. During the War of the Five Kings, the role became a point of contention between the Lannister-Tyrell alliance. [Affiliations]: Small Council, Royal Fleet.
236.name: Office: Master of Ships

237.content: Master of Coin: The head of the crown's finances and treasury. [Description]: Responsible for collecting taxes, managing the royal budget, and negotiating loans with institutions like the Iron Bank of Braavos. [Key History]: Traditionally filled by individuals with mercantile or administrative talent. Petyr Baelish notably used the office to expand his personal influence by manipulating crown debt and trade tariffs. [Affiliations]: Small Council, Iron Throne.
237.name: Office: Master of Coin

238.content: Master of Laws: The king's chief advisor on legal matters and justice. [Description]: Oversees the administration of the King's Justice and typically manages the City Watch of King's Landing. [Key History]: This councillor is responsible for interpreting the law and ensuring its enforcement throughout the Seven Kingdoms. It was once held by Prince Aemon Targaryen and later by Renly Baratheon. [Affiliations]: Small Council, Iron Throne.
238.name: Office: Master of Laws

239.content: Grand Maester: The designated representative of the Order of Maesters to the Iron Throne. [Description]: An elected member of the small council who provides scholarly, medical, and scientific counsel. [Traits]: Unlike ordinary maesters, the Grand Maester is chosen by the Conclave in Oldtown and is sworn to serve the realm rather than a specific lord. They typically maintain the Red Keep’s rookery and ravens. [Affiliations]: Small Council, The Citadel.
239.name: Office: Grand Maester

240.content: Warden of the South: A title traditionally held by House Tyrell of Highgarden, acting as a representative of the Iron Throne. The Warden of the South is designated as the supreme general in the southern regions of Westeros, tasked with defending the realm against southern invaders. The office originated during Aegon's Conquest when Harlan Tyrell, the hereditary high steward of the Reach, surrendered Highgarden to Aegon the Conqueror and was rewarded with the lordship of the province. It is currently held by Lord Mace Tyrell, who also serves as Hand of the King to Tommen I. Historical holders include the ancestors of the current line, such as Harlan and Luthor Tyrell.
240.name: Title: Warden of the South

241.content: Warden of the East: A military office and warden title traditionally belonging to House Arryn of the Eyrie. As the supreme general of the eastern forces, the warden is responsible for the defense of the eastern coasts and the Vale against threats from across the narrow sea. The title was first granted to Lord Ronnel Arryn following his submission to Queen Visenya Targaryen during Aegon's Conquest. Although King Robert I Baratheon briefly transferred the honor to Ser Jaime Lannister following the death of Jon Arryn, the title was eventually restored to the current holder, Lord Robert Arryn. The office has been held by a long line of Arryn lords, including Jasper and Jon Arryn.
241.name: Title: Warden of the East

242.content: Warden of the West: A hereditary military title traditionally held by the head of House Lannister of Casterly Rock. The Warden of the West serves as the supreme general in western Westeros, overseeing the defense of the westerlands against invaders, particularly maritime threats such as ironborn reavers. The title was established during Aegon's Conquest after King Loren I Lannister submitted to Aegon I Targaryen and became the first Lord of Casterly Rock. Following the death of Tywin Lannister, the title was granted to his cousin, Ser Daven Lannister, by Queen Regent Cersei. Notable historical holders include Tytos and Tywin Lannister.
242.name: Title: Warden of the West

243.content: Lann the Clever: The legendary founding ancestor of House Lannister who lived during the Age of Heroes. He is famous for tricking the Casterlys out of Casterly Rock using only his wits and supposedly stealing gold from the sun to brighten his hair. While some tales call him an Andal, most connect him to the First Men or claim he was a bastard son of Garth Greenhand. Archmaester Perestan suggested he may have been a retainer who impregnated the Casterly lord's daughters to inherit the seat.
243.name: Character: Lann the Clever

244.content: Garth Greenhand: A mythical High King of the First Men and common ancestor to numerous noble houses in the Reach. He is depicted wearing a crown of vines and flowers and was said to possess the power to make the land bloom. He is the father of Garth the Gardener, founder of House Gardener, and ancestor to the Tyrells and Florents. While some legends name him the first man to lead the invasion across the Arm of Dorne, northern tales claim the First King preceded him.
244.name: Character: Garth Greenhand

245.content: Durran Godsgrief: The mythic first Storm King and founder of House Durrandon during the Age of Heroes. According to legend, he built Storm's End to withstand the wrath of the gods after he married their daughter, Elenei. Septons claim his actions earned his line eternal enmity from the gods of wind and sea. He is the first in a lineage that includes legendary figures such as Durran the Dour, who slew the King of the Giants.
245.name: Character: Durran Godsgrief

246.content: Grey King: The legendary first king of the Iron Islands who ruled for a thousand years during the Age of Heroes. He is said to have wed a mermaid and held dominion over the western isles and the Sunset Sea. Legend holds that he slew the sea dragon Nagga and used her bones to build his hall on Old Wyk. His descendants include the founders of various ironborn noble houses, including House Greyjoy and House Goodbrother.
246.name: Character: Grey King

247.content: Symeon Star-Eyes: A legendary blind knight from the Age of Heroes who replaced his eyes with star sapphires. He is often cited in tales alongside other great heroes like Prince Aemon the Dragonknight or the Falcon Knight. Singers tell of his prowess in battle and his chivalry despite his blindness.
247.name: Character: Symeon Star-Eyes

248.content: Florian the Fool: A legendary knight and fool whose romance with Jonquil is a favorite subject of singers and puppet shows. He famously described himself as both the greatest fool and the greatest knight who ever lived. His fables date back to the Age of Heroes and are remembered by highborn children such as Sansa Stark and Brienne of Tarth. Modern figures such as Ser Dontos Hollard have been mockingly or affectionately compared to him.
248.name: Character: Florian the Fool

249.content: Nymeria: A Rhoynar warrior-princess who led ten thousand ships from the Rhoyne to Dorne to escape Valyrian expansion. She formed an alliance with Mors Martell, marrying him and helping to unite Dorne under House Nymeros Martell. She famously burned her fleet upon arrival to show her people there was no turning back. After the death of Mors, she ruled Dorne as its first Princess, eventually marrying two more times to Lord Uller and Ser Davos Dayne.
249.name: Character: Nymeria

250.content: Harren the Black: The last King of the Isles and the Rivers, known for completing the construction of Harrenhal. His cruel reign saw the impoverishment of both lords and smallfolk to fund the massive castle's construction. He was killed along with his sons during the burning of Harrenhal by Aegon the Conqueror and the dragon Balerion. His death brought an end to the Hoare dynasty's rule over the riverlands.
250.name: Character: Harren the Black

251.content: Argilac Durrandon: The last Storm King and head of House Durrandon at the time of Aegon's Conquest. He was killed in single combat by Orys Baratheon during the battle known as the Last Storm. His daughter, Argella, was subsequently married to Orys, who took the Durrandon sigil and words to found House Baratheon. His death ended the thousands-of-years rule of the Storm Kings.
251.name: Character: Argilac Durrandon

252.content: Torrhen Stark: The last King in the North, who submitted to Aegon the Conqueror rather than face dragonfire. He surrendered the crown of the Kings of Winter and was named the first Warden of the North and Lord of Winterfell. His surrender led to the formation of the Company of the Rose by northmen who chose exile over submission. He is entombed in the crypts of Winterfell.
252.name: Character: Torrhen Stark

253.content: Mern IX Gardener: The last King of the Reach and head of House Gardener. He commanded the center of the combined host of the Two Kings during the War of Conquest. He was killed alongside his sons and entire kin at the Field of Fire when Aegon and his sisters unleashed all three dragons. His death resulted in the elevation of the Tyrells to Lord Paramounts of the Mander.
253.name: Character: Mern IX Gardener

254.content: Alicent Hightower: The second wife of King Viserys I and a primary leader of the Greens during the Dance of the Dragons. She is the mother of King Aegon II, Helaena, Aemond, and Daeron Targaryen. Her rivalry with Princess Rhaenyra Targaryen split the court and precipitated the Targaryen civil war. She was eventually taken captive after the fall of King's Landing and died of the Winter Fever in 133 AC.
254.name: Character: Alicent Hightower

255.content: Otto Hightower: A knight of House Hightower who served as Hand of the King to Jaehaerys I, Viserys I, and Aegon II. He was a bitter rival of Prince Daemon Targaryen and worked tirelessly to see his grandson, Aegon II, installed on the Iron Throne. Known for his learning and arrogance, his machinations were a key cause of the Dance of the Dragons. He was beheaded as a traitor by Queen Rhaenyra after she captured the capital in 130 AC.
255.name: Character: Otto Hightower

256.content: Helaena Targaryen: The sister-wife of King Aegon II and a dragonrider of Dreamfyre. She was the mother of twins Jaehaerys and Jaehaera, as well as Maelor Targaryen. She descended into madness and depression after the murder of her eldest son by the assassins Blood and Cheese. She eventually committed suicide by jumping from a window in Maegor's Holdfast during the riots in King's Landing.
256.name: Character: Helaena Targaryen

257.comment: Character: Daeron Targaryen (son of Viserys I)
257.content: Daeron Targaryen: The youngest son of King Viserys I and Queen Alicent, known as Daeron the Daring. He was a dragonrider who rode Tessarion and served as a squire to Lord Ormund Hightower in Oldtown. He became a critical military commander for the Greens, participating in the Battle of the Honeywine and the sack of Bitterbridge. He died under mysterious circumstances during the Second Battle of Tumbleton in 130 AC.
257.name: Character: Daeron Targaryen (son of Viserys I)

258.content: Baela Targaryen: The eldest daughter of Prince Daemon Targaryen and Lady Laena Velaryon. She was a dragonrider who rode Moondancer and was captured by Aegon II after a fierce duel at Dragonstone. She eventually married her cousin, Lord Alyn Velaryon, and served as a prominent figure during the regency of her half-brother, Aegon III. She was known for her willful and fearless nature.
258.name: Character: Baela Targaryen

259.content: Rhaena Targaryen: The twin sister of Baela Targaryen and daughter of Prince Daemon and Laena Velaryon. She was a dragonrider who eventually rode the hatchling Morning at the end of the civil war. She was married first to Ser Corwyn Corbray and later to Garmund Hightower, with whom she had six daughters. She spent much of her youth in the Vale and at Dragonstone before joining the court in King's Landing.
259.name: Character: Rhaena Targaryen (daughter of Daemon)

260.content: Jacaerys Velaryon: The eldest son of Rhaenyra Targaryen and heir to the Iron Throne during the Dance of the Dragons. He was a dragonrider of Vermax and successfully negotiated alliances with the Arryns, Manderlys, and Starks. He was rumored to be the biological son of Ser Harwin Strong rather than Ser Laenor Velaryon. Jacaerys was killed by Myrish crossbowmen during the Battle of the Gullet in 130 AC.
260.name: Character: Jacaerys Velaryon

261.content: Lucerys Velaryon: The second son of Rhaenyra Targaryen and rider of the dragon Arrax. As a child, he famously put out the eye of his uncle, Aemond Targaryen, during a quarrel on Driftmark. At the start of the civil war, he was sent as an envoy to Storm's End but was pursued and killed by Aemond and Vhagar over Shipbreaker Bay. His death triggered the retaliatory murder of Prince Jaehaerys Targaryen.
261.name: Character: Lucerys Velaryon

262.content: Joffrey Velaryon: The third son of Rhaenyra Targaryen and rider of Tyraxes. He was named after his father's late favorite, Ser Joffrey Lonmouth, and was betrothed to a daughter of Lord Desmond Manderly. During the riots in King's Landing, he fell to his death after attempting to mount his mother's dragon, Syrax, to save his own dragon from the mob at the Dragonpit. His death deeply affected his mother, who fled the capital shortly thereafter.
262.name: Character: Joffrey Velaryon

263.content: Addam Velaryon: A dragonseed of Hull who successfully claimed the dragon Seasmoke during the Dance of the Dragons. He and his brother Alyn were legitimized by Queen Rhaenyra and adopted into House Velaryon as the heirs to Corlys Velaryon. Despite being declared a traitor by the queen, he remained loyal and died at the Second Battle of Tumbleton while leading a host of rivermen to victory. His bones were later entombed at Driftmark.
263.name: Character: Addam Velaryon

264.content: Alyn Velaryon: A legitimized dragonseed who became the Lord of the Tides and a legendary admiral known as Oakenfist. He failed to tame a dragon but rose to fame through his six great voyages and his rescue of Prince Viserys II from Lys. He married Lady Baela Targaryen and was a prominent rival to the Hand Unwin Peake during the regency of Aegon III. He is considered one of the greatest seafarers in Westerosi history.
264.name: Character: Alyn Velaryon

265.content: Nettles: A common-born dragonseed who tamed the wild dragon Sheepstealer by feeding it sheep carcasses daily. She was a small, brown-skinned girl with crooked teeth who became a close companion and rumored paramour of Prince Daemon Targaryen. After Queen Rhaenyra ordered her death, she escaped from Maidenpool on her dragon and vanished from history. She was last sighted in the Mountains of the Moon in 134 AC.
265.name: Character: Nettles

266.content: Hugh Hammer: A blacksmith's bastard who became a dragonrider of Vermithor during the Red Sowing. He fought for the Blacks at the Battle of the Gullet but later betrayed them for the Greens at the First Battle of Tumbleton. In his arrogance, he wore an iron crown and sought to claim the Iron Throne himself. He was killed by Lord Jon Roxton with the blade Orphan-Maker during the Second Battle of Tumbleton.
266.name: Character: Hugh Hammer

267.content: Ulf the White: A man-at-arms and dragonseed who claimed the dragon Silverwing. He betrayed Queen Rhaenyra alongside Hugh Hammer during the First Battle of Tumbleton. Notorious for his drunkenness and lack of ambition beyond wine and lordships, he aspired to hold Highgarden. He was assassinated by Ser Hobert Hightower, who served him poisoned Arbor gold at Tumbleton.
267.name: Character: Ulf the White

268.content: Larys Strong: The Lord of Harrenhal and master of whisperers for Viserys I and Aegon II. Known as 'the Clubfoot,' he was a cunning and enigmatic figure who survived the fall of King's Landing to sabotage Rhaenyra's rule from within. He helped Aegon II escape the capital and was eventually executed by Lord Cregan Stark during the Hour of the Wolf. His death brought an end to the male line of House Strong.
268.name: Character: Larys Strong

269.content: Tyland Lannister: A knight of House Lannister who served as master of ships, master of coin, and eventually Hand of the King. During the Dance, he hid the royal treasury and was subsequently blinded, gelded, and mutilated by Queen Rhaenyra's torturers. He served Aegon III faithfully as the 'Hooded Hand,' wearing a silk veil to hide his disfigured face. He died of the Winter Fever in 133 AC.
269.name: Character: Tyland Lannister

270.content: Jason Lannister: The Lord of Casterly Rock and twin brother to Tyland Lannister. He was a proud and wealthy lord who had unsuccessfully courted Rhaenyra Targaryen in his youth. He declared for Aegon II at the start of the civil war and led the westermen to the Red Fork. He was mortally wounded by Pate of Longleaf during the Battle of the Red Fork in 130 AC.
270.name: Character: Jason Lannister

271.content: Mysaria: A Lysene dancer and longtime paramour of Prince Daemon Targaryen. Known as 'the White Worm' for her pale skin, she served as an unofficial mistress of whisperers for Rhaenyra's faction. She orchestrated the Blood and Cheese plot and maintained a network of spies in the capital. She died during the riots in King's Landing after being forced to walk naked through the streets until she collapsed.
271.name: Character: Mysaria

272.content: Aerion Targaryen: A highborn prince known for his instability and cruelty. [Appearance]: Handsome with classic Valyrian silver hair, purple eyes, and a straight nose. [Personality]: Vainglorious and sadistic; he believed himself to be a dragon in human form. [Key History]: He was exiled to the Free Cities for a time and eventually died after drinking a jar of wildfire in the mistaken belief it would transform him into a dragon. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
272.name: Character: Aerion Brightflame

273.content: Duncan the Tall: A legendary Lord Commander of the Kingsguard who rose from the slums of Flea Bottom. [Appearance]: Standing nearly seven feet tall with a massive, powerful build and brown hair. [Personality]: Humble, courageous, and deeply committed to his knightly vows despite his self-perceived lack of wit. [Key History]: He traveled the realm as a hedge knight with his squire, the future King Aegon V, and later died alongside him during the Tragedy at Summerhall. [Affiliations]: Kingsguard, Aegon V Targaryen, House Osgrey.
273.name: Character: Duncan the Tall

274.content: Rohanne Webber: The formidable Lady of Coldmoat known for her survival and political acumen. [Appearance]: Diminutive in height with vibrant red hair, freckles, and green or grey eyes. [Personality]: Shrewd, dangerous, and fiercely protective of her lands and smallfolk. [Key History]: Called the 'Red Widow' after outliving four husbands, she eventually married Ser Eustace Osgrey and later Lord Gerold Lannister, becoming the mother of Tytos Lannister. [Affiliations]: House Webber, House Osgrey, House Lannister.
274.name: Character: Rohanne Webber

275.content: Eustace Osgrey: The aging head of the once-great House Osgrey of Standfast. [Appearance]: An old, grey-haired man with a gaunt face and a faded surcoat of the chequy lion. [Personality]: Stubborn, prideful, and obsessed with the lost history and titles of his lineage. [Key History]: A secret supporter of Daemon I Blackfyre, he lost his sons and status after the First Blackfyre Rebellion and eventually wed Rohanne Webber to secure his legacy. [Affiliations]: House Osgrey.
275.name: Character: Eustace Osgrey

276.content: Lyonel Baratheon: The boisterous Lord of Storm's End during the reign of Aegon V. [Appearance]: A massive, powerfully built man with black hair and blue eyes. [Personality]: Jolly and fierce; he was famous for laughing as he fought and for his love of the melee. [Key History]: He fought as a champion for Duncan the Tall in his Trial of Seven and later led a brief rebellion, crowning himself a Storm King. [Affiliations]: House Baratheon.
276.name: Character: Lyonel Baratheon

277.content: Quentyn Ball: A legendary warrior and master-at-arms of the Red Keep. [Appearance]: Distinguished by his fiery red hair and a matching hot-blooded temperament. [Personality]: A master of warcraft considered one of the greatest knights of his era. [Key History]: Denied a place in the Kingsguard by Aegon IV, he became a primary commander for the Black Dragon during the First Blackfyre Rebellion and was killed by a common archer on the eve of the Redgrass Field. [Affiliations]: House Ball, House Blackfyre.
277.name: Character: Quentyn Ball (Fireball)

278.content: Castle Driftmark: The ancient ancestral seat of House Velaryon located on the island of Driftmark.. Historically described as a damp and crowded fortress.. It was eventually superseded by the construction of High Tide as the primary residence for the Lords of the Tides.. [Geography]: Island in Blackwater Bay.. [Affiliations]: House Velaryon..
278.name: Location: Castle Driftmark

279.content: High Tide: A magnificent castle of House Velaryon on the island of Driftmark.. Built by Lord Corlys Velaryon from pale stone with slender towers crowned in silver.. It sits on a peninsula that becomes an island during high tide, connected to the main landmass only by a causeway.. The castle housed the Driftwood Throne before its destruction during the Dance of the Dragons in 130 AC.. [Affiliations]: House Velaryon..
279.name: Location: High Tide

280.content: The Eyrie: The primary ancestral seat of House Arryn, situated atop the Giant's Lance.. A small, unassailable summer palace made of pale stone, considered the most impregnable fortress in the Seven Kingdoms.. Its grounds are too thin for a weirwood, featuring instead a statue of Alyssa Arryn and the Waterfall known as Alyssa's Tears.. [Ruler]: Robert Arryn.. [Affiliations]: House Arryn..
280.name: Location: The Eyrie

281.content: Riverrun: The ancestral three-sided castle of House Tully.. It is located at the confluence of the Tumblestone and Red Fork rivers in the central riverlands.. By opening its sluice gates, the fortress can be completely surrounded by water, turning it into an island.. It was founded by Axel Tully during the Andal invasion.. [Ruler]: Edmure Tully.. [Affiliations]: House Tully, House Frey of Riverrun..
281.name: Location: Riverrun

282.content: The Twins: The fortified seat of House Frey, consisting of two identical stone towers.. They are connected by a bridge across the Green Fork of the Trident, providing the only crossing for many leagues.. The castle served as the site of the Red Wedding massacre during the War of the Five Kings.. [Ruler]: Walder Frey.. [Affiliations]: House Frey..
282.name: Location: The Twins

283.content: The Dreadfort: The formidable ancestral seat of House Bolton in the North.. A strong fortress located on the banks of the Last River.. Historically associated with the Bolton practice of flaying, it remains one of the major strongholds of the northern regions.. [Ruler]: Roose Bolton.. [Affiliations]: House Bolton..
283.name: Location: The Dreadfort

284.content: Moat Cailin: An ancient, ruinous First Men stronghold on the northern edge of the Neck.. It commands the causeway, acting as a natural choke point that has protected the North from southern invasion for millennia.. Only three towers remain of the original twenty: the Children's Tower, the Gatehouse Tower, and the Drunkard's Tower.. [Affiliations]: House Stark, House Bolton..
284.name: Location: Moat Cailin

285.content: Greywater Watch: The reclusive seat of House Reed located in the swamps of the Neck.. It is a castle built on a floating man-made crannog that moves through the marshes, making it impossible to find for outsiders.. It possesses no maester, knights, or masters-at-arms.. [Ruler]: Howland Reed.. [Affiliations]: House Reed..
285.name: Location: Greywater Watch

286.content: White Harbor: The North's primary port city and seat of House Manderly.. It is the largest northern settlement and the smallest of Westeros's five major cities.. The city is constructed of whitewashed stone and contains the New Castle and the Wolf's Den.. [Ruler]: Wyman Manderly.. [Affiliations]: House Manderly, House Stark..
286.name: Location: White Harbor

287.content: Casterly Rock: The colossal fortress seat of House Lannister, carved from a stone hill beside the Sunset Sea.. It is the capital of the westerlands and sits atop rich gold mines.. Key features include the natural cavern known as the Lion's Mouth and the Hall of Heroes.. [Ruler]: Cersei Lannister.. [Affiliations]: House Lannister..
287.name: Location: Casterly Rock

288.content: Lannisport: A wealthy walled city in the westerlands near Casterly Rock.. It serves as one of the major ports of the Seven Kingdoms and is the largest settlement in the West.. Known for its skilled goldsmiths and its own City Watch.. [Ruler]: House Lannister of Lannisport.. [Affiliations]: House Lannister..
288.name: Location: Lannisport

289.content: Highgarden: The palatial ancestral seat of House Tyrell and former seat of House Gardener.. Located on the river Mander, it is surrounded by concentric rings of white stone and a briar labyrinth.. It is considered the heart of chivalry and is filled with flowers and fountains.. [Ruler]: Mace Tyrell.. [Affiliations]: House Tyrell, House Gardener..
289.name: Location: Highgarden

290.content: The Arbor: An island seat belonging to House Redwyne, located off the southwestern coast of Dorne.. Famed for its vineyards which produce the finest wines in Westeros.. It is the base for the Redwyne fleet, the largest naval force in the Seven Kingdoms.. [Affiliations]: House Redwyne..
290.name: Location: The Arbor

291.content: Sunspear: The capital of Dorne and ancestral seat of House Martell.. The complex includes the ancient Sandship and the newer Spear Tower and Tower of the Sun.. It is surrounded by a sprawling labyrinth known as the shadow city.. [Ruler]: Doran Martell.. [Affiliations]: House Martell..
291.name: Location: Sunspear

292.content: Water Gardens: A tranquil palace retreat of House Martell, located on the coast three leagues from Sunspear.. Featuring elaborate pools and pink marble, it is a place of solitude for the Princes of Dorne.. It is famous for the sight of highborn and lowborn children playing together in its waters.. [Affiliations]: House Martell..
292.name: Location: Water Gardens

293.content: Starfall: The ancestral seat of House Dayne, located at the mouth of the Torentine river in western Dorne.. Legend states it was built where the first Dayne tracked a falling star.. It includes the Palestone Sword tower from which Lady Ashara Dayne allegedly leaped.. [Ruler]: Edric Dayne.. [Affiliations]: House Dayne..
293.name: Location: Starfall

294.content: Storm's End: The ancient ancestral seat of House Baratheon, originally built by Durran Godsgrief.. A massive drum tower protected by sheer walls and supposedly by ancient magic woven into the stones.. It overlooks Shipbreaker Bay and is considered one of the strongest castles in the realm.. [Ruler]: Stannis Baratheon.. [Affiliations]: House Baratheon, House Durrandon..
294.name: Location: Storm's End

295.content: Castle Pyke: The ancestral island seat of House Greyjoy in the Iron Islands.. It is built upon stone stacks that have been separated from the land by the sea, connected only by rope bridges.. [Ruler]: Euron Greyjoy.. [Affiliations]: House Greyjoy..
295.name: Location: Castle Pyke

296.content: Ten Towers: The seat of House Harlaw on the eastern coast of Harlaw.. Built by Lord Theomore Harlaw, it features ten uniquely shaped towers, including the octagonal Book Tower.. It is the newest castle in the Iron Islands and houses one of the realm's largest private libraries.. [Ruler]: Rodrik Harlaw.. [Affiliations]: House Harlaw..
296.name: Location: Ten Towers

297.content: Harlaw Hall: The ancient ancestral seat of House Harlaw, located on the island of Harlaw.. It was eventually abandoned as a primary seat by Lord Theomore Harlaw due to its damp and unhealthy conditions, leading to the construction of Ten Towers.. [Affiliations]: House Harlaw..
297.name: Location: Harlaw Hall

298.content: Harrenhal: The largest and most cursed castle in Westeros, located on the northern shore of the Gods Eye.. Built by Harren the Black and ruined by dragonfire during Aegon's Conquest, its five towers remain melted and twisted.. It has passed through many houses, all of whom faced tragedy or extinction.. [Ruler]: Petyr Baelish.. [Affiliations]: House Whent, House Baelish..
298.name: Location: Harrenhal

299.content: Griffin's Roost: The ancestral seat of House Connington on Cape Wrath.. A small but strong castle situated on a crag surrounded by red stone cliffs.. It is accessible by a natural ridge known as the Griffin's Throat.. [Ruler]: Jon Connington.. [Affiliations]: House Connington..
299.name: Location: Griffin's Roost

300.content: Summerhall: The ruins of a Targaryen summer palace in the Dornish Marches.. It was a favorite residence of many Targaryen kings before being destroyed by a catastrophic fire in 259 AC.. The fire claimed the lives of King Aegon V and Ser Duncan the Tall.. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen..
300.name: Location: Summerhall

301.content: Tower of Joy: A tower located in the northern foothills of the Red Mountains of Dorne.. It was the site of the final battle of Robert's Rebellion where Eddard Stark and his companions fought the Kingsguard.. Lord Eddard Stark ordered the tower torn down to use its stones for cairns.. [Affiliations]: Prince Rhaegar Targaryen..
301.name: Location: Tower of Joy

302.content: Bear Island: A remote, forested island in the Bay of Ice and the home of House Mormont.. Known for its warrior women who defend the island from ironborn and wildlings while the men are at sea.. It was reportedly won by Rodrik Stark in a wrestling match and given to the Mormonts.. [Ruler]: Maege Mormont.. [Affiliations]: House Mormont, House Stark..
302.name: Location: Bear Island

303.content: Skagos: A large, mountainous island in the mouth of the Bay of Seals.. Its name means 'stone' in the Old Tongue, and it is inhabited by the reclusive 'stoneborn' clans.. The island has a dread reputation for cannibalism and is believed to be the home of unicorns.. [Affiliations]: House Stark..
303.name: Location: Skagos

304.content: Tarth: A beautiful island in the narrow sea off the coast of the stormlands, known as the 'Sapphire Isle' for its blue waters.. It features soaring mountains and waterfalls, with the seat of House Tarth located at Evenfall Hall.. It was the first stormlands territory reached by Andal invaders.. [Ruler]: Selwyn Tarth.. [Affiliations]: House Tarth, House Baratheon..
304.name: Location: Tarth

305.content: Gulltown: The major port city of the Vale of Arryn and seat of House Grafton.. It is the largest northern settlement in the region and a vital hub for trade across the narrow sea.. It remains an important center for contact with the south even in winter.. [Ruler]: Gerold Grafton.. [Affiliations]: House Grafton, House Arryn..
305.name: Location: Gulltown

306.content: Duskendale: A large port town in the crownlands, formerly the seat of the Darklyn kings.. It is dominated by the Dun Fort and served as the site of the Defiance of Duskendale.. It is now the seat of House Rykker.. [Ruler]: Renfred Rykker.. [Affiliations]: House Rykker..
306.name: Location: Duskendale

307.content: Maidenpool: A town and castle in the eastern riverlands, seat of House Mooton.. Named for Jonquil's Pool where Florian the Fool supposedly first saw Jonquil bathing.. It is a busy harbor on the southern shore of the Bay of Crabs.. [Ruler]: William Mooton.. [Affiliations]: House Mooton..
307.name: Location: Maidenpool

308.content: Fairmarket: A market town in the northern riverlands located on the Blue Fork of the Trident.. It served as a former seat for the Hoare kings before the construction of Harrenhal.. [Affiliations]: House Hoare..
308.name: Location: Fairmarket

309.content: Saltpans: A town in the riverlands on the Bay of Crabs, seat of House Cox.. It was the site of a brutal raid by outlaws during the War of the Five Kings, which left the town in ruins.. [Affiliations]: House Cox..
309.name: Location: Saltpans

310.content: Vaes Dothrak: The only city of the Dothraki, located in the shadow of the Mother of Mountains.. It is a vast city of tents and plundered monuments where shedding blood is strictly forbidden.. It serves as the permanent home of the dosh khaleen.. [Affiliations]: The Dothraki..
310.name: Location: Vaes Dothrak

311.content: Meereen: The largest of the three slaver cities of Slaver's Bay, built of multicolored brick.. It is dominated by the 800-foot-tall Great Pyramid and the Temple of the Graces.. Historically ruled by the Great Masters until its conquest by Daenerys Targaryen.. [Ruler]: Daenerys Targaryen.. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, Great Masters..
311.name: Location: Meereen

312.content: Yunkai: Known as the 'Yellow City,' it is a slaver city in central Essos built of yellow brick.. It is ruled by the Wise Masters and is famous for training bed slaves.. Its emblem is a variation of the Ghiscari harpy.. [Affiliations]: Wise Masters..
312.name: Location: Yunkai

313.content: Astapor: Known as the 'Red City,' it is the southernmost slaver city on Slaver's Bay, built of red brick.. Famed throughout the world for the training of the Unsullied eunuch soldiers.. It was sacked and liberated by Daenerys Targaryen.. [Affiliations]: Good Masters, House Targaryen..
313.name: Location: Astapor

314.content: New Ghis: An island city in the Gulf of Grief that serves as the dynamic successor to Old Ghis.. It utilizes iron legions trained in the fashion of the Unsullied but composed of free men.. The city is heavily dependent on the slave trade.. [Affiliations]: Ghiscar..
314.name: Location: New Ghis

315.content: Chroyane: Once the magnificent 'Festival City' of the Rhoynar, now a foggy ruin known as the Sorrows.. It is inhabited by stone men afflicted with greyscale and is said to be haunted by the Shrouded Lord.. It was destroyed by Valyria during the Second Spice War.. [Affiliations]: The Rhoynar..
315.name: Location: Chroyane

316.content: Brave Companions: A notorious sellsword company from Essos composed of criminals and outcasts. [Appearance]: A motley collection of Dothraki, Ibbenese, and men from the Free Cities dressed in outlandish, flamboyant gear. [Personality]: Infamous for extreme brutality and the practice of mutilating captives by cutting off hands and feet. [Key History]: Led by Vargo Hoat of Qohor; they famously switched allegiance from House Lannister to House Bolton, taking Harrenhal as reward. [Affiliations]: Vargo Hoat, Black Goat of Qohor.
316.name: Organization: Brave Companions

317.content: Second Sons: An ancient sellsword company of Essos. [Description]: Comprised of roughly five hundred men; they maintain a leather-bound book recording every member in red ink. [Traits]: Less disciplined than the Golden Company but possessing a long history in the Disputed Lands. [Key History]: Formerly led by the Braavosi Mero and currently by Ben Plumm; they have served both Yunkai and Daenerys Targaryen during the Meereenese campaigns. [Affiliations]: Ben Plumm, Daenerys Targaryen, House Targaryen.
317.name: Organization: Second Sons

318.content: Stormcrows: A mercenary company of five hundred horsemen. [Description]: A company of free men where major decisions are debated by the rank and file. [Sigil]: Four crows between crossed lightning bolts. [Key History]: Originally contracted to defend Yunkai, they defected to Daenerys Targaryen after Daario Naharis executed his fellow captains. [Affiliations]: Daario Naharis, Daenerys Targaryen.
318.name: Organization: Stormcrows

319.content: Windblown: A mercenary company numbering two thousand horse and foot. [Description]: Characterized by their fork-tailed blue-and-white banners and a diverse membership of exiles. [Traits]: They speak classic High Valyrian and maintain a fierce rivalry with the Company of the Cat. [Key History]: Founded and led for thirty years by the Tattered Prince, a Pentoshi noble who fled his election as Prince. [Affiliations]: The Tattered Prince, Yunkai (formerly).
319.name: Organization: Windblown

320.content: Company of the Cat: A sellsword company of three thousand men. [Description]: Led by the savage captain Bloodbeard, they are known for their fierce combat style. [Traits]: They harbor deep-seated enmity for the Windblown. [Key History]: Contracted by Yunkai during the Meereenese campaign, they were noted for their desire to sack and plunder Meereen. [Affiliations]: Bloodbeard, Yunkai.
320.name: Organization: Company of the Cat

321.content: Poor Fellows: The 'Stars' of the Faith Militant, composed of armed commoners. [Appearance]: Ragged, unshaven men in white surcoats blazoned with a seven-pointed star, wielding axes and spears. [Personality]: Driven by extreme religious zeal and a desire to protect the smallfolk. [Key History]: Outlawed by Maegor the Cruel, the order was restored by the High Sparrow after a bargain with Cersei Lannister. [Affiliations]: Faith of the Seven, High Sparrow.
321.name: Organization: Poor Fellows

322.content: Warrior's Sons: The 'Swords' of the Faith Militant, an order of anointed knights. [Appearance]: They wear rainbow-striped cloaks and inlay their greathelms with seven-pointed crystals. [Personality]: Ascetic and fanatical, they surrender all lands and gold to serve the High Septon. [Key History]: Reformed during the reign of Tommen I; their ranks include former lords such as Lancel Lannister. [Affiliations]: Faith of the Seven, High Sparrow.
322.name: Organization: Warrior's Sons

323.content: Alchemists' Guild: An ancient order of alchemists in King's Landing. [Description]: Known primarily as pyromancers, they produce wildfire, which they call 'the substance.' [Traits]: Members use the title 'Wisdom' and guard their secrets with intense paranoia. [Key History]: Once highly powerful, they were largely supplanted by the Citadel; they regained prominence under the fire-obsessed Aerys II. [Affiliations]: Iron Throne, Aerys II Targaryen.
323.name: Organization: Alchemists' Guild

324.content: Undying Ones: The ancient, withered masters of the warlocks of Qarth.
