[Appearance]: In life, they are shriveled husks with blue-black flesh and violet eyes; in visions, they appear as beautiful wizards. [Personality]: They seek to preserve their power by consuming the life force of others. [Key History]: They attempted to drain the life of Daenerys Targaryen but were destroyed when Drogon set the House of the Undying aflame. [Affiliations]: Warlocks of Qarth.
324.name: Organization: Undying Ones

325.content: Warlocks of Qarth: An order of sorcerers residing in the House of the Undying. [Appearance]: Distinguished by their blue-stained lips, a result of consuming shade of the evening. [Traits]: Their influence and magic have waned over centuries, though the return of dragons has begun to restore their powers. [Key History]: Led by Pyat Pree, they unsuccessfully attempted to entrap Daenerys Targaryen. [Affiliations]: Qarth, Undying Ones.
325.name: Organization: Warlocks of Qarth

326.content: Shadowbinder: The most sinister practitioners of magic from Asshai. [Description]: Sorcerers capable of binding shadows to their will to perform assassinations or cast glamors. [Appearance]: They often hide their faces behind lacquered wooden masks. [Key History]: Notorious for their willingness to venture upriver toward the haunted city of Stygai. [Affiliations]: Asshai, Shadow Lands.
326.name: Magic: Shadowbinder

327.content: Moonsingers: The priestesses of the Jogos Nhai and founders of Braavos. [Description]: They serve as healers, judges, and prophets who led escaped Valyrian slaves to the safety of the Great Lagoon. [Traits]: Their temple in Braavos is the largest in the city, constructed of white marble with a silvered dome. [Affiliations]: Jogos Nhai, Braavos.
327.name: Religion: Moonsingers

328.content: Bearded Priests: The theocratic rulers of the Free City of Norvos. [Description]: An order of monks who practice ritual flagellation and possess absolute authority over the city's magisters. [Traits]: They are the only Norvoshi permitted to wear beards; they clothe themselves in hair shirts and untanned hides. [Affiliations]: Norvos.
328.name: Religion: Bearded Priests

329.content: Weirwood: A species of deciduous tree sacred to the Old Gods. [Appearance]: Distinguished by bone-white bark, blood-red leaves, and red sap. [Personality/Traits]: Faces are traditionally carved into their trunks; greenseers can use these trees to look across time and space. [Key History]: Once grew across Westeros, they were largely cut down in the south by the Andals. [Affiliations]: Old Gods, Children of the Forest, House Stark.
329.name: Nature: Weirwood

330.content: Ironwood: A species of extremely hard, black-wooded tree found in northern Westeros. [Description]: Native to the wolfswood and the haunted forest beyond the Wall. [Traits]: Its wood is exceptionally resistant to damage, used for the massive doors of the Winterfell crypts. [Affiliations]: The North.
330.name: Nature: Ironwood

331.content: Dreamwine: A medicinal draft used as a painkiller and sleep aid. [Description]: Often sweetened with honey, it is considered a gentler alternative to milk of the poppy. [Key History]: Used extensively by maesters to treat the ailing Hoster Tully and the young Robert Arryn. [Affiliations]: Maesters, Citadel.
331.name: Medicine: Dreamwine

332.content: Milk of the poppy: A powerful anaesthetic and painkiller made from poppy flowers. [Description]: A white liquid that induces heavy sleep and vivid dreams. [Traits]: While effective for severe trauma, it can be addictive and dull the senses if used excessively. [Key History]: Crucial in treating Gregor Clegane's migraines and Robert Baratheon's fatal wound. [Affiliations]: Maesters, Citadel.
332.name: Medicine: Milk of the Poppy

333.content: Shade of the evening: A thick, blue, viscous liquid consumed by the warlocks of Qarth. [Description]: Produced from the leaves of black-barked trees; it has a foul initial smell but tastes of all things the imbiber has ever known. [Traits]: Induces powerful hallucinogenic visions and turns the consumer's lips blue. [Affiliations]: Warlocks of Qarth, Undying Ones.
333.name: Medicine: Shade of the Evening

334.content: Tears of Lys: A rare and expensive poison manufactured in Lys. [Description]: Clear, tasteless, and odorless, it leaves no trace after being ingested. [Traits]: It kills by attacking the stomach and bowels, mimicking a natural disease. [Key History]: Utilized to assassinate Lord Jon Arryn and the members of Aegon III's court. [Affiliations]: Lys, Alchemists of Lys.
334.name: Poison: Tears of Lys

335.content: The Strangler: A lethal poison that causes the throat to constrict and suffocate the victim. [Appearance]: Manifests as small, deep purple crystals derived from a plant in the Jade Sea. [Key History]: Smuggled into Joffrey Baratheon's wedding in Sansa Stark's hairnet and used to assassinate the king. [Affiliations]: Maesters, Petyr Baelish, Olenna Tyrell.
335.name: Poison: The Strangler

336.content: Manticore: A deadly, insect-like creature native to the islands of the Jade Sea. [Description]: Possesses a human-like face and a barbed tail capable of delivering a fatal sting. [Traits]: Its venom is highly prized by assassins for its speed and agony. [Affiliations]: House Lorch (sigil).
336.name: Creature: Manticore

337.content: Shadowcat: A large predatory feline native to the mountainous regions of Westeros. [Appearance]: Possesses thick black fur with white stripes. [Personality]: Fierce and stealthy hunters that can smell blood from leagues away. [Traits]: Their pelts are highly valued for warmth and prestige. [Affiliations]: Beyond the Wall, Mountains of the Moon.
337.name: Creature: Shadowcat

338.content: Lizard-lion: A massive, swamp-dwelling reptile native to the Neck. [Description]: Crocodilian in appearance, they dwell in bogs and stagnant waters. [Traits]: They are the primary predators of the crannogmen's territory. [Affiliations]: The Neck, House Reed.
338.name: Creature: Lizard-lion

339.content: Kraken: A legendary sea monster of immense size. [Description]: Resembles a giant squid capable of pulling down whaling ships. [Traits]: Though largely considered myth, recent sightings have been reported near the Fingers. [Affiliations]: House Greyjoy (sigil), Drowned God.
339.name: Creature: Kraken

340.content: Basilisk: A hideous and fierce reptile found in Sothoryos and Yi Ti. [Description]: They range in size from small pests to beasts twice the size of lions. [Traits]: Their blood and venom are used in various dark alchemical processes. [Affiliations]: Basilisk Isles.
340.name: Creature: Basilisk

341.content: Wyvern: A winged reptile of Sothoryos, considered kin to dragons. [Description]: Possesses two legs and a barbed tail, but lacks the ability to breathe fire. [Traits]: Highly aggressive aerial hunters known for their variegated colors. [Affiliations]: Sothoryos, House Vyrwel (sigil).
341.name: Creature: Wyvern

342.content: Firewyrm: Wingless, fire-breathing creatures that bore through rock. [Description]: Indigenous to the volcanoes of the Fourteen Flames in Valyria. [Traits]: They grow to immense sizes as they age and are extremely hostile toward men. [Affiliations]: Valyrian Freehold.
342.name: Creature: Firewyrm

343.content: Ice spider: A legendary creature of the Long Night. [Description]: Enormous, monstrous spiders said to be as big as hounds. [Traits]: According to myth, they were utilized as mounts by the Others during their invasion of Westeros. [Affiliations]: Others.
343.name: Creature: Ice Spider

344.content: Azor Ahai: A legendary hero who ended the Long Night. [Key History]: To forge the sword Lightbringer, he sacrificed his wife, Nissa Nissa, by driving the blade through her heart. [Traits]: Prophesied to be reborn to combat a new darkness. [Affiliations]: R'hllor, Asshai.
344.name: Legend: Azor Ahai

345.comment: Legend: The Prince That Was Promised
345.content: The Prince That Was Promised: A prophesied hero expected to be born from the line of Aerys II and Rhaella. [Description]: Associated with a 'song of ice and fire' and a 'bleeding star.' [Key History]: Prince Rhaegar Targaryen believed his son Aegon was the fulfillment of this prophecy. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
345.name: Legend: The Prince That Was Promised

346.content: Greenseer: The rarest and most powerful magical practitioners among the Children of the Forest and First Men. [Description]: They possess the ability to slip into the minds of any beast and see through the eyes of weirwoods. [Traits]: Only one in a thousand skinchangers can become a greenseer. [Affiliations]: Children of the Forest, Bloodraven, Bran Stark.
346.name: Magic: Greenseer

347.content: Warg: A specific type of skinchanger with a spiritual bond to wolves or direwolves. [Description]: They can experience the senses of their wolves and control their actions. [Key History]: All the current Stark children are recognized as wargs. [Affiliations]: House Stark, Free Folk.
347.name: Magic: Warg

348.content: Skinchanger: A person with the supernatural ability to enter the mind of an animal. [Description]: A rare trait most common among the descendants of the First Men. [Traits]: When the human body dies, the skinchanger can live a 'second life' inside their beast. [Affiliations]: Free Folk, House Stark.
348.name: Magic: Skinchanger

349.content: Greensight: The power to witness prophetic visions through dreams. [Description]: These visions are often cryptic and symbolic but inevitably come to pass. [Key History]: Jojen Reed uses his greensight to guide Bran Stark to the north. [Affiliations]: Children of the Forest, Jojen Reed.
349.name: Magic: Greensight

350.content: Dragon dreams: Prophetic dreams specific to those with the blood of old Valyria. [Description]: Often involve dragons and significant future events for House Targaryen. [Key History]: Daenys the Dreamer foresaw the Doom of Valyria through these visions. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
350.name: Magic: Dragon Dreams

351.comment: Character: Rhaena Targaryen (daughter of Aenys I)
351.content: Rhaena Targaryen: The eldest child of King Aenys I and Queen Alyssa Velaryon. She was a dragonrider who bonded with Dreamfyre and was known for a shifting temperament that could be shy, sullen, or fiercely protective. Her life was defined by tragedy; she was widowed when her brother-husband Aegon the Uncrowned was killed by their uncle Maegor I, who then forced her to become one of his 'Black Brides'. After Maegor's death, she lived on Fair Isle and later Dragonstone before retiring to Harrenhal, where she died in 73 AC. She was the mother of twins Aerea and Rhaella Targaryen.
351.name: Character: Rhaena Targaryen (daughter of Aenys I)

352.comment: Character: Baelon Targaryen (son of Jaehaerys I)
352.content: Baelon Targaryen: The fourth child of King Jaehaerys I and Queen Alysanne, known as 'Baelon the Brave'. He was a formidable knight and dragonrider who flew Vhagar and wielded the Valyrian steel sword Dark Sister. He was deeply close to his brother Aemon, whose death he avenged by single-handedly driving Myr exiles from Tarth. Baelon served as Hand of the King and was the Prince of Dragonstone until his sudden death from a burst belly in 101 AC. He was the father of King Viserys I and Prince Daemon Targaryen.
352.name: Character: Baelon Targaryen (son of Jaehaerys I)

353.comment: Character: Aemon Targaryen (son of Jaehaerys I)
353.content: Aemon Targaryen: The third child of King Jaehaerys I and Prince of Dragonstone. He was a dragonrider who rode Caraxes and was described as a tall, handsome warrior with pale lilac eyes and hair like white gold. He served the realm as Master of Laws and Lord Justiciar. Aemon married Lady Jocelyn Baratheon and fathered Princess Rhaenys, the 'Queen Who Never Was'. He was killed on Tarth in 92 AC by a Myrish crossbow bolt while defending the isle.
353.name: Character: Aemon Targaryen (son of Jaehaerys I)

354.content: Alyssa Targaryen: The fifth child of King Jaehaerys I, noted for her tomboyish and spirited nature. She possessed classic Valyrian features but had mismatched eyes—one violet and one green—and a crooked nose from a childhood injury. A bold dragonrider, she claimed Meleys and was the first woman to take an infant for a dragon flight. She married her brother Baelon the Brave and bore him three sons: Viserys I, Daemon, and Aegon. Alyssa died in childbed in 84 AC at the age of twenty-four.
354.name: Character: Alyssa Targaryen

355.content: Saera Targaryen: The rebellious ninth child of King Jaehaerys I and Queen Alysanne. She was a courageous, clever, and demanding girl whose refusal to conform to court expectations led to multiple scandals, including the seduction of three young knights. After being sent to serve the Faith as a novice, she fled to the Free Cities, eventually becoming a wealthy prostitute in Lys and later the proprietor of a famous pleasure house in Volantis. She never returned to Westeros, claiming she had her own kingdom in Essos, though her three bastard sons later pressed claims at the Great Council of 101 AC.
355.name: Character: Saera Targaryen

356.comment: Character: Daella Targaryen (daughter of Jaehaerys I)
356.content: Daella Targaryen: The eighth child of King Jaehaerys I, remembered as a shy, delicate, and easily frightened princess. She was notably innocent and struggled with learning, often crying when forced to read aloud. After a series of failed betrothals, she married Lord Rodrik Arryn of the Vale. She died in childbed at age eighteen while giving birth to her only child, Aemma Arryn, who would later become the first queen of Viserys I.
356.name: Character: Daella Targaryen (daughter of Jaehaerys I)

357.content: Viserra Targaryen: The tenth child of King Jaehaerys I, widely considered the most beautiful of his daughters. She possessed deep purple eyes and silver-gold hair, and she was well aware of her own charms, often playing her suitors against one another. Intending to escape a marriage to the elderly Lord Manderly, she attempted to seduce her brother Baelon, who rejected her. She died in 87 AC at the age of fifteen after falling from her horse during a drunken race through the streets of King's Landing.
357.name: Character: Viserra Targaryen

358.content: Gael Targaryen: The thirteenth and youngest child of King Jaehaerys I, born during winter and thus called 'the Winter Child'. She was a frail, sweet, and simple-minded girl who remained her mother Queen Alysanne's constant companion. In 99 AC, she disappeared from court; it was later revealed she had been seduced by a traveling singer and committed suicide by walking into Blackwater Bay after giving birth to a stillborn bastard son. Her death contributed significantly to the eventual decline of Queen Alysanne.
358.name: Character: Gael Targaryen

359.content: Valarr Targaryen: The eldest son of Baelor Breakspear and heir to the Iron Throne. Known as 'the Young Prince,' he was a dragonrider with silver hair streaked with brown and blue eyes. He served as a knight and potentially as Hand of the King during his father's short tenure. He was considered a model prince but died alongside his grandfather King Daeron II and brother Matarys during the Great Spring Sickness in 209 AC.
359.name: Character: Valarr Targaryen

360.content: Matarys Targaryen: The second son of Baelor Breakspear, mockingly dubbed 'the Even Younger Prince' by a court fool. He was a prince of House Targaryen during the reign of Daeron II. Like his older brother Valarr and his grandfather the King, he succumbed to the Great Spring Sickness in 209 AC.
360.name: Character: Matarys Targaryen

361.comment: Character: Daeron Targaryen (son of Maekar I)
361.content: Daeron Targaryen: The eldest son of King Maekar I, known as 'Daeron the Drunken' for his preference for wine over martial pursuits. He was a dragonless prince who possessed the gift of dragon dreams, which often left him morose and terrified. He served briefly as Prince of Dragonstone but preferred the title Prince of Summerhall. He died of a pox caught from a prostitute, leaving only a feeble-witted daughter, Vaella, as his heir.
361.name: Character: Daeron Targaryen (son of Maekar I)

362.content: Aerion Targaryen: The second son of King Maekar I, infamous for his cruelty and insanity. He was a vain and arrogant prince who believed he was a dragon in human form. His instability was evidenced by his brutal treatment of commoners and his involvement in the Trial of Seven at Ashford Meadow. He died in 232 AC after drinking a cup of wildfire in the delusion that it would trigger his transformation into a dragon.
362.name: Character: Aerion Targaryen

363.content: Rhae Targaryen: A daughter of King Maekar I and Lady Dyanna Dayne. She had children of her own, as recalled by her brother Maester Aemon in his dying visions of the Seven Heavens. In her youth, she once attempted to poison her brother Aegon with a love potion so he would marry her instead of Daella.
363.name: Character: Rhae Targaryen

364.comment: Character: Daella Targaryen (daughter of Maekar I)
364.content: Daella Targaryen: The eldest daughter of King Maekar I. She was one of the sisters to whom Maester Aemon hoped to return after death. She was the sister for whom Aegon V was intended to marry before their siblings' interference with love potions and other schemes.
364.name: Character: Daella Targaryen (daughter of Maekar I)

365.content: Maegor Targaryen: The only son of Prince Aerion Brightflame and Princess Daenora Targaryen. He was born in 232 AC, shortly before his father's death by wildfire. At the Great Council of 233 AC, his claim to the Iron Throne was passed over due to his infancy and fears that he might have inherited his father's madness and cruelty.
365.name: Character: Maegor Targaryen (son of Aerion)

366.comment: Character: Jaehaerys Targaryen (son of Aerys II)
366.content: Jaehaerys Targaryen: The fourth son of King Aerys II Targaryen and Queen Rhaella Targaryen. Born in 274 AC, his birth was briefly celebrated before he died later that same year in infancy. His death was one of many reproductive tragedies that plagued the later years of his parents' marriage.
366.name: Character: Jaehaerys Targaryen (son of Aerys II)

367.content: Shaera Targaryen: The daughter of King Aegon V Targaryen and Queen Betha Blackwood. She served as the queen consort to her brother-husband, King Jaehaerys II Targaryen. She was the mother of King Aerys II and Queen Rhaella. Her marriage was part of a pattern of sibling unions in her generation that defied their father's attempts to arrange political alliances with the Great Houses.
367.name: Character: Shaera Targaryen

368.content: Rhaella Targaryen: The daughter of King Jaehaerys II and Queen Shaera, and the sister-wife of King Aerys II. She was the mother of Prince Rhaegar, Prince Viserys, and Queen Daenerys Targaryen. Her life was marked by a series of miscarriages and stillbirths, as well as the increasing madness and cruelty of her husband. She died on Dragonstone while giving birth to her daughter Daenerys during a great summer storm following the end of Robert's Rebellion.
368.name: Character: Rhaella Targaryen

369.content: Lyanna Stark: The only daughter of Lord Rickard Stark, noted for her 'wild beauty' and willful 'wolf blood.' She was betrothed to Robert Baratheon, but her life took a historic turn when Prince Rhaegar Targaryen crowned her the Queen of Love and Beauty at the tourney at Harrenhal. Her subsequent disappearance with Rhaegar sparked Robert's Rebellion and the downfall of the Targaryen dynasty. She died in a 'bed of blood' at the tower of joy in Dorne, leaving her brother Eddard with a haunting, whispered promise.
369.name: Character: Lyanna Stark

370.content: Rickard Stark: The Lord of Winterfell and Warden of the North prior to Robert's Rebellion. He was the father of Brandon, Eddard, Lyanna, and Benjen Stark. Rickard harbored 'southron ambitions,' arranging high-profile betrothals for his children with the Great Houses of the south. He was brutally executed by the Mad King Aerys II, who burned him alive in his own armor within the throne room of the Red Keep.
370.name: Character: Rickard Stark

371.content: Brandon Stark: The eldest son and heir of Lord Rickard Stark, remembered for his fierce temperament and skill as a swordsman. He was betrothed to Catelyn Tully but was also known for his dalliances, most notably with Barbrey Ryswell. Upon hearing of his sister Lyanna's alleged abduction, he rode to King's Landing to challenge Prince Rhaegar. He died a gruesome death, strangled by a Tyroshi device while reaching for a sword to save his father from the Mad King's flames.
371.name: Character: Brandon Stark (son of Rickard)

372.content: Benjen Stark: The youngest son of Lord Rickard Stark and a dedicated member of the Night's Watch. He served as the First Ranger at Castle Black and was instrumental in bringing his nephew, Jon Snow, to the Wall. Known for his stern sense of duty and survival skills, he went missing during a ranging expedition into the haunted forest. He remains a legendary figure in the Watch, though his ultimate fate beyond the Wall is unknown.
372.name: Character: Benjen Stark

373.content: Elia Martell: A Princess of Dorne and the wife of Prince Rhaegar Targaryen. Described as kind, clever, and gracious, she suffered from delicate health and nearly died giving birth to her two children, Rhaenys and Aegon. During the Sack of King's Landing, she was trapped in the Red Keep and met a tragic end. She was raped and murdered by Ser Gregor Clegane, an atrocity that left a permanent scar on the relationship between House Martell and the Iron Throne.
373.name: Character: Elia Martell

374.content: Lewyn Martell: A Dornish prince who served as a knight of King Aerys II Targaryen's Kingsguard. He was the uncle of the current Prince of Dorne, Doran Martell. Despite having a secret paramour, he was regarded as a formidable warrior and a brother of great honor. He fell in the Battle of the Trident during Robert's Rebellion, slain by Ser Lyn Corbray while fighting to defend the Targaryen cause.
374.name: Character: Lewyn Martell

key: The maid with laughing purple eyes
375.content: Ashara Dayne: A highborn lady of House Dayne, famous for her exceptional beauty, dark hair, and 'laughing' purple eyes. She served as a lady-in-waiting to Princess Elia Martell and was a prominent figure at the tourney at Harrenhal. Rumors persist linking her romantically to Eddard Stark and suggesting she may be the mother of Jon Snow. She reportedly committed suicide by throwing herself from the Palestone Sword tower at Starfall following the death of her brother, Ser Arthur Dayne.
keys: The maid with laughing purple eyes
375.name: Character: Ashara Dayne

376.content: Wylla: A common servant in the household of House Dayne at Starfall. She is named by Lord Eddard Stark and Lord Edric Dayne as the mother of Jon Snow. She served as a wet-nurse to Edric Dayne when his own mother lacked milk. Though her true relationship to Eddard Stark remains a subject of whispered rumors, she is remembered at Starfall as a loyal servant of the family.
376.name: Character: Wylla

377.content: Howland Reed: The reclusive Lord of Greywater Watch and ruler of the crannogmen of the Neck. He is a small man but possessed of great loyalty, having been a close friend and companion to Eddard Stark since the tourney at Harrenhal. He was the only other survivor of the combat at the tower of joy, where he reportedly saved Eddard's life from Ser Arthur Dayne. He has not left the swamps of the Neck since the end of Robert's Rebellion, though he sent his children to Winterfell to aid Bran Stark.
377.name: Character: Howland Reed

378.content: Jon Connington: The exiled Lord of Griffin's Roost and a former Hand of the King to Aerys II. A headstrong and proud man, he was one of Prince Rhaegar Targaryen's most devoted friends. After being stripped of his lands following the Battle of the Bells, he fled to Essos and served with the Golden Company. He spent years in hiding as 'Griff,' raising a youth he claims is Rhaegar's surviving son, Aegon. He is currently leading an invasion of the stormlands while suffering from the terminal disease greyscale.
378.name: Character: Jon Connington

379.content: Haldon: A learned man known as the 'Halfmaester' who serves as the tutor and healer for Young Griff. He is a member of Jon Connington's secret company aboard the Shy Maid. Though he never finished his studies at the Citadel, he is highly intelligent, multilingual, and cynical. He is tasked with providing the boy Aegon with an education befitting a king, covering everything from history to languages and geometry.
379.name: Character: Haldon

380.content: Rolly Duckfield: A brawny warrior known as 'Duck,' who was the first knight named to Young Griff's Kingsguard. Originally the son of a blacksmith at Bitterbridge, he fled to Essos after a violent dispute with Lord Caswell's son. He served with the Golden Company as a blacksmith before being recruited by Jon Connington to train Aegon in skill at arms. He is characterized by his orange hair, shaggy beard, and simple but absolute loyalty to his prince.
380.name: Character: Rolly Duckfield

381.content: Lemore: A handsome woman of the Faith who serves as a septa and tutor to Young Griff. She accompanies the company aboard the Shy Maid, providing Aegon with instruction in the Faith of the Seven. She is noted for her maturity and her habit of bathing naked in the Rhoyne, revealing stretch marks that suggest she has borne a child in the past. Despite her clerical role, her true history and identity remain a subject of mystery to her companions.
381.name: Character: Septa Lemore

382.content: Young Griff: A lithe and well-educated youth who claims to be Prince Aegon Targaryen, the son of Rhaegar and Elia. He was raised in secrecy in Essos by Jon Connington and a small band of loyalists. He dyes his hair blue to hide his Valyrian features and claims it is in honor of his late Tyroshi mother. He is highly intelligent, fluent in multiple languages, and trained to rule as the 'perfect king.' He has recently landed in the stormlands with the Golden Company to reclaim the Iron Throne.
382.name: Character: Young Griff

383.content: Maelys I Blackfyre: The last of the Blackfyre Pretenders and a fearsome warrior of grotesque appearance. He possessed an inhumanly large torso and a second head sprouting from his neck, said to be a twin he devoured in the womb. He seized command of the Golden Company by killing his cousin Daemon in single combat. He led the Band of Nine during the War of the Ninepenny Kings and was ultimately slain by Ser Barristan Selmy, an event that extinguished the male line of House Blackfyre.
383.name: Character: Maelys I Blackfyre

384.content: Daemon II Blackfyre: The third son of Daemon I Blackfyre and the leader of the failed Second Blackfyre Rebellion. He was a dragon dreamer who disguised himself as a hedge knight named 'John the Fiddler' to infiltrate a wedding tourney at Whitewalls. Charming and musically gifted, he possessed the traditional Valyrian features of silver-gold hair and purple eyes. His attempt to seize the throne collapsed due to the lack of support from Bittersteel and the swift intervention of Lord Bloodraven.
384.name: Character: Daemon II Blackfyre

385.content: Haegon I Blackfyre: The son of Daemon I Blackfyre and a prominent Blackfyre Pretender. He championed the cause of the Black Dragon during the Third Blackfyre Rebellion, supported by the military might of Bittersteel and the Golden Company. He was known as a determined claimant who sought to reclaim the legacy of his father. He was ultimately killed in 219 AC after the failure of the rebellion, passing the claim to his son, Daemon III.
385.name: Character: Haegon I Blackfyre

key: The Old Man of the North
386.content: Cregan Stark: Lord of Winterfell and Warden of the North during the reign of Aegon III, often called the 'Old Man of the North'. He led the 'Winter Wolves' to King's Landing at the end of the Dance of the Dragons and served as Hand of the King for a single day, a period known as the Hour of the Wolf. A formidable warrior, he famously dueled Prince Aemon the Dragonknight, who called him the finest swordsman he ever faced. He was a staunch supporter of the blacks and Rhaenyra Targaryen. [Affiliations]: House Stark, Blacks.
keys: The Old Man of the North
386.name: Character: Cregan Stark

387.content: Rodrik Stark: An ancient King in the North whose statue stands in the crypts of Winterfell. According to northern chronicles, he won Bear Island from the ironborn in a wrestling match and subsequently granted the isle to House Mormont. His descendants continued to battle the ironborn over control of Cape Kraken for generations. [Affiliations]: House Stark.
387.name: Character: Rodrik Stark

388.content: Edwyn Stark: A historical King in the North known as the 'Spring King'. He is entombed in the crypts of Winterfell, where his likeness is preserved with a stone statue. [Affiliations]: House Stark.
388.name: Character: Edwyn Stark

389.content: Brandon the Shipwright: A King in the North characterized by his immense love for the sea. He commissioned the construction of a vast northern fleet and ultimately vanished while attempting to sail across the Sunset Sea. [Affiliations]: House Stark.
389.name: Character: Brandon the Shipwright

390.content: Brandon the Burner: The son and successor of Brandon the Shipwright. In his grief following his father's disappearance at sea, he put the northern shipyards to the torch. His actions effectively ended the North's status as a naval power for centuries. [Affiliations]: House Stark.
390.name: Character: Brandon the Burner

391.content: Garth VII Gardener: Known as 'Garth Goldenhand,' he is celebrated as the greatest of the Gardener kings. He ascended the throne at age twelve and ruled for eighty-one years, bringing unprecedented peace and prosperity to the Reach. He was a legendary figure of the First Men who died at the age of ninety-three. [Affiliations]: House Gardener.
391.name: Character: Garth VII Gardener

392.content: Sharra Arryn: Known as the 'Flower of the Mountain,' she was the Queen Regent of the Vale during the War of Conquest. She ruled in the name of her son, the boy-king Ronnel Arryn, and was considered one of the most beautiful women in the Seven Kingdoms. She submitted to Visenya Targaryen after find her son sitting on the Queen's knee asking for a dragon ride. [Affiliations]: House Arryn.
392.name: Character: Sharra Arryn

393.content: Ronnel Arryn: Known as the 'King Who Flew,' he was the final King of Mountain and Vale and the first Warden of the East. As a boy, he yielded his crown to Visenya Targaryen in exchange for a flight atop the dragon Vhagar. He was later murdered by his brother Jonos, who seized the Eyrie and threw Ronnel out of the Moon Door. [Affiliations]: House Arryn.
393.name: Character: Ronnel Arryn

394.content: Meria Martell: The 'Yellow Toad of Dorne,' she was the ruling Princess of Dorne during the arrival of Aegon the Conqueror. Despite being old, blind, and bald, she successfully resisted the Targaryens by refusing to give battle, famously telling Queen Rhaenys that Dorne would not bend. Her scorched-earth tactics and desert warfare kept Dorne independent while the other six kingdoms fell. [Affiliations]: House Martell, Dorne.
394.name: Character: Meria Martell

395.content: Nymor Martell: Prince of Dorne and the son of Meria Martell. He succeeded his mother and brought an end to the First Dornish War by sending his daughter to King's Landing with a mysterious letter for Aegon I. This negotiation resulted in a lasting peace and the recognition of Dornish independence. [Affiliations]: House Martell, Dorne.
395.name: Character: Nymor Martell

396.content: Benedict I Justman: Born Benedict Rivers, he was a bastard of Blackwood and Bracken descent who rose to become a great knight. Known as 'Benedict the Bold' and 'Benedict the Just,' he unified the warring river lords and founded House Justman. He ruled as the first Justman King of the Trident for thirty years. [Affiliations]: House Justman, Riverlands.
396.name: Character: Benedict I Justman

397.content: Arlan III Durrandon: A Storm King who conquered the Riverlands and destroyed House Teague at the Battle of Six Kings. He married a daughter of Roderick Blackwood and extended the Durrandon domain to the Sunset Sea. Though a powerful conqueror, his successors were unable to hold the vast territory he seized. [Affiliations]: House Durrandon, Stormlands.
397.name: Character: Arlan III Durrandon

398.comment: Character: Durran Durrandon (Kings of the Storm)
398.content: Durran Durrandon: A name shared by many Storm Kings of House Durrandon, beginning with the founder Durran Godsgrief. Notable figures include Durran the Dour, who slew the King of the Giants, and Durran the Fair, who annexed the Kingdom of Tarth. The line was defined by its perpetual struggle against the elements and rival kings. [Affiliations]: House Durrandon, Stormlands.
398.name: Character: Durran Durrandon (Kings of the Storm)

399.content: Harren the Black: The last King of the Isles and the Rivers and builder of the monstrous fortress Harrenhal. His forty-year project beggared the Riverlands and the Iron Islands alike, costing thousands of lives. He refused to yield to Aegon the Conqueror and was roasted alive with his sons by Balerion's fire within his own walls. [Affiliations]: House Hoare, Iron Islands.
399.name: Character: Harren the Black

400.content: Halleck Hoare: The son of Harwyn Hardhand and father of Harren the Black, he ruled as King of the Isles and the Rivers. He spent nearly his entire reign at Fairmarket in the Riverlands, largely ignoring his ancestral seats in the Iron Islands. [Affiliations]: House Hoare.
400.name: Character: Halleck Hoare

401.content: Torgon Greyiron: Known as 'Torgon the Latecomer,' he was a High King of the Iron Islands who overthrew a usurper. After his father's death, a kingsmoot unlawfully chose Urrathon IV Goodbrother in Torgon's absence. Upon his return, Torgon successfully revolted with the aid of priests and captains to reclaim his birthright. [Affiliations]: House Greyiron, Iron Islands.
401.name: Character: Torgon Greyiron

402.content: Urron Greyiron: Known as 'Urron Redhand,' he was the first King of the Iron Islands to transform the elective monarchy into a hereditary one. He achieved this five thousand years ago by descending upon a kingsmoot with his axemen and slaughtering every rival lord and priest present. His line, House Greyiron, ruled the isles for a thousand years thereafter. [Affiliations]: House Greyiron, Iron Islands.
402.name: Character: Urron Greyiron

403.content: Joramun: A legendary King-Beyond-the-Wall during the Age of Heroes. He is famed for blowing the Horn of Winter and for allying with Brandon the Breaker to defeat the sorcerous Night's King. [Affiliations]: Free Folk.
403.name: Character: Joramun

404.content: Horn of Winter: Also known as the Horn of Joramun, it is a legendary artifact possessed of ancient magic. According to myth, the sound of the horn is capable of waking giants from the earth. [Affiliations]: Free Folk.
404.name: Object: Horn of Winter

405.content: Raymun Redbeard: A King-Beyond-the-Wall who successfully led a wildling host across the Wall in 226 AC. He bypassed the Night's Watch due to the negligence of Lord Commander Jack Musgood. He was eventually defeated and slain at the Battle of Long Lake by the combined forces of Lord Willam Stark and Lord Harmond Umber. [Affiliations]: Free Folk.
405.name: Character: Raymun Redbeard

406.content: Bael the Bard: A legendary King-Beyond-the-Wall and master singer. Legend states he infiltrated Winterfell under the alias 'Sygerrik,' sang for Lord Brandon Stark, and disappeared with the lord's only daughter. He left her behind with a babe who would grow to be the next Lord Stark, ensuring the survival of the line. [Affiliations]: Free Folk.
406.name: Character: Bael the Bard

407.comment: Lore: The crime of killing family
407.content: Kinslaying: The act of murdering one's own family members, regarded as a uniquely cursed crime in the eyes of gods and men. Notable individuals branded with this title include Aemond Targaryen, for the death of his nephew Lucerys, and Ser Erryk Cargyll, who slew his twin brother. It is one of the few crimes held in the same level of abhorrence as the violation of guest right.
407.name: Lore: The crime of killing family

408.content: Right of the first night: An ancient custom allowing a lord to bed any new bride on her wedding night within his domain. The practice was formally abolished throughout the Seven Kingdoms during the reign of Jaehaerys I at the urging of Queen Alysanne. Despite its legal prohibition, rumors persist that the custom still lingers in remote regions like Skagos and among certain northern clans.
408.name: Lore: Ancient feudal marriage custom

409.content: Trial by combat: A judicial method used in Westeros to determine guilt or innocence through martial contest. Based on the belief that the gods will grant victory to the righteous party, the accused may fight personally or name a champion to fight in their stead. It is a frequent recourse for nobility, such as Tyrion Lannister's duel at the Eyrie resolved by Bronn.
409.name: Lore: Judicial duel

410.content: Trial of seven: A rare and ancient form of trial by combat involving seven champions on each side. Originally brought to Westeros by the Andals, it is intended to honor the seven aspects of the deity and seek a more divine judgment. A famous instance occurred in 42 AC when Maegor I was the sole survivor of a trial against the Warrior's Sons.
410.name: Lore: Religious judicial duel

411.content: Ward: A noble child sent to be raised in the household of another lord. Wards often serve as political hostages to ensure the loyalty of their parents, as seen with Theon Greyjoy at Winterfell. They can also be fosterlings intended to build lifelong alliances between great houses, such as Robert Baratheon and Eddard Stark at the Eyrie.
411.name: Lore: Political hostage/fosterling system

412.comment: Lore: Common people of the world
412.content: Smallfolk: The vast, non-noble population of the known world, consisting primarily of illiterate farmers, artisans, and laborers. Most smallfolk lack surnames and live simple lives governed by local lords and seasonal cycles. They are traditionally the primary victims of the wars and political games played by the high nobility.
412.name: Lore: Common people of the world

413.comment: Lore: Social status of illegitimate children
413.content: Bastardy: The state of being born to parents who are not legally married. Bastards are socially stigmatized, frequently referred to as 'baseborn' if of low birth, and are generally excluded from inheritance rights. By custom, highborn bastards are given regional surnames like Snow or Waters to mark their status while separating them from their parent's house.
413.name: Lore: Social status of illegitimate children

414.comment: Item: Token of the Faceless Men
414.content: Iron coin: A small, worn piece of iron used as a token by the Faceless Men of Braavos. It features a man's faded features on one side and cryptic writing on the other. When presented to a Braavosi with the phrase 'valar morghulis,' it signifies the bearer's affiliation with the secret order of assassins.
414.name: Item: Token of the Faceless Men

415.content: Gold dragon: The standard gold currency of the Seven Kingdoms, bearing the image of a king's face. It is used for high-value transactions, including significant ransoms, bounties, and the purchase of expensive commodities.
415.name: Item: Primary gold currency

416.content: Silver stag: A silver coin used throughout Westeros for mid-tier economic transactions. It has been used to pay smaller bounties, such as the reward offered for the scalp of a member of the Poor Fellows during Maegor's reign.
416.name: Item: Silver currency

417.content: Copper star: A copper coin representing a minor unit of currency in the Seven Kingdoms. It is the most common coinage used by the smallfolk for daily necessities.
417.name: Item: Low-value currency

418.content: Tourney at Ashford Meadow: A grand tournament hosted by House Ashford in 209 AC. It became historically significant for the accidental death of Prince Baelor Breakspear during a Trial of Seven fought to defend the hedge knight Duncan the Tall. The event drew participation from major houses including Lannister, Tyrell, and Hightower.
418.name: Event: Significant tourney of 209 AC

419.content: Tourney at Lannisport: A tournament held in 289 AC to celebrate the end of Greyjoy's Rebellion. It is most notable for the victory of Lord Jorah Mormont, who unhorsed many of the realm's greatest knights to win the favor of Lynesse Hightower.
419.name: Event: Victory celebration of 289 AC

420.content: Tourney of the Hand: A lavish tournament staged in King's Landing to mark the appointment of Eddard Stark as Hand of the King. The event featured a high-profile joust won by Sandor Clegane and an archery contest won by Anguy. It was marked by the death of Ser Hugh of the Vale during a tilt against Gregor Clegane.
420.name: Event: Celebration for Eddard Stark

421.content: Great Council of 101 AC: A historic assembly convened by Jaehaerys I at Harrenhal to resolve the question of his succession. The council chose Viserys I over Laenor Velaryon, firmly establishing the precedent that the crown cannot pass to a woman or through a female line.
421.name: Event: Major succession council

422.comment: Event: Succession council for Aegon V
422.content: Great Council of 233 AC: An assembly gathered after the death of Maekar I to decide between several complicated claims. The council offered the throne to Aemon Targaryen, who refused, leading to the selection of Aegon V. It is infamous for the murder of the pretender Aenys Blackfyre by Lord Bloodraven.
422.name: Event: Succession council for Aegon V

423.content: Widow's Law: A legal decree established by King Jaehaerys I regarding the rights of wives and heirs. It protects the rights of widows to remain in their husband's castles and prohibits a lord from disinheriting children of a first marriage in favor of those from a second.
423.name: Law: Inheritance protection

424.content: Laws of the Seven Kingdoms: A unified code of law created during the reign of Jaehaerys I to replace regional traditions. The project was led by Septon Barth and Albin Massey and took decades to complete, eventually forming the 'Great Code'.
424.name: Law: The unified legal system

425.content: Silence: A formidable red-hulled galley captained by Euron Greyjoy. The ship is manned entirely by mutes whose tongues have been removed by Euron to ensure secrecy and obedience. It is notorious for reaving across the known world from Asshai to Ib.
425.name: Ship: Euron Greyjoy's flagship

426.comment: Ship: Flagship of the Iron Fleet
426.content: Iron Victory: The massive flagship of the Iron Fleet, captained by Victarion Greyjoy. Significantly larger than standard longships, it is equipped with a powerful ram and serves as the command vessel for the fleet's squadrons.
426.name: Ship: Flagship of the Iron Fleet

427.content: Sea Bitch: A lean black longship captained by Theon Greyjoy during the harrying of the Stony Shore. It features a single mast, fifty oars, and an arrowhead-shaped iron ram. The name was given mockingly by Asha Greyjoy when the ship was launched at Lordsport.
427.name: Ship: Theon Greyjoy's longship

428.content: Black Betha: A war galley captained by Davos Seaworth in service to Stannis Baratheon. It was presumably named after Queen Betha Blackwood. The vessel was destroyed by wildfire during the Battle of the Blackwater.
428.name: Ship: Davos Seaworth's galley

429.content: Fury: A triple-decked war galley and the flagship of the royal fleet at Dragonstone. Commanded by Stannis Baratheon, it was the largest ship in his navy before its destruction at the Blackwater.
429.name: Ship: Royal flagship of Stannis

430.content: Moondancer: A slender, pale green dragon ridden by Lady Baela Targaryen. Though smaller than many of her kin, she was noted for her speed and agility. She was killed at Dragonstone during a fierce duel with the wounded Sunfyre.
430.name: Dragon: Ridden by Baela Targaryen

431.content: Cannibal: A massive wild dragon that dwelled on Dragonstone during the Dance of the Dragons. Coal black with green eyes, he was named for his habit of devouring other dragons, hatchlings, and eggs. He was the oldest and largest of the island's three wild dragons.
431.name: Dragon: Large wild dragon

432.content: Grey Ghost: A wild dragon living in the caverns of the Dragonmont on Dragonstone. He was a pale grey creature, notoriously shy and elusive. He was eventually killed and partially devoured by the wounded Sunfyre.
432.name: Dragon: Elusive wild dragon

433.content: Stone Crows: A prominent mountain clan inhabiting the Vale of Arryn. They are known for their sharp axes and fierce combat style. Historically, they are infamous for slaying the father and brothers of Jeyne Arryn in 97 AC. Under the leadership of Gunthor son of Gurn and the warrior Shagga, they pledged service to Tyrion Lannister in exchange for superior weaponry and armor. They played a significant role in the Lannister vanguard during the War of the Five Kings. [Affiliations]: Vale Mountain Clans, Tyrion Lannister.
433.name: Group: Stone Crows

434.content: Burned Men: A feared mountain clan of the Vale of Arryn. They are distinguished by a coming-of-age ritual where youths must burn off a body part, such as a finger or nipple, to earn prestige; the more vital the part, the higher their status. They are believed to be an offshoot of the Painted Dogs and reportedly once worshipped a 'fire witch' with a dragon in the mountains. Under Timett son of Timett, they became a fearless military force in the service of the Iron Throne. [Affiliations]: Vale Mountain Clans, Tyrion Lannister.
434.name: Group: Burned Men

435.content: Black Ears: A mountain clan in the Vale noted for their grisly practice of taking the ears of defeated enemies as trophies. They wear these trophies on necklaces and leave their victims alive as a mark of shame. Led by the formidable Chella daughter of Cheyk, they formed part of Tyrion Lannister's personal guard in King's Landing. They served as scouts in the kingswood during the Battle of the Blackwater but were ultimately driven out of the capital by the city rabble. [Affiliations]: Vale Mountain Clans, Tyrion Lannister.
435.name: Group: Black Ears

436.content: Painted Dogs: An ancient mountain clan of the Vale mentioned in historical chronicles. They were responsible for the death of Roland I Arryn, the fourth King of Mountain and Vale, during a harsh winter. Modern maesters believe the Burned Men originated as an offshoot of this clan. They are known for their primitive ferocity and historic hostility toward House Arryn. [Affiliations]: Vale Mountain Clans.
436.name: Group: Painted Dogs

437.content: Thenn: A region and people dwelling in a hidden valley within the Frostfangs beyond the Wall. Unlike other free folk, they are highly disciplined and more technologically advanced, utilizing bronze weaponry and following hereditary leaders known as Magnars. They consider themselves a more civilized folk with established lords and laws. Under Sigorn, the Magnar of Thenn, they entered into an alliance with the Night's Watch, cemented by a marriage to Alys Karstark. [Affiliations]: Free Folk, House Thenn.
437.name: Group: Thenn

438.content: Hornfoot men: A specific tribe of the free folk residing in the harsh lands beyond the Wall. They were part of the massive host gathered by Mance Rayder during his attempt to lead the free folk south of the Wall. Their name suggests a physiological adaptation or cultural practice related to their life in the extreme northern cold. [Affiliations]: Free Folk.
438.name: Group: Hornfoot men

439.content: ice-river clans: Savage free folk tribes living near the great ice rivers north of the Frozen Shore. They are notorious cannibals who feast upon human flesh. Historically, they were engaged in a state of perpetual warfare with the men of the Frozen Shore until Mance Rayder brokered a peace between the groups. [Affiliations]: Free Folk.
439.name: Group: Ice-river clans

440.content: Cave dwellers: Free folk clans inhabiting the cavern systems of the Frostfangs. They are distinguished by filing their teeth and painting their faces in vibrant shades of blue, green, and purple. Their religion involves the worship of dark, subterranean deities. Many were part of Mance Rayder's host and scattered during the battle beneath the Wall. [Affiliations]: Free Folk.
440.name: Group: Cave dwellers

441.content: northern mountain clans: Ancient First Men tribes living in the mountains north of the wolfswood. Major clans include the Wulls, Norreys, Liddles, and the Flints of the mountains. They are fiercely loyal to House Stark, often referring to Eddard Stark as 'The Ned'. Their leaders are called 'The' followed by their clan name (e.g., The Wull). They have joined Stannis Baratheon in his march on Winterfell to rescue 'The Ned's girl'. [Affiliations]: House Stark, Stannis Baratheon.
441.name: Group: Mountain clans (The North)

442.content: Vale mountain clans: Savage tribes of First Men descent inhabiting the Mountains of the Moon. They are the descendants of those who refused to submit to the Andal invaders and were driven into the high places. They live as raiders, making travel through the mountains hazardous for those who do not travel in force. Principal clans include the Stone Crows, Burned Men, Black Ears, and Moon Brothers. [Affiliations]: First Men, Tyrion Lannister.
442.name: Group: Mountain clans (Vale of Arryn)

443.content: Skagosi: The isolated and widely feared inhabitants of the island of Skagos. They call themselves the stoneborn and are believed to be descended from the First Men. Rumors suggest they practice cannibalism during winter and perform human sacrifices to weirwoods. They are reportedly large, hairy warriors who ride shaggy unicorns into battle. Although nominally sworn to Winterfell, they effectively rule themselves and have historically rebelled against Stark authority. [Affiliations]: First Men, House Stark (nominally).
443.name: Group: Skagosi

444.content: Crannogmen: A diminutive and reclusive people dwelling in the swamps of the Neck. They live in moving villages built upon floating crannogs. Expert hunters and guerrilla warriors, they utilize bronze knives, nets, and poison-tipped spears. They are often disparaged by southerners as 'frogeaters' or 'mudmen'. Historically, they have remained leal to House Stark since the last Marsh King was defeated. [Affiliations]: House Reed, House Stark.
444.name: Group: Crannogmen

445.content: Sistermen: The inhabitants of the Three Sisters archipelago in the Bite. Some carry 'the mark,' a physical trait of webbing between their digits. Historically, they were governed by pirate kings and worshipped the Lady of the Waves and the Lord of the Skies until the Andal invasion. Their culture is marked by a deep-seated resentment of the North following the 'Rape of the Three Sisters'. [Affiliations]: The Three Sisters, Vale of Arryn.
445.name: Group: Sistermen

446.content: Ironborn: A fierce, seafaring race inhabiting the Iron Islands. They follow the 'Old Way,' a culture centered on reaving, plundering, and the taking of thralls and salt wives. They are devout followers of the Drowned God, believing they originated from his watery halls. They disdain agriculture and commerce, preferring to pay the 'iron price' for wealth. [Affiliations]: House Greyjoy, Drowned God.
446.name: Group: Ironborn

447.content: Dothraki: A nomadic warrior people of central Essos who range the Dothraki sea in massive hordes called khalasars. Their culture is entirely equestrian, and they hold their horses in high esteem, even worshipping a horse god. They are experts at light cavalry warfare and slave raiding. Within their holy city, Vaes Dothrak, no blood may be shed and no weapons may be carried. [Affiliations]: The Dothraki.
447.name: Group: Dothraki

448.content: Lhazareen: A peaceful, copper-skinned people of shepherds and farmers inhabiting Lhazar. They worship the Great Shepherd and believe all men are one flock. They are frequently preyed upon by Dothraki khalasars, who derisively call them 'Lamb Men'. Under Daenerys Targaryen, they have formed a tentative alliance with Meereen. [Affiliations]: Great Shepherd, Daenerys Targaryen.
448.name: Group: Lhazareen

449.content: Jogos Nhai: Nomadic tribes inhabiting the plains north of Yi Ti. They are a squat, sallow-skinned people who practice skull modification by binding the heads of their infants. They ride zorses, a crossbreed of horses and striped creatures from Leng. Each band is led by a jhat (war chief) and a moonsinger (priestess/judge). They are known for their centuries-long conflict with the Golden Empire of Yi Ti. [Affiliations]: Moonsingers.
449.name: Group: Jogos Nhai

450.content: N'Ghai: A people and region in the far east of Essos, kin to the nomadic Jogos Nhai. They are the primary inhabitants of Nefer, the last remaining city of their civilization. Their territory lies east of the Bone Mountains and remains largely mysterious to those in the west. [Affiliations]: Nefer.
450.name: Group: N'Ghai

451.content: Sarnori: Also known as the Tall Men, they were the inhabitants of the once-great Kingdom of Sarnor. They were a proud, chariot-driving people whose civilization centered on the river Sarne. Most of their kingdom was razed and their people slaughtered by Dothraki khalasars during the Century of Blood. Today, they are nearly extinct, with the only surviving settlement being the city of Saath. [Affiliations]: Kingdom of Sarnor.
451.name: Group: Sarnori

452.content: Ibbenese: A unique race of mankind inhabiting the island of Ibben. They are a squat, heavy-boned, and exceptionally hairy people. Taciturn and suspicious of foreigners, they excel as whale hunters, wrestlers, and craftsmen. Their ships are among the strongest in the world, built to withstand northern storms and leviathans. [Affiliations]: Port of Ibben.
452.name: Group: Ibbenese

453.content: Brindle Men: Also known as Sothoryi, these are the humanoid inhabitants of the continent of Sothoryos. They are massively muscled half-men with thick, brindled skin, heavy jaws, and snout-like noses. They are considered slow of wit but fierce fighters, often used as slave soldiers by the Ghiscari. Farther south, they are reputed to be savage cannibals who worship dark gods. [Affiliations]: Sothoryos.
453.name: Group: Brindle Men

454.content: Undying Ones: The ancient and withered chief warlocks of Qarth. They dwell within a lightless chamber in the House of the Undying. Consumed by their addiction to shade of the evening, their flesh and eyes have turned shades of blue and violet-blue. They were largely destroyed when the dragon Drogon incinerated their heart during Daenerys Targaryen's visit. [Affiliations]: Warlocks of Qarth.
454.name: Group: Undying Ones

455.content: The Thirteen: A prominent faction of merchant princes in the city of Qarth. They control a fleet of approximately one thousand ships and compete for political dominance against the Pureborn and other merchant guilds. Xaro Xhoan Daxos is one of its most influential members. [Affiliations]: Qarth.
455.name: Group: Thirteen

456.content: Tourmaline Brotherhood: A powerful guild of Qartheen merchant princes that maintains a fleet of roughly eight hundred ships. They are a major rival to the Thirteen and the Ancient Guild of Spicers. Xaro Xhoan Daxos disparagingly refers to them as being full of pirates. [Affiliations]: Qarth.
456.name: Group: Tourmaline Brotherhood

457.content: Ancient Guild of Spicers: The wealthiest of the Qartheen merchant organizations, claiming to own over twelve hundred ships. They are known for their pride and political influence within the city. Following the destruction of the House of the Undying, the guild called for the death of Daenerys Targaryen. [Affiliations]: Qarth.
457.name: Group: Ancient Guild of Spicers

458.content: Pureborn: The hereditary noble rulers of Qarth, also known as the Enthroned. They claim direct descent from the city's ancient kings and queens. They govern from the Hall of a Thousand Thrones and command the city's Civic Guard and war fleet. They are noted for their extreme courtesy, avarice, and habit of offering poisoned wine to those they find dangerous. [Affiliations]: Qarth.
458.name: Group: Pureborn

459.content: The Peach: A large, pink-painted inn and brothel in the town of Stoney Sept. It is managed by a woman named Tansy. During Robert's Rebellion, Robert Baratheon successfully hid within its walls from the forces of Jon Connington. It is rumored that Robert fathered a daughter named Bella at the establishment during that time. [Affiliations]: Stoney Sept, Robert Baratheon.
459.name: Location: Peach (inn)

460.content: Inn at the Crossroads: A historic and strategically located establishment in the riverlands where the kingsroad, the river road, and the high road meet. Built during the reign of Jaehaerys I, it was once known as the 'Two Crowns' in honor of the King and Queen Alysanne. It has been the site of numerous pivotal events, including the arrest of Tyrion Lannister by Catelyn Stark. During the War of the Five Kings, it fell into the hands of the brotherhood without banners. [Affiliations]: Riverlands.
460.name: Location: Inn at the Crossroads

461.content: Chataya's: An upscale and well-regarded brothel located on the Street of Silk in King's Landing. It is owned by a woman from the Summer Isles named Chataya. King Robert Baratheon frequented the establishment, fathering a bastard daughter named Barra there. Tyrion Lannister utilized the brothel's secret entrance through a nearby manse to conduct his affair with Shae. [Affiliations]: King's Landing, Summer Isles.
461.name: Location: Chataya's

462.content: Nymeria Sand: The second eldest Sand Snake, born to Prince Oberyn Martell and a noblewoman of the Old Blood of Volantis. She is a tall and elegant woman with olive skin and a long black braid bound in red-gold wire. Possessing a languid demeanor that masks a calculated and dangerous mind, she is known for her skill with concealed daggers. Following the death of her father, she was appointed to the small council in King's Landing to represent Dornish interests. She is affiliated with House Martell and the royal court of Tommen I.
462.name: Character: Nymeria Sand

463.content: Tyene Sand: A bastard daughter of Prince Oberyn Martell and a septa from the Reach. She appears blonde and blue-eyed with soft hands and a child-like, innocent demeanor that belies her expertise in poisons. She is highly manipulative and dangerous, often seen working on delicate embroidery or displaying a deceptive sweetness. Tyene conspired to crown Princess Myrcella Baratheon to provoke a war with the Iron Throne. She is affiliated with House Martell and the Sand Snakes.
463.name: Character: Tyene Sand

464.content: Sarella Sand: The fourth daughter of Prince Oberyn Martell, sired upon a captain from the Summer Isles. She is a nineteen-year-old woman of mixed heritage, noted for her brown skin and intellectual curiosity. Unlike her sisters who remain in Dorne, Sarella is known for her independence and frequent absence from the court. She is a member of the Sand Snakes and affiliated with House Martell.
464.name: Character: Sarella Sand

465.content: Elia Sand: The eldest daughter of Prince Oberyn Martell and his paramour Ellaria Sand. Nicknamed 'Lady Lance' for her prowess with a tilting spear, she is an energetic and willful youth. She possesses the dark features typical of her Martell lineage and the fiery spirit of her father. She accompanied Princess Arianne on a diplomatic mission to meet the claimant Aegon Targaryen in the stormlands. She is affiliated with House Martell and the Sand Snakes.
465.name: Character: Elia Sand

466.content: Areo Hotah: The Captain of the Guards for Prince Doran Martell, originally a sellsword from the Free City of Norvos. He is a massive, broad-shouldered man with a seamed face and white hair that was once dark. Stoic and absolutely loyal, he lives by the simple code: 'Serve. Protect. Obey.'. He wields a six-foot-long shafted axe with deadly precision, which he used to slay Ser Arys Oakheart. He is the primary protector of House Martell.
466.name: Character: Areo Hotah

467.content: Gerold Dayne: A knight of High Hermitage known as Darkstar, considered the most dangerous man in Dorne. He is exceptionally handsome with an aquiline nose, high cheekbones, dark purple eyes, and silver hair with a black streak. Cruel, arrogant, and deeply jealous of his late cousin Arthur Dayne, he participated in Arianne Martell's plot to crown Myrcella Baratheon. He is currently an outlaw fleeing justice after maiming Princess Myrcella. He is affiliated with House Dayne of High Hermitage.
467.name: Character: Gerold Dayne

468.content: Arys Oakheart: A member of the Kingsguard and the youngest son of Lady Arwyn Oakheart. He is described as a handsome man with light-brown hair and a comely, polite face. Known for being more courteous and cordial than his fellow white cloaks, he was seduced by Arianne Martell and drawn into her treasonous plot. He was slain by Areo Hotah during a failed attempt to protect the conspiracy at the Greenblood. He was affiliated with House Oakheart and the Kingsguard.
468.name: Character: Arys Oakheart

469.content: Myrcella Baratheon: The second child of Queen Cersei Lannister and Ser Jaime Lannister, legally the daughter of King Robert I. She possesses the golden hair and emerald eyes of her Lannister parents. Gentle, courteous, and highly intelligent, she was sent to Sunspear as a ward of House Martell and betrothed to Prince Trystane. Her face was severely scarred and she lost an ear during an assassination attempt by Gerold Dayne. She is affiliated with House Baratheon and House Martell.
469.name: Character: Myrcella Baratheon

470.content: Tommen Baratheon: The current King on the Iron Throne, biologically the son of Cersei and Jaime Lannister. He is a plump boy with white-blond hair, green eyes, and a sweet, tractable nature. Unlike his brother Joffrey, Tommen is kind-hearted and fond of his kittens, though he is easily manipulated by his mother and his wife, Margaery Tyrell. He succeeded to the throne after the Purple Wedding. He is the head of House Baratheon of King's Landing.
470.name: Character: Tommen Baratheon

471.content: Qyburn: A former maester and current Master of Whisperers for Queen Cersei, stripped of his chain for conducting unethical experiments in necromancy. He has a fatherly, grandfatherly appearance with grey hair and warm brown eyes that mask an amoral and clinical mind. He served with the Brave Companions before entering Lannister service at the Red Keep. He is responsible for the creation of the monstrous champion Ser Robert Strong. He is affiliated with House Lannister and the small council.
471.name: Character: Qyburn

472.content: Harys Swyft: The Knight of Cornfield and current Master of Coin under the title of Lord Treasurer. He is an elderly, bald man described as a chinless lickspittle who rose through his daughter’s marriage to Kevan Lannister. Noted for his timidity and lack of tactical acumen, he briefly served as Hand of the King to Cersei Lannister because he would not challenge her. He is often mocked by the court for his yellow rooster sigil. He is affiliated with House Swyft and House Lannister.
472.name: Character: Harys Swyft

473.content: Orton Merryweather: The Lord of Longtable who served as Hand of the King and Justiciar for Tommen I. He possesses messy orange-red hair and a large bulbous nose. Described as sycophantic and bountiful rather than dangerous, he spent much of his life in exile before returning to Westeros with his Myrish wife. He fled King's Landing after the arrest of Queen Cersei by the Faith. He is affiliated with House Merryweather and the Iron Throne.
473.name: Character: Orton Merryweather

474.content: Taena of Myr: A Myrish noblewoman and the wife of Lord Orton Merryweather. She is a sultry, dark-eyed beauty with thick black hair and an olive complexion. She became a close confidante, spy, and lover to Queen Cersei Lannister, assisting in the plot to frame Margaery Tyrell. She eventually fled to Longtable to escape the scrutiny of the High Sparrow. She is affiliated with House Merryweather and the court of Cersei Lannister.
474.name: Character: Taena of Myr

475.content: Gyles Rosby: The Lord of Rosby and former Master of Coin designated as Lord Treasurer. He was an extremely wealthy but sickly old man who coughed constantly into pink silk squares. Though often close to death, he remained a fixture of the court until he eventually succumbed to his lung disease. He died without an immediate heir, leaving his lands in dispute. He was affiliated with House Rosby and the small council.
475.name: Character: Gyles Rosby

476.content: Aurane Waters: A bastard member of House Velaryon who served as Grand Admiral and Master of Ships for Cersei Lannister. He is a lean, handsome youth with silver-gold hair and grey-green eyes, strongly resembling Rhaegar Targaryen. He successfully manipulated the Queen Regent into building a new royal fleet, which he then used to desert the capital and turn pirate. He is rumored to be the pirate king styled 'Lord of the Waters' in the Stepstones. He is affiliated with House Velaryon.
476.name: Character: Aurane Waters

477.content: High Septon (fat one): The supreme leader of the Faith of the Seven during the early War of the Five Kings. He was a squat, ponderously fat man with grey hair, widely considered gluttonous and corrupt. He lived a life of luxury in the Great Sept, bathed in scented waters while the smallfolk starved. He was ripped apart by a starving mob during the riots in King's Landing. He was the head of the Faith and a member of the small council.
477.name: Character: High Septon (fat one)

478.content: High Septon (High Sparrow): The current leader of the Faith of the Seven and a radical ascetic. He is a lean, small man with a lined face, hard brown eyes, and bare, heavily callused feet. He is a fanatical populist who sold the Faith's gold crowns to feed the poor and re-established the Faith Militant. He wields massive political influence, having imprisoned both Cersei Lannister and Margaery Tyrell for their alleged crimes. He is the leader of the sparrows and the head of the Faith.
478.name: Character: High Septon (High Sparrow)

479.content: Septa Unella: A member of the Most Devout and one of the 'white septas' serving the High Septon. She is a stern and pious woman assigned to guard and interrogate Queen Cersei Lannister during her imprisonment. She is dedicated to the strict moral enforcement of the Faith of the Seven. She is affiliated with the High Sparrow and the Most Devout.
479.name: Character: Septa Unella

480.content: Septa Moelle: A prominent member of the Most Devout within the hierarchy of the Faith. She is a formidable and devout woman tasked with overseeing the conduct of noblewomen and ensuring religious compliance. She assisted in the interrogation and surveillance of high-ranking prisoners in the Great Sept of Baelor. She is affiliated with the Faith of the Seven and the High Sparrow.
480.name: Character: Septa Moelle

481.content: Osney Kettleblack: The youngest of the three Kettleblack brothers and a sworn sword to Cersei Lannister. He is a tall man with dark hair and a hooked nose, bearing scars on his cheek from the prostitute Alayaya. He acted as a double agent for both Cersei and Tyrion while secretly being a pawn of Petyr Baelish. He confessed to murdering the previous High Septon and bedding the Queen Regent. He is affiliated with House Kettleblack and House Lannister.
481.name: Character: Osney Kettleblack

482.content: Osmund Kettleblack: The eldest Kettleblack brother and a member of the Kingsguard under Joffrey and Tommen. He is a tall, dark-haired man with a hooked nose who claims to be an experienced sellsword. He is perceived as a hollow and deceitful rogue who was knighted on a battlefield by the now-dead Ser Robert Stone. Though serving the Lannisters, he is secretly loyal to his father's master, Petyr Baelish. He is affiliated with the Kingsguard and House Kettleblack.
482.name: Character: Osmund Kettleblack

483.content: Osfryd Kettleblack: The middle Kettleblack brother and former Commander of the City Watch of King's Landing. He is the tallest and sternest of the three, with a drooping black mustache and a cruel smile. He is noted for his brutality and was promoted rapidly by Cersei Lannister after the Battle of the Blackwater. He was later stripped of his command by Kevan Lannister. He is affiliated with House Kettleblack and the gold cloaks.
483.name: Character: Osfryd Kettleblack

484.content: Moon Boy: The royal jester and court fool at the Red Keep. He is a pie-faced man with big round eyes, dressed in colorful motley and carrying a rattle. Although he appears to be a simpleton, he is highly acrobatic and makes deft, cruel jokes about the nobility. He is suspected by Dontos Hollard of being a spy in the employ of Varys. He is affiliated with the court of King Robert I and his successors.
484.name: Character: Moon Boy

485.content: Patchface: The court fool to Stannis Baratheon and constant companion to Princess Shireen. He is an obese, tattooed man whose face is a motley of red and green squares. Broken in mind after surviving the wreck of the Windproud, he speaks exclusively in cryptic, prophetic rhymes about 'under the sea'. Melisandre views him as a dangerous creature, glimpsing him in her flames surrounded by skulls. He is affiliated with House Baratheon of Dragonstone.
485.name: Character: Patchface

486.content: Dontos Hollard: The last surviving member of House Hollard, a portly and frequently drunken knight turned court fool. He has blotchy skin and a nose webbed with broken veins. After being spared execution for his drunkenness by Sansa Stark, he acted as her secret contact and orchestrated her escape from the Red Keep. He was murdered by Petyr Baelish immediately after delivering Sansa to him. He was affiliated with House Hollard and Petyr Baelish.
486.name: Character: Dontos Hollard

487.content: Illyrio Mopatis: A powerful and morbidly obese Magister of the Free City of Pentos. He has a yellow forked beard, piggish eyes, and fingers adorned with numerous gemstone rings. Once a lithe sellsword and bravo, he accumulated vast wealth and now serves as a key benefactor for the Targaryen restoration. He is a lifelong collaborator with Varys, with whom he plots to place Aegon Targaryen on the Iron Throne. He is affiliated with House Targaryen and the Free City of Pentos.
487.name: Character: Illyrio Mopatis

488.content: Hizdahr zo Loraq: A fabulously wealthy Ghiscari merchant who became the King of Meereen. He is a tall, slender man with amber skin and hair styled into wings until he shaved it in emulation of a humble style. He married Daenerys Targaryen as part of a peace pact with the Yunkai'i, though he is widely suspected of ties to the Sons of the Harpy. He was arrested and deposed by Barristan Selmy following Daenerys's disappearance. He is the head of the House of Loraq.
488.name: Character: Hizdahr zo Loraq

489.content: Reznak mo Reznak: The Ghiscari seneschal of the city of Meereen. He is a small, fleshy, and bald man who uses excessive amounts of perfume to mask his odor. Known for his slimy smile and excessively flattering manner of speech, he is distrusted by both Daenerys Targaryen and her Westerosi advisors. He serves as a primary administrator of the city during the Targaryen occupation. He is affiliated with House Targaryen and the city of Meereen.
489.name: Character: Reznak mo Reznak

490.content: Skahaz mo Kandaq: A Meereenese noble known as the Shavepate who commands the Brazen Beasts. He is an ugly man with oily yellow skin, a beetled brow, and a big nose dark with blackheads. He is a ruthless opportunist who abandoned Ghiscari tradition to support Daenerys Targaryen, making him a primary target of the Sons of the Harpy. He orchestrated the coup against Hizdahr zo Loraq alongside Barristan Selmy. He is the head of the House of Kandaq.
490.name: Character: Skahaz mo Kandaq

491.content: Tattered Prince: The founder and commander of the Windblown mercenary company. He is an elderly, elegant man who sits straight and tall atop a huge grey warhorse. He wears a distinctive cloak made of multi-colored torn rags. Born a noble of Pentos, he fled to the Disputed Lands at age twenty-three after the magisters chose him to be the new Prince of Pentos. [Affiliations]: Windblown, Pentos (formerly).
491.name: Character: Tattered Prince

492.content: Pretty Meris: A member of the Windblown sellsword company who serves as its torturer. She is an exile from Westeros who was imprisoned in Meereen. She serves under the Tattered Prince and acted as a representative for the company's potential defection to Daenerys Targaryen. [Affiliations]: Windblown.
492.name: Character: Pretty Meris

493.content: Inkpots: The paymaster for the Second Sons sellsword company, originally named Tybero Istarion. He is a professional administrator who maintains the company's leather-bound book of members. He oversees the signing of contracts and manages the company's financial promises. [Affiliations]: Second Sons.
493.name: Character: Inkpots

494.content: Penny: A dwarf woman from the Free Cities who was a mummer alongside her brother Oppo. She is young with warm brown, thick curly hair and large, trusting eyes. She often performs jousting acts atop her dog, Crunch, and her pig, Pretty Pig. After being enslaved and nearly killed in the pits of Meereen, she joins the Second Sons. [Affiliations]: Second Sons.
494.name: Character: Penny

495.content: Marwyn: An Archmaester of the Citadel known as 'Marwyn the Mage'. He possesses a ring, rod, and mask made of Valyrian steel and has studied the higher mysteries and shadowbinding in his travels. He is a blunt man who keeps company with outcasts and believes the Citadel helped extinguish the world's dragons. Upon hearing of Daenerys Targaryen, he departs Oldtown to find her in Slaver's Bay. [Affiliations]: Citadel.
495.name: Character: Marwyn the Mage

496.content: Alleras: An acolyte at the Citadel known as 'the Sphinx'. He is a mixed-race youth with a Dornish father and a mother from the Summer Isles. He is exceptionally skilled with a bow and is a trusted follower of Archmaester Marwyn. [Affiliations]: Citadel, Marwyn.
496.name: Character: Alleras

497.content: Leo Tyrell: A novice at the Citadel and a member of House Tyrell, mockingly called 'Lazy Leo'. He is an arrogant youth who disparages his fellow students and follows the teachings of Archmaester Marwyn. He is the son of Ser Moryn Tyrell. [Affiliations]: House Tyrell, Citadel.
497.name: Character: Leo Tyrell (Lazy Leo)

498.content: Pate: A novice at the Citadel originally from the westerlands who served as an assistant to Archmaester Walgrave. He was a simple, struggling student who was unable to earn any links for his maester's chain. Driven by his love for a serving wench named Rosey, he stole a master key from Walgrave to sell to a mysterious 'Alchemist'. He was killed by the Alchemist immediately after the trade. [Affiliations]: Citadel.
498.name: Character: Pate (novice)

499.content: Roone: A young novice at the Citadel who was born in the Reach. He is part of a small circle of students that gathers at the Quill and Tankard to discuss rumors of dragons. [Affiliations]: Citadel.
499.name: Character: Roone

500.content: Mollander: A novice at the Citadel who has a clubfoot and is nicknamed 'Hopfrog'. He is the son of a knight who died at the Battle of the Blackwater. He is known for his skill at throwing apples despite his deformity. [Affiliations]: Citadel.
500.name: Character: Mollander

501.content: Armen: An acolyte at the Citadel known as 'Armen the Acolyte'. He has a long, thin, pointy nose and has earned four links to his maester's chain. He is a studious and cautious individual within his group of peers. [Affiliations]: Citadel.
501.name: Character: Armen

502.content: Sphinx: A mythical creature often depicted with a human face, a lion's body, and hawk's wings. In legend, they are known for speaking in riddles. The name is used as an alias by the acolyte Alleras at the Citadel. Statues of green sphinxes flank the gates of the Citadel in Oldtown.
502.name: Lore/Alias: Sphinx

503.content: Moqorro: A powerful red priest from the Temple of the Lord of Light in Volantis. He is a massive man with skin as black as pitch and a tangle of pure white hair like a lion's mane. He has orange-and-yellow flame tattoos inked across his cheeks and forehead. He possesses the ability to see visions in fire and is the right hand of the High Priest Benerro. [Affiliations]: R'hllor, Volantis.
503.name: Character: Moqorro

504.content: Benerro: The High Priest of the Temple of the Lord of Light in Volantis. He is a powerful and fanatical figure who preaches to thousands of slaves about the return of Azor Ahai. He supports Daenerys Targaryen, believing her coming is the fulfillment of an ancient prophecy. [Affiliations]: R'hllor, Volantis.
504.name: Character: Benerro

505.content: Lady Stoneheart: The resurrected, vengeful form of Catelyn Stark. Her flesh is soft as pudding and the color of curdled milk, with a face marked by shredded skin and a throat gash hidden by a collar. She is consumed by a desire for vengeance against those she believes betrayed her family at the Red Wedding. She assumed leadership of the brotherhood without banners after being revived by Beric Dondarrion. [Affiliations]: Brotherhood without banners.
505.name: Character: Lady Stoneheart

506.content: Lem: A fierce member of the brotherhood without banners known for his heavy yellow cloak. He has a harsh voice and served as a loyal soldier under Beric Dondarrion and later Lady Stoneheart. He is aggressive and participated in the capture of Brienne of Tarth. [Affiliations]: Brotherhood without banners.
506.name: Character: Lem Lemoncloak

507.content: Tom of Sevenstreams: A singer and member of the brotherhood without banners. He is a small man with a big mouth and a sharp tongue who plays the woodharp. He is known for his many illegitimate children and his vast knowledge of bawdy songs. He eventually infiltrates Riverrun as a musician. [Affiliations]: Brotherhood without banners.
507.name: Character: Tom of Sevenstreams

508.content: Anguy: A skilled archer from the Dornish Marches who joined the brotherhood without banners. He gained fame by winning the archery contest at the Hand's tourney in King's Landing. He is known for his freckles, red hair, and cheerful disposition. [Affiliations]: Brotherhood without banners.
508.name: Character: Anguy

509.content: Thoros of Myr: A red priest of R'hllor from the Free City of Myr.
