Once a thin man in red robes, he became a portly drinking companion to King Robert I before joining the brotherhood without banners. He possesses the power to resurrect the dead through the 'last kiss,' which he used on Beric Dondarrion. [Affiliations]: R'hllor, Brotherhood without banners.
509.name: Character: Thoros of Myr

510.content: Edric Dayne: The young Lord of Starfall and head of House Dayne. He is a boy of twelve with pale blond hair and dark blue eyes. He served as a squire to Lord Beric Dondarrion and claims to be the 'milk brother' of Jon Snow. [Affiliations]: House Dayne, Brotherhood without banners.
510.name: Character: Edric Dayne

511.content: Mad Huntsman: A member of the brotherhood without banners and a former farmer from Stoney Sept. He is a stocky, balding man who leads a pack of fierce hunting dogs. He is driven by rage after the Lannisters pillaged his lands and raped his family. [Affiliations]: Brotherhood without banners.
511.name: Character: Mad Huntsman

512.content: Jeyne Westerling: The eldest daughter of Lord Gawen Westerling and the widow of King Robb Stark. She is a pretty girl with curly chestnut hair, brown eyes, and a heart-shaped face. She nursed Robb back to health after he was wounded at the Crag, eventually marrying him. She was largely a pawn in her mother Sybell Spicer's political machinations. [Affiliations]: House Westerling, House Stark.
512.name: Character: Jeyne Westerling

513.content: Roslin Frey: A daughter of Lord Walder Frey and the wife of Lord Edmure Tully. She is described as a small, pretty girl with brown hair and blue eyes. She was married to Edmure as part of the trap that culminated in the Red Wedding. [Affiliations]: House Frey, House Tully.
513.name: Character: Roslin Frey

514.content: Lothar Frey: The twelfth son of Lord Walder Frey and the steward of the Twins. He is a portly man with a twisted leg, shoulder-length dark ringlets, and a pointed beard. He is considered highly intelligent, cunning, and more dangerous than his brothers. He played a primary role in planning the Red Wedding. [Affiliations]: House Frey.
514.name: Character: Lothar Frey

515.content: Black Walder Frey: The second son of Ser Ryman Frey, known for his hot temper and fearsome reputation. He is a lean man with a beard and is active as a military leader for his house. He personally participated in the killings at the Red Wedding. [Affiliations]: House Frey.
515.name: Character: Black Walder Frey

516.content: Olyvar Frey: A younger son of Lord Walder Frey who served as a squire to Robb Stark. He was loyal to the Young Wolf and was noticeably absent during the Red Wedding due to his Stark sympathies. [Affiliations]: House Frey, House Stark.
516.name: Character: Olyvar Frey

517.content: Perwyn Frey: A son of Lord Walder Frey and a knight known for his decency. He served as a guard for Catelyn Stark during her mission to meet Renly Baratheon. Like his brother Olyvar, he was sent away from the Twins before the Red Wedding because of his Stark friendships. [Affiliations]: House Frey.
517.name: Character: Perwyn Frey

518.content: Wyman Manderly: The Lord of White Harbor and head of House Manderly. He is an immensely corpulent man, so large he cannot sit a horse and must be carried in a litter. Though he appears amiable and gluttonous, he is a shrewd and loyal Stark bannerman who secretly plots against the Boltons and Freys. He famously served pies made of his enemies at Winterfell. [Affiliations]: House Manderly, House Stark.
518.name: Character: Wyman Manderly

519.content: Wylla Manderly: The second daughter of Ser Wylis Manderly and a brave young girl. She has blonde hair that she dyes green in honor of the merman of her house. She famously defied the Freys in the Merman's Court, reminding her grandfather and the city of their ancient debt to House Stark. [Affiliations]: House Manderly, House Stark.
519.name: Character: Wylla Manderly

520.content: Wynafryd Manderly: The eldest daughter and heir of Ser Wylis Manderly. She is a young woman with brown hair who resides at the New Castle in White Harbor. She is betrothed to Rhaegar Frey as part of her grandfather's public facade of alliance with the Iron Throne. [Affiliations]: House Manderly.
520.name: Character: Wynafryd Manderly

521.content: Barbrey Dustin: The Lady of Barrowton and a daughter of Lord Rodrik Ryswell. She is a tall, handsome woman with brown hair streaked with grey tied in a widow's knot. She harbors a deep resentment for House Stark, particularly Eddard Stark, for the death of her husband Willam and her former lover Brandon Stark. She is a staunch but wary ally of House Bolton. [Affiliations]: House Dustin, House Ryswell.
521.name: Character: Barbrey Dustin

522.content: Hother Umber: A joint castellan of the Last Hearth known as 'Whoresbane'. He is an old, gaunt man with a hard face and a long white beard. He earned his nickname by disemboweling a whore in Oldtown while he was a novice at the Citadel. He supports House Bolton in the north only because his nephew, the Greatjon, is a captive of the Freys. [Affiliations]: House Umber.
522.name: Character: Hother Umber

523.content: Mors Umber: A joint castellan of the Last Hearth known as 'Crowfood'. He is a massive, powerful old man who wears a chunk of dragonglass in place of a lost eye. He joined the cause of Stannis Baratheon on the condition that he receives the head of Mance Rayder. He led the green boys in the ambush outside the walls of Winterfell. [Affiliations]: House Umber, Stannis Baratheon.
523.name: Character: Mors Umber

524.content: Arnolf Karstark: The castellan of Karhold and an uncle to the late Lord Rickard Karstark. He is an old, stooped man who feigned loyalty to Stannis Baratheon while secretly plotting with the Boltons to seize Karhold for his own branch. His treachery was discovered by Jon Snow and revealed to Stannis. [Affiliations]: House Karstark, House Bolton.
524.name: Character: Arnolf Karstark

525.content: Alys Karstark: The daughter of Lord Rickard Karstark and the heiress to Karhold. She is a tall girl with a long face, grey eyes, and brown hair. Fleeing a forced marriage to her cousin Cregan, she sought the protection of Jon Snow at the Wall. She was married to Sigorn, the Magnar of Thenn, to secure her claim to Karhold. [Affiliations]: House Karstark, House Thenn.
525.name: Character: Alys Karstark

526.content: House Corbray of Heart's Home: An old but poor noble house from the Vale of Arryn. Their seat is Heart's Home, and they historically claimed the titles of Lord of the Five Fingers and King of the Fingers. Their sigil features three black ravens in flight holding three red hearts on a white field. The house possesses the ancestral Valyrian steel longsword known as Lady Forlorn. Founded during the Andal invasion, they rose to prominence by defeating First Men monarchs.
526.name: House: Corbray of Heart's Home

527.content: House Waynwood of Ironoaks: A great noble family of the Vale of Arryn known for their insistence on ceremony and pride. Their seat is Ironoaks, and they blazon their arms with a black broken wheel on a green field. Members of the house typically have brown hair and long faces. They are an old house of high honor, currently fostering the heir presumptive to the Vale, Harrold Hardyng.
527.name: House: Waynwood of Ironoaks

528.content: House Grafton of Gulltown: The noble rulers of Gulltown, the only city in the Vale of Arryn. Their sigil is a burning yellow tower within a black pile on a flaming red field. The house was founded by an Andal knight who usurped the city from the First Men House Shett. They control a major port and are noted for staying loyal to the Iron Throne during Robert's Rebellion.
528.name: House: Grafton of Gulltown

529.content: House Hunter of Longbow Hall: A principal noble house of the Vale of Arryn with ancient First Men roots. Their seat is Longbow Hall, located in the eastern Vale. Their sigil depicts five silver arrows fanned on a brown field. Legend states the house joined the realm of the Arryns after an archery contest during the Andal invasion. They are traditionally known for their skill in hunting and archery.
529.name: House: Hunter of Longbow Hall

530.content: House Belmore of Strongsong: A powerful house of First Men origin situated at Strongsong in the Vale of Arryn. Their sigil consists of six silver bells arranged 3-2-1 on a purple field. Members of the family are often characterized by red hair. They submitted to House Arryn during the Andal invasion after the defeat of the First Men at the Battle of the Seven Stars.
530.name: House: Belmore of Strongsong

531.content: House Templeton of Ninestars: A powerful landed knightly house in the Vale of Arryn whose influence is comparable to that of great lords. Their seat is Ninestars, and the head of the house is titled the Knight of Ninestars. Their sigil features nine stars on a gold saltire over a black field. They can easily raise a thousand men and are believed to have blood ties to House Stark.
531.name: House: Templeton of Ninestars

532.content: House Cerwyn of Cerwyn: One of the closest and most powerful bannermen to House Stark, located only a half day's ride from Winterfell. Their seat is Castle Cerwyn, and their words are 'Honed and Ready'. Their sigil is a black battle-axe on a silver field. Historically, the lords of this house were considered the closest friends of the Starks of Winterfell.
532.name: House: Cerwyn of Cerwyn

533.content: House Glover of Deepwood Motte: A prominent northern house that holds the rank of Master rather than Lord. Their seat is Deepwood Motte in the northwestern wolfswood. Their sigil is a silver mailed fist on a scarlet field. They rule over several petty houses in the wolfswood and were historically First Men kings before being reduced to vassals by the Starks.
533.name: House: Glover of Deepwood Motte

534.content: House Tallhart of Torrhen's Square: A noble northern house of First Men descent that uses the title Master. Their seat is Torrhen's Square, and their words are 'Proud and Free'. Their sigil depicts three green sentinel trees on a brown field. They are among the principal bannermen of Winterfell and are located southwest of the Stark seat.
534.name: House: Tallhart of Torrhen's Square

535.content: House Hornwood of Hornwood: A principal northern house whose lands border those of House Bolton and House Manderly. Their seat is Hornwood, and their words are 'Righteous in Wrath'. Their sigil is a brown bullmoose with black antlers on an orange field. Their domains include the forest of the Hornwood and reach as far as the White Knife. Their line faced a succession crisis after the deaths of Lord Halys and his heir Daryn.
535.name: House: Hornwood of Hornwood

536.content: House Ryswell of the Rills: A prominent northern family ruling the extensive region known as the Rills. Their sigil is a black horse's head with red eyes and mane on a bronze field with a black border. Individual family members often personalize the horsehead color on their own banners, using grey, brown, or gold. They are an ancient house of First Men origin that once rebelled against the Kings of Winter.
536.name: House: Ryswell of the Rills

537.content: House Dustin of Barrowton: A major noble house of the north seated at Barrow Hall in the town of Barrowton. Their sigil features two crossed rusted longaxes with a black crown between the points on a yellow field. They claim descent from the First King and the kings of the barrowlands. The house is currently ruled by Lady Barbrey Dustin, who harbors a deep grievance against House Stark.
537.name: House: Dustin of Barrowton

538.content: House Flint: A name shared by several distinct noble houses in the north. Major branches include House Flint of the northern mountains, House Flint of Breakstone Hill, House Flint of Flint's Finger, and House Flint of Widow's Watch. They are of First Men descent and are noted for their varying levels of power and divergent geographic locations.
538.name: House: Multiple Northern Flint branches

539.content: House Crakehall of Crakehall: A primary noble house of the westerlands with First Men roots. Their seat is Crakehall, and their words are 'None so Fierce'. Their sigil is a black and white brindled boar on a brown field. Members are traditionally big-boned and exceptionally strong. They once briefly provided a king to the Iron Islands.
539.name: House: Crakehall of Crakehall

540.content: House Marbrand of Ashemark: A major noble house of the westerlands formed by the union of First Men and Andal blood. Their seat is Ashemark, and their words are 'Burning Bright'. Their sigil depicts a burning orange tree on a smoke-grey field. They are considered key bannermen of Casterly Rock and are often high in the councils of House Lannister.
540.name: House: Marbrand of Ashemark

541.comment: House: Lefford of the Golden Tooth
541.content: House Lefford of the Golden Tooth: A principal house of the westerlands that controls the Golden Tooth, the main entrance to the west. Their sigil is a golden inverted pile on sky blue with a yellow sun in the canton. The house was established when an Andal warlord married into First Men nobility. They are responsible for the logistics and supplies of the Lannister armies.
541.name: House: Lefford of the Golden Tooth

542.content: House Swyft of Cornfield: A knightly house from the westerlands seated at Cornfield. Their sigil is a blue bantam rooster on a yellow field, and their words are 'Awake! Awake!'. Though currently knightly, they may have once been a lordly house. The family rose to prominence through the marriage of Dorna Swyft to Kevan Lannister.
542.name: House: Swyft of Cornfield

543.content: House Payne: A noble house of the westerlands and principal bannerman to House Lannister. Their sigil is purple and white chequy with a golden coin in each square. They have produced notable figures such as Ser Ilyn Payne, the King's Justice, and Podrick Payne. The origin of the coins on their arms is associated with an ancient house tale.
543.name: House: Payne of the Westerlands

544.content: House Westerling of the Crag: An ancient but impoverished house of First Men origin from the northwestern westerlands. Their seat is the Crag, and their words are 'Honor, Not Honors'. Their sigil consists of six white seashells on a sand-colored field. Despite their noble lineage, their wealth declined after their gold mines failed.
544.name: House: Westerling of the Crag

545.content: House Brax of Hornvale: A lordly house from the westerlands and among the chief bannermen to Casterly Rock. Their seat is Hornvale, and their sigil is a purple unicorn on a silver field. The family provides significant heavy cavalry to the Lannister host. They were founded during the Andal invasion of the west.
545.name: House: Brax of Hornvale

546.content: House Florent of Brightwater Keep: A noble house from the Reach that claims a superior right to Highgarden due to blood ties to the Gardener kings. Their seat is Brightwater Keep, and their sigil is a red fox in a circle of blue flowers on ermine. Members are physically distinguished by prominent ears. They were attainted and dispossessed of their lands during the War of the Five Kings.
546.name: House: Florent of Brightwater Keep

547.content: House Oakheart of Old Oak: An ancient and powerful First Men house from the Reach. Their seat is Old Oak, and their words are 'Our Roots Go Deep'. Their sigil depicts three green oak leaves on a gold field. They have a long history of enmity with the Dornish and were founding members of the Kingdom of the Reach.
547.name: House: Oakheart of Old Oak

548.content: House Rowan of Goldengrove: One of the oldest and most prominent noble families in the Reach. Their seat is Goldengrove, and their sigil is a golden tree on a silver field. They serve as Marshals of the Northmarch and rule over extensive northern territories in the Reach. They trace their descent back to Rowan Gold-Tree, a legendary daughter of Garth Greenhand.
548.name: House: Rowan of Goldengrove

549.comment: House: Fossoway (Red and Green Apple branches)
549.content: House Fossoway: A noble family of the Reach that split into two rival branches. House Fossoway of Cider Hall uses a red apple sigil and is known as the 'red-apple Fossoways'. House Fossoway of New Barrel, founded after a tourney dispute, uses a green apple and is known as the 'green-apple Fossoways'. Both houses trace their origin to the legendary Foss the Archer.
549.name: House: Fossoway (Red and Green Apple branches)

550.content: House Mullendore of Uplands: A lordly house from the Reach that serves as a vassal to House Hightower. Their seat is Uplands, and the family is currently headed by Lord Martyn Mullendore. Members of the house are known for their cheerful dispositions and their history of service in the Reach. They have occasionally married into other high-ranking families like House Templeton.
550.name: House: Mullendore of Uplands

551.content: House Yronwood: The most powerful house in Dorne after the ruling Martells. Their seat is Yronwood, a fortress defending the Stone Way into Dorne. The head of the house is known as the Bloodroyal, and the house sigil is a black portcullis grill over sand. They are stony Dornishmen who typically possess blond hair and blue eyes. Historically, the Yronwoods claimed the title High King of Dorne before the arrival of the Rhoynar.
551.name: House: Yronwood of Yronwood

552.content: House Fowler: An ancient First Men family that rules as the Warden of the Prince's Pass. Their seat is Skyreach, and their house words are 'Let Me Soar'. The house sigil depicts a hooded blue hawk on a silver field. In antiquity, the Fowlers reigned as Kings of Stone and Sky and were among the most powerful monarchs in Dorne.
552.name: House: Fowler of Skyreach

553.content: House Qorgyle: A principal noble house of Dorne seated at Sandstone in the western deserts. Their sigil consists of three black scorpions on a red field. Founded by Andal adventurers, the house fortified the only well for fifty leagues to establish their stronghold. They were historically bannermen to House Yronwood before the unification of Dorne under House Martell.
553.name: House: Qorgyle of Sandstone

554.content: House Uller: A great noble house of Dorne known for a reputation of being impulsive and unpredictable. Their seat is the Hellholt, located deep within the Dornish desert. The house sigil is rayonne yellow over crimson. They are of Andal origin and established their rule during the invasion of Westeros.
554.name: House: Uller of Hellholt

555.comment: House: Vaith of the Red Dunes
555.content: House Vaith: A Dornish house whose head holds the title Lord of the Red Dunes. Their seat is the castle Vaith, located beside the river of the same name. Their sigil is three black leopards standing on a yellow pile on an orange field. The house was established by Andal adventurers during the invasion of Dorne.
555.name: House: Vaith of the Red Dunes

556.content: House Allyrion: A major Dornish noble house seated at Godsgrace near the confluence of the Scourge and the Vaith. Their sigil is a golden hand on gyronny red and black, and their words are 'No Foe May Pass'. Originally founded by Andal adventurers, they were once the overlords of House Martell.
556.name: House: Allyrion of Godsgrace

557.content: House Jordayne: One of the principal noble houses of Dorne, ruling from the Tor on the southern coast of the Sea of Dorne. Their sigil is a golden quill on checkered dark and light green, and their words are 'Let It Be Written'. Founded by Andals, the house was once powerful enough to demand fealty from House Martell.
557.name: House: Jordayne of the Tor

558.content: House Santagar: A house of landed knights from Spottswood in Dorne. Their sigil is a spotted leopard with a golden axe over a per bend sinister blue and white field. Established by Andal adventurers, they have traditionally been noted for their martial service and sand steeds.
558.name: House: Santagar of Spottswood

559.content: House Mallister: A prominent noble family from the riverlands whose seat is the coastal fortress Seagard. Their sigil is a silver eagle on indigo, and their house words are 'Above the Rest'. Seagard was built specifically to defend the coastline from ironborn reavers. The house once ruled as independent Kings of the Trident in antiquity.
559.name: House: Mallister of Seagard

560.content: House Piper: A chief noble house of the riverlands seated at Pinkmaiden Castle. Their sigil depicts a pink dancing maiden in a swirl of white silk over a blue field. Their words are 'Brave and Beautiful'. The house has a history of loyalty to House Tully and famously stood against the Lannisters at the Golden Tooth.
560.name: House: Piper of Pinkmaiden

561.comment: House: Vance (Atranta and Wayfarer's Rest branches)
561.content: House Vance: A noble house divided into two branches: House Vance of Atranta and House Vance of Wayfarer's Rest. They descend from Armistead Vance, one of the mightiest Andal warlords to invade the riverlands. The house traditionally holds significant influence among the river lords of the Trident.
561.name: House: Vance (Atranta and Wayfarer's Rest branches)

562.comment: House: Roote of Lord Harroway's Town
562.content: House Roote: A noble house of the riverlands that rules Lord Harroway's Town. Their historical lineage includes Ser Richard Roote, a founding member of the Kingsguard. The house supported the Blacks during the Dance of the Dragons and remained a prominent vassal in the region.
562.name: House: Roote of Lord Harroway's Town

563.content: House Darry: A noble house from the riverlands whose seat is Castle Darry, featuring the central Plowman's Keep. Their sigil is a black plowman on a brown field. They were staunch Targaryen loyalists who suffered greatly following Robert's Rebellion. The house became functionally extinct in the male line during the War of the Five Kings.
563.name: House: Darry of Darry

564.content: House Mooton: A wealthy noble house of the riverlands ruling the port town of Maidenpool. Their sigil is a red salmon on a white field with a gold tressure, and their words are 'Wisdom and Strength'. They claim descent from the First Men and were once independent kings in the Age of Heroes.
564.name: House: Mooton of Maidenpool

565.content: House Whent: The last house to legally hold the massive castle Harrenhal before being dispossessed. Their sigil depicts nine black bats on a yellow field. Originally knights in service to House Lothston, they were granted Harrenhal for their role in the Lothstons' downfall. The house is noted for its involvement in the great tourney of 281 AC and its history of subsequent tragedy.
565.name: House: Whent of Harrenhal

566.content: House Smallwood: A noble house of the riverlands seated at Acorn Hall. Their sigil is six brown acorns on a yellow field, and their words are 'From These Beginnings'. Though formerly sworn to House Tully, they are currently vassals of House Vance.
566.name: House: Smallwood of Acorn Hall

567.content: House Dondarrion: An old marcher house of the stormlands seated at Blackhaven. Their sigil is a forked purple lightning bolt on a black field speckled with four-pointed stars. The house was founded in the Age of Heroes by a messenger who was saved by lightning during a storm. They are traditional defenders against Dornish incursions.
567.name: House: Dondarrion of Blackhaven

568.content: House Selmy: A principal marcher house of the stormlands located at Harvest Hall. Their sigil depicts three stalks of yellow wheat on a brown field. Known for producing famed warriors, most notably Ser Barristan the Bold, they are among the most respected families of the Dornish Marches.
568.name: House: Selmy of Harvest Hall

569.content: House Swann: One of the oldest and most powerful noble houses in the stormlands, ruling from Stonehelm. Their sigil is two battling swans, black and white, on a per pale white and black field. As marcher lords, they control a major river route inland and are regarded as proud and cautious.
569.name: House: Swann of Stonehelm

570.content: House Caron: A principal marcher house ruling from the castle Nightsong. Their sigil is a field of black nightingales on yellow, and their house words are 'No Song so Sweet'. They hold the title Lord of the Marches and claim to be the oldest of the stormlands' marcher lords.
570.name: House: Caron of Nightsong

571.content: House Estermont: A noble house of the stormlands ruling from the island of Greenstone. Their sigil is a dark green sea turtle on a pale green field. The house rose to high prominence during the reign of Robert I, who was the son of Lady Cassana Estermont.
571.name: House: Estermont of Greenstone

572.content: House Connington: A noble house of the stormlands seated at Griffin's Roost on Cape Wrath. Their sigil depicts two battling griffins countercharged on a red and white field. Once a wealthy lordly house, they were stripped of much of their land and reduced to landed knights following Robert's Rebellion.
572.name: House: Connington of Griffin's Roost

573.content: House Tarth: A noble house that rules the island of Tarth from the seat of Evenfall Hall. Their head is titled the Evenstar, and their sigil is quartered with yellow suns and white crescents on rose and azure. The house has Andal ancestry and historically reigned as independent kings before joining the Storm Kings.
573.name: House: Tarth of Evenfall Hall

574.content: House Velaryon: An ancient house of Valyrian descent ruling the island of Driftmark. Their sigil is a silver seahorse on sea green, and their words are 'The Old, the True, the Brave'. Historically the richest house in the Seven Kingdoms under Lord Corlys, they traditionally provide the bulk of the royal fleet.
574.name: House: Velaryon of Driftmark

575.content: House Celtigar: An ancient and proud house with Valyrian blood, seated on Claw Isle. Their sigil is red crabs strewn on white. They possess a Valyrian steel axe and were among the first houses to support House Targaryen during the Conquest.
575.name: House: Celtigar of Claw Isle

576.content: House Sunglass: A noble house of the crownlands sworn to Dragonstone. Their sigil consists of seven golden seven-pointed stars arranged in a ring on a white field. They are known for their piety and adherence to the Faith of the Seven.
576.name: House: Sunglass of Sweetport Sound

577.comment: House: Bar Emmon of Sharp Point
577.content: House Bar Emmon: A noble house from Sharp Point on Massey's Hook in the crownlands. Their sigil is a leaping blue swordfish on fretty silver and white. Founded by Andal warlords, they were once petty kings before yielding to the Storm Kings and later House Targaryen.
577.name: House: Bar Emmon of Sharp Point

578.content: House Harlaw: One of the most powerful and wealthiest houses of the Iron Islands, ruling the entire island of Harlaw. Their sigil is a silver scythe on black. They rule from the castle of Ten Towers and possess several junior branches across the island.
578.name: House: Harlaw of Harlaw

579.content: House Goodbrother: A powerful ironborn house from Great Wyk, seated at the inland castle of Hammerhorn. Their sigil is a gold-banded black warhorn on red. Unlike most major houses of the isles, they claim descent from the Grey King's eldest brother rather than the king himself.
579.name: House: Goodbrother of Hammerhorn

580.content: House Drumm: An ancient ironborn house that rules Old Wyk, the island considered holiest by the ironmen. Their sigil is a white bone hand on a red field. They possess the Valyrian steel sword Red Rain and trace their history back at least eight hundred years.
580.name: House: Drumm of Old Wyk

581.content: House Botley: A noble house of the Iron Islands seated at Lordsport on the island of Pyke. Their sigil is a shoal of silver fish on a pale green field. They are one of the primary bannermen to House Greyjoy and control the main port of Pyke.
581.name: House: Botley of Lordsport

582.content: [The Rains of Castamere]: A somber ballad commemorating the destruction of House Reyne by Tywin Lannister following their rebellion. The lyrics describe a dialogue between the proud Lord of Castamere and a Lannister lion, culminating in the complete annihilation of the former's line. Tywin Lannister frequently utilizes the performance of this song as a method of intimidation against potential rivals.
582.name: Song: The Rains of Castamere

583.content: [The Dornishman's Wife]: A popular song detailing the tryst between a man and the wife of a Dornishman. Despite the protagonist being mortally wounded by the husband's black steel blade, he considers the encounter a fair trade for the woman's warm kisses. The lyrics contrast the beauty and song of the wife with the cold, leech-like bite of the Dornish blade.
583.name: Song: The Dornishman's Wife

584.content: [Jenny of Oldstones]: A strange and lovely woman of the riverlands who claimed descent from the First Men kings of House Mudd. She was the wife of Prince Duncan Targaryen, who famously renounced his claim to the Iron Throne to marry her. Jenny was often accompanied by an albino woods witch who prophesied the coming of the prince that was promised. Numerous songs, including 'Jenny's Song,' were written to commemorate her tragic romance.
584.name: Character/Song: Jenny of Oldstones

585.comment: Song: The Last of the Giants
585.content: [The Last of the Giants]: A melancholic song performed by the free folk and giants. The lyrics lament the loss of the giants' ancestral forests, rivers, and hills to the encroachment of 'men who are small' and their construction of the Wall. It is often sung to express grief for a disappearing race and their lost companionhood.
585.name: Song: The Last of the Giants

586.content: [Rat Cook]: An infamous figure of the Night's Watch whose legend is associated with the Nightfort. According to myth, he was transformed into an enormous white rat by the gods for the crime of serving a king a pie made of the king's own son. The story serves as a primary representation of the terrible divine consequences awaiting those who violate the sacred laws of guest right.
586.name: Legend: Rat Cook

587.content: [The Seven-Pointed Star]: The oldest and most sacred holy text of the Faith of the Seven. It is divided into sections based on the aspects of the godhead, such as the Maiden's Book. The text chronicles the history of the Faith, teaches that all mankind belongs to the Many-Faced God, and defines the structure of the Seven Heavens and Seven Hells.
587.name: Book: The Seven-Pointed Star

588.content: [White Book]: Also known as 'The Book of the Brothers,' it is a record of the history and achievements of the Kingsguard kept in the White Sword Tower. Every knight who has ever served in the order has a dedicated page to record his deeds. The Lord Commander is responsible for updating the entries, while septons contribute heraldic drawings and illuminations.
588.name: Book: The White Book

589.content: [Dragonkin]: A scholarly work titled 'Dragonkin, Being a History of House Targaryen from Exile to Apotheosis, with a Consideration of the Life and Death of Dragons'. It is part of the collection of rare books kept in the library beneath Castle Black. Maester Aemon considered it important enough to have Samwell Tarly bring it with them on their journey to Oldtown.
589.name: Book: Dragonkin

590.content: [Maiden's Day]: A holy day in the calendar of the Faith of the Seven dedicated to the Maiden. Maidens of noble houses gather in septs to light white candles and hang garlands about the Maiden's statue while singing songs of innocence. All men, as well as mothers, widows, and prostitutes, are strictly barred from entering the sept during these rites.
590.name: Holy Day: Maiden's Day

591.content: [Smith's Day]: A holy day within the religious calendar of the Faith of the Seven. It is a day of religious significance where specific births and events are sometimes noted as occurring on its eve.
591.name: Holy Day: Smith's Day

592.content: [Golden wedding]: A lavish historical celebration in 49 AC held to mark the marriage of Queen Regent Alyssa Velaryon and Lord Rogar Baratheon. The event drew nobility and dignitaries from throughout Westeros and the Free Cities, including the son of the Sealord of Braavos. It was characterized by immense pageantry, feasting, and the presence of numerous knights and performers.
592.name: Event: The Golden Wedding

593.content: [Bedding custom]: A raucous traditional wedding custom in Westeros involving the guests forcibly carrying the bride and groom to their bedchamber. During the process, the guests of the opposite gender undress the couple while shouting ribald jests. The custom is intended to mark the transition to the consummation of the marriage.
593.name: Custom: Bedding

594.content: [Name day]: The annual celebration of the day an individual was named, serving as the Westerosi equivalent of a birthday. Major events, such as royal tournaments or religious drownings, are often staged to coincide with a significant name day. Some superstitious beliefs suggest it is ill fortune to kill a man on his name day.
594.name: Custom: Name Day

595.content: [Guest right]: An ancient and sacred law of hospitality inherited from the First Men. It is formally invoked when a guest eats food and drinks drink, traditionally bread and salt, provided by the host beneath their roof. Once established, both host and guest are protected from mutual harm; the violation of this law is considered a crime equivalent only to kinslaying and invites divine wrath.
595.name: Custom: Guest Right

596.content: [Godswood]: A wooded grove found within the walls of castles throughout the Seven Kingdoms. In the north, every godswood contains a weirwood heart tree, whereas in the south, most were destroyed or replaced by other species like oak or elm. It serves as a place of prayer for those who follow the Old Gods or as a private area of solitude for those who follow the Seven.
596.name: Location: Godswood

597.content: [Sept]: A seven-walled place of worship for the Faith of the Seven. Every sept contains artistic representations of the seven aspects of the godhead, ranging from simple charcoal drawings to ornate marble statues. They are considered holy ground where bloodshed is forbidden. The Great Sept of Baelor in King's Landing is the most significant and holiest sept in the realm.
597.name: Location: Sept

598.content: [Septry]: A monastic community of men, known as brown brothers, sworn to the service of the Faith of the Seven. These communities are often self-sufficient, tending to livestock, vineyards, and orchards while living in quiet contemplation. The leader of a septry is titled the Elder Brother, who oversees the resident proctors and brothers.
598.name: Location: Septry

599.content: [Motherhouse]: A monastic community of the Faith of the Seven for women, including septas, silent sisters, and novices. They are led by a high-ranking member of the clergy titled a Mother. Famous examples include the great motherhouse in Lannisport and the Motherhouse of Maris in Gulltown.
599.name: Location: Motherhouse

600.content: [Silent Sisters]: An order of godsworn women tasked with the preparation of the deceased for the grave. They take a vow of silence and dress in grey robes with hoods that conceal their faces, leaving only the eyes visible. They are often called to escort the bodies of highborn individuals back to their family seats.
600.name: Organization: Silent Sisters

601.content: [Begging Brothers]: A mendicant order of holy brothers within the Faith of the Seven who travel the realms. They are humble members of the clergy who often wear tonsures and simple robes of brown, dun, or green. They are known for preaching to smallfolk and are sometimes viewed as the street-level face of the Faith.
601.name: Organization: Begging Brothers

602.content: [Faith of the Seven]: The dominant religion of the Seven Kingdoms, imported to Westeros by the Andal invaders. It recognizes one god with seven distinct aspects: the Father, Mother, Maiden, Crone, Smith, Warrior, and Stranger. Worship is conducted in seven-walled septs through prayer, hymns, and the lighting of candles.
602.name: Religion: Faith of the Seven

603.content: [Maidenvault]: A keep within the Red Keep of King's Landing, located behind the royal sept. It is a long, slate-roofed building with tall carved doors. It received its name after King Baelor the Blessed confined his three sisters within its walls to prevent them from tempting him with carnal thoughts.
603.name: Location: Maidenvault

604.content: [Moon tea]: A potent medicinal herbal draft used to prevent or abort pregnancies. It is traditionally brewed by maesters or woods witches using ingredients such as tansy, mint, wormwood, honey, and pennyroyal. While commonly used, it can have dangerous side effects and its use is considered a grave sin by devout members of the Faith.
604.name: Medicine: Moon Tea

605.content: [Myrish lace]: A variety of exceptionally intricate and costly lace produced in the Free City of Myr. It is considered highly valuable, often said to be worth its weight in gold. The lace is a popular luxury import among the high nobility of Westeros and is frequently used to adorn gowns and royal wedding attire.
605.name: Item: Myrish Lace

606.content: [Arbor gold]: A premium white wine produced in the Arbor, noted for being fruity, rich, and sweet. It possesses an excellent reputation throughout the known world and is a particular favorite of Queen Cersei Lannister. The wine is frequently served at noble feasts and small council meetings.
606.name: Drink: Arbor Gold

607.comment: Lore: Legendary era following the Pact
607.content: Age of Heroes: An era of Westerosi history following the forging of the Pact between the First Men and the children of the forest. It lasted for approximately four thousand years, characterized by the rise of numerous petty kings and the foundation of the Great Houses. Known through oral histories recorded millennia later by septons, it is populated by figures such as Brandon the Builder and Lann the Clever.
607.name: Lore: Legendary era following the Pact

608.comment: Lore: A generation-long winter and darkness
608.content: Long Night: A prehistoric period approximately 8,000 years before Aegon's Conquest characterized by a generation-long darkness and a winter that lasted for years. During this time, the Others emerged from the uttermost north, wielding swords of ice and raising wights to destroy humanity. The darkness was eventually ended by the Battle for the Dawn, in which the children of the forest and First Men united to drive the Others back into the frozen north.
608.name: Lore: A generation-long winter and darkness

609.content: Night's King: The legendary thirteenth Lord Commander of the Night's Watch who reigned during the Age of Heroes. [Appearance details]: Said to be a fearless warrior who fell in love with a woman with skin white as the moon and eyes like blue stars. [Personality/Traits]: A sorcerer who declared himself king and his lover queen. [Key History]: He ruled from the Nightfort for thirteen years, committing horrific atrocities and making sacrifices to the Others before being cast down by the joint forces of Brandon the Breaker and Joramun. [Affiliations]: Night's Watch, House Stark (allegedly).
609.name: Character: Legendary 13th Lord Commander

610.content: Bran the Builder: A legendary figure from the Age of Heroes and the founder of House Stark. [Personality/Traits]: Renowned as the greatest architect and builder in history. [Key History]: He is credited with raising the Wall with the aid of giants and the children of the forest, as well as constructing Winterfell, Storm's End, and the Hightower. [Affiliations]: House Stark, First Men.
610.name: Character: Founder of House Stark

611.comment: Character: Legendary savior of the R'hllor faith
611.content: Azor Ahai: A legendary hero from Asshai who rose to fight the darkness during the Long Night. [Personality/Traits]: A messianic warrior expected to be reborn as a champion of R'hllor. [Key History]: He forged the flaming sword Lightbringer by plunging it into the heart of his wife, Nissa Nissa. [Affiliations]: R'hllor, Asshai.
611.name: Character: Legendary savior of the R'hllor faith

612.content: Nissa Nissa: The wife of the legendary hero Azor Ahai. [Key History]: She sacrificed her living heart to her husband's steel, combining her soul with the blade to create the flaming sword Lightbringer. [Affiliations]: Azor Ahai.
612.name: Character: Wife of Azor Ahai

613.comment: Character: Legendary figure of the Long Night
613.content: Last Hero: A legendary northern figure who lived during the Long Night. [Key History]: He traveled into the north to seek the aid of the children of the forest to defeat the Others, allegedly slaying them with a blade of dragonsteel. [Affiliations]: First Men, Night's Watch.
613.name: Character: Legendary figure of the Long Night

614.content: Children of the Forest: A diminutive, non-human race of creatures who inhabited Westeros during the Dawn Age. [Appearance details]: Small humanoid beings, dark and beautiful, with large eyes and mysterious powers. [Personality/Traits]: Gifted with supernatural abilities over nature and dreams, including greensight and skinchanging. [Key History]: They fought the First Men before signing the Pact on the Isle of Faces and later aided in the fight against the Others. [Affiliations]: Old Gods.
614.name: Group: Original inhabitants of Westeros

615.comment: Group: Massive humanoids of the north
615.content: Giants: A dwindling race of huge, shaggy humanoids inhabiting the lands beyond the Wall. [Appearance details]: Growing between ten to fourteen feet tall with squashed-in faces and square teeth. [Personality/Traits]: Possessed of immense strength but below-human intelligence; they speak the Old Tongue. [Key History]: They aided Brandon the Builder in raising the Wall and were part of Mance Rayder's host. [Affiliations]: Free Folk.
615.name: Group: Massive humanoids of the north

616.content: Valyrian Freehold: A vast territory in Essos centered on the Valyrian peninsula. [Geography]: Built around the Fourteen Flames, a chain of volcanoes. [Ruler]: Governed by lords freeholder, the most powerful being the dragonlords. [Key Features]: Renowned for its advanced magic, dragons, and the forging of Valyrian steel. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, House Velaryon, House Celtigar.
616.name: Location: Ancient empire of Essos

617.content: Doom of Valyria: A cataclysm of unspecified nature that occurred in 102 BC, causing the collapse of the Valyrian Freehold. [Key History]: It resulted in the destruction of the city of Valyria, the loss of ancient magic and records, and the fragmentation of the peninsula into islands surrounded by the Smoking Sea. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen (survivors).
617.name: Event: Cataclysmic destruction of Valyria

618.content: Aurion: A dragonlord who was visiting Qohor during the Doom of Valyria. [Personality/Traits]: Ambitious survivor who proclaimed himself the first Emperor of Valyria. [Key History]: He raised a host of thirty thousand Qohorik and flew south atop his dragon to reclaim the ruins of the Freehold, but he and his army were never seen again. [Affiliations]: Valyrian Freehold.
618.name: Character: Surviving Valyrian dragonlord

619.content: Jaenara Belaerys: A noblewoman and dragonrider of the Valyrian Freehold. [Key History]: She explored the continent of Sothoryos for three years atop her dragon, Terrax, traveling farther south than anyone before her; she returned declaring the land to be as large as Essos and without end. [Affiliations]: Belaerys family, Valyria.
619.name: Character: Valyrian dragonrider and explorer

620.content: Terrax: A dragon belonging to Jaenara Belaerys. [Key History]: It carried its rider on a three-year exploration of the continent of Sothoryos, reaching deeper into the southern jungles than any other recorded flight. [Affiliations]: Jaenara Belaerys, Valyrian Freehold.
620.name: Dragon: Mount of Jaenara Belaerys

621.content: Garin the Great: The legendary Prince of Chroyane who led the Rhoynar during the Second Spice War. [Key History]: He raised an army of a quarter-million to oppose the Valyrian Freehold but was defeated and captured; legend states he called down Mother Rhoyne's wrath, resulting in Garin's Curse (greyscale) falling upon the conquerors. [Affiliations]: Rhoynar, Chroyane.
621.name: Character: Prince of the Rhoynar

622.content: Mors Martell: The Lord of the Sandship who became the first Prince of Dorne. [Key History]: He formed a strategic alliance by marrying the Rhoynish queen Nymeria, combining their forces to conquer the Dornish peninsula in Nymeria's War; he was slain in the Third Battle of the Boneway. [Affiliations]: House Martell, Nymeria.
622.name: Character: Prince of Dorne

623.comment: Character: Lord of Dragonstone who led the Targaryens to Westeros
623.content: Aenar Targaryen: A dragonlord of the Valyrian Freehold known as Aenar the Exile. [Key History]: In response to his daughter Daenys's prophetic visions, he sold his holdings in Valyria and moved his entire family and five dragons to Dragonstone twelve years before the Doom. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, Valyrian Freehold.
623.name: Character: Lord of Dragonstone who led the Targaryens to Westeros

624.comment: Character: Prophetic daughter of Aenar Targaryen
624.content: Daenys Targaryen: The maiden daughter of Lord Aenar Targaryen, famously called Daenys the Dreamer. [Personality/Traits]: A powerful dragon dreamer and visionary. [Key History]: She foretold the total destruction of Valyria, prompting the Targaryen migration to Dragonstone; her visions were recorded in the lost book 'Signs and Portents'. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
624.name: Character: Prophetic daughter of Aenar Targaryen

625.content: Artys Arryn: The legendary founder of House Arryn and the first King of Mountain and Vale. Known as the Falcon Knight, he was an Andal knight esteemed as the finest warrior of his age. During the Andal invasion, he unified the Andal forces and defeated High King Robar II Royce at the Battle of the Seven Stars. His legacy is often conflated in song with the mythical Winged Knight who slew the Griffin King. [Affiliations]: House Arryn, Andals.
625.name: Character: Artys I Arryn

626.content: Erreg the Kinslayer: A legendary Andal king known for his brutal conquest of the riverlands. He is infamous for attacking the sacred grove of High Heart, where he slaughtered the resident children of the forest and First Men. He ordered the felling of the hill's thirty-one ancient weirwood trees, an act for which he is still remembered in song. [Affiliations]: Andals.
626.name: Character: Erreg the Kinslayer

627.content: Tristifer IV Mudd: The fourth King of the Rivers and the Hills to bear his name and the last truly great First Men monarch of the riverlands. Known as the Hammer of Justice, he was a formidable warrior who defended his realm against the initial waves of the Andal invasion. He raised the castle of Oldstones and famously defeated and beheaded King Roland II Arryn. He was eventually overwhelmed by the combined strength of seven Andal kings. [Affiliations]: House Mudd.
627.name: Character: Tristifer IV Mudd

628.content: Theon Stark: A King in the North during the era of the Andal invasion, known as the Hungry Wolf. He is depicted in the crypts of Winterfell as a gaunt man with long hair and a skinny beard. He earned his nickname through near-constant warfare, most notably smashing the Andal warlord Argos Sevenstar at the Weeping Water. Following his victory, he raided the coast of Andalos and displayed the heads of his victims along the northern shores. [Affiliations]: House Stark.
628.name: Character: Theon Stark

629.content: Robar II Royce: The last of the First Men Bronze Kings and the only High King of the Vale, the Fingers, and the Mountains of the Moon. He succeeded his grandfather Yorwyck VI Royce and successfully unified the remaining First Men houses of the Vale against the Andal invaders. A celebrated archer, he was eventually defeated and slain by the Andal host of Artys Arryn at the Battle of the Seven Stars. [Affiliations]: House Royce, First Men.
629.name: Character: Robar II Royce

630.content: Argos Sevenstar: A prominent Andal warlord who attempted to conquer the North during the migration from Andalos. He led one of the most significant Andal threats to the Stark domains but was ultimately defeated by King Theon Stark. Following his death at the Battle of the Weeping Water, his body was displayed on the prow of Theon's ship during the retaliatory raid on Andalos. [Affiliations]: Andals.
630.name: Character: Argos Sevenstar

631.content: Armistead Vance: Regarded as the mightiest of the Andal warlords to invade the riverlands. He was one of the seven kings who finally defeated Tristifer IV Mudd, the last great First Men king of the region. He granted lands at the confluence of the Red Fork and Tumblestone to Axel Tully, which led to the foundation of Riverrun. [Affiliations]: House Vance, Andals.
631.name: Character: Armistead Vance

632.content: Mern IX Gardener: The ninth of his name and the final King of the Reach from House Gardener. He allied with King Loren I Lannister to form the 'Two Kings' and oppose Aegon the Conqueror with a massive host. He commanded the center of the combined army at the Battle of the Field of Fire. He perished in dragonflame along with his sons and all his kin, leading to the extinction of his ancient line. [Affiliations]: House Gardener.
632.name: Character: Mern IX Gardener

633.content: Loren I Lannister: Known as Loren the Last, he was the final King of the Rock and the head of House Lannister during the Conquest. He allied with King Mern IX Gardener to oppose the Targaryen invasion. After surviving the Field of Fire, he submitted to Aegon I and was named the first Lord of Casterly Rock and Warden of the West. His submission ensured the survival of House Lannister under the new dynasty. [Affiliations]: House Lannister.
633.name: Character: Loren I Lannister

634.content: Edmyn Tully: The Lord of Riverrun who led the river lord rebellion against King Harren the Black. He was the first lord to go over to Aegon the Conqueror during the War of Conquest. In reward for his loyalty, he was named the first Lord Paramount of the Trident. He later served as the second Hand of the King to Aegon I Targaryen. [Affiliations]: House Tully.
634.name: Character: Edmyn Tully

635.content: Vickon Greyjoy: The Lord Reaper of Pyke who became the first Lord of the Iron Islands under the Iron Throne. Following the invasion of the Iron Islands by Aegon I in 2 AC, the ironborn were allowed to choose their own ruler and selected Vickon. He ruled as a loyal vassal of House Targaryen and was eventually succeeded by his son, Goren. [Affiliations]: House Greyjoy.
635.name: Character: Vickon Greyjoy

636.content: Visenya Targaryen: The elder sister and wife of King Aegon I. She was a formidable dragonrider who flew Vhagar and a skilled warrior who wielded the Valyrian steel sword Dark Sister. Visenya possessed a harsh, austere beauty with long silver-gold hair often bound in rings or braids. She was characterized as stern, serious, and unforgiving, with some claiming she dabbled in dark sorceries and poisons. She was instrumental in establishing the Kingsguard and oversaw the construction of the Red Keep. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, Greens.
636.name: Character: Visenya Targaryen

637.content: Rhaenys Targaryen: The youngest sister and favorite wife of King Aegon I. She was a dragonrider who flew Meraxes and was known for her playful, mischievous personality. She possessed the classical Valyrian features of silver-gold hair and purple eyes. Rhaenys was a patron of the arts and singers, and she was responsible for knitting the realm together through arranged marriages and legal decrees like the rule of thumb. She died in Dorne during the First Dornish War. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
637.name: Character: Rhaenys Targaryen

638.content: Orys Baratheon: The founder of House Baratheon and the first Lord of Storm's End. He was a close companion and rumored bastard half-brother of Aegon the Conqueror. A fierce commander, he slew the last Storm King, Argilac the Arrogant, in single combat during the Last Storm. He served as the first Hand of the King but resigned after his sword hand was chopped off by the Wyl of Wyl during the First Dornish War. Orys married Argilac's daughter, Argella Durrandon, and adopted her house's sigil and words. [Affiliations]: House Baratheon, House Targaryen.
638.name: Character: Orys Baratheon

639.content: Aenys I Targaryen: The second Targaryen king to sit the Iron Throne, the son of Aegon I and Rhaenys. He was described as a weak and indecisive ruler, lacking the martial strength of his father and brother. His reign was plagued by multiple rebellions and a deteriorating relationship with the Faith of the Seven due to his family's marriage practices. He eventually fled King's Landing for Dragonstone, where he died of illness. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
639.name: Character: Aenys I Targaryen

640.content: Maegor I Targaryen: The third Targaryen monarch, known as Maegor the Cruel. The son of Aegon I and Visenya, he was a massive, bull-like man of immense strength and a savage nature. He usurped the throne from his nephew Aegon the Uncrowned, whom he later slew in battle. Maegor is infamous for his war against the Faith Militant and for executing the builders of the Red Keep to preserve its secrets. He had six wives, known as the Black Brides, but failed to produce a living heir. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
640.name: Character: Maegor I Targaryen

641.content: Jaehaerys I Targaryen: The fourth Targaryen king, celebrated as the Conciliator and the Old King. He ruled for fifty-five years, bringing unprecedented peace and prosperity to the Seven Kingdoms. Alongside Septon Barth, he unified the realm's laws into the Great Code and established the Doctrine of Exceptionalism to reconcile with the Faith. He was a wise diplomat, an avid traveler, and a dragonrider who flew Vermithor. He was married to his sister-wife, Queen Alysanne, with whom he had thirteen children. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
641.name: Character: Jaehaerys I Targaryen

642.content: Alysanne Targaryen: The queen consort of Jaehaerys I, beloved by the smallfolk as Good Queen Alysanne. She was a dragonrider who flew Silverwing and was known for her wisdom and sharp mind. Alysanne was a champion of women's rights, establishing women's courts and persuading the king to abolish the right of the first night. She bore thirteen children, though few outlived her, leading to a life marked by both duty and personal grief. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
642.name: Character: Alysanne Targaryen

643.content: Barth: A blacksmith's son who rose to become a septon and the Hand of the King to Jaehaerys I for forty years. He was considered the wisest man to ever serve as Hand, providing the realm with peace and plenty. Barth was a brilliant scholar and the author of 'Dragons, Wyrms, and Wyverns: Their Unnatural History'. He was instrumental in creating the first unified code of law for the Seven Kingdoms. [Affiliations]: Faith of the Seven, House Targaryen.
643.name: Character: Septon Barth

644.content: Elysar: A Grand Maester who served King Jaehaerys I Targaryen on the small council. He was a member of the order of maesters and participated in the king's governance for several decades. He is associated with the study of mathematics or economics, symbolized by his ring, rod, and mask of electrum. [Affiliations]: Citadel, House Targaryen.
644.name: Character: Grand Maester Elysar

645.content: Rego Draz: A wealthy merchant from Pentos who served as master of coin for Jaehaerys I. Despite his low birth, he became the richest man in Pentos before moving to King's Landing to help rebuild the realm's depleted treasury. He was known for his stout build, silken robes, and ruby rings, and he was mockingly titled the 'Lord of Air' as he held no lands. Rego was responsible for securing loans from the Iron Bank and implementing luxury taxes. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, Pentos.
645.name: Character: Rego Draz

646.content: Daemon Velaryon: The Lord of the Tides and first master of ships for Aegon the Conqueror. He was a wealthy and loyal vassal of House Targaryen and one of Aegon's closest friends. He led the Targaryen fleet during the initial invasion of Westeros and participated in the council at Dragonstone where the conquest was planned. [Affiliations]: House Velaryon, House Targaryen.
646.name: Character: Daemon Velaryon

647.comment: Character: Aemon Targaryen (son of Jaehaerys I)
647.content: Aemon Targaryen: The son and heir of King Jaehaerys I, who served as Prince of Dragonstone and master of laws. He was a tall, handsome man with pale lilac eyes and hair that shone like white gold. A dragonrider who flew Caraxes, he was a skilled warrior and respected leader. He was married to Lady Jocelyn Baratheon and was the father of Princess Rhaenys. Aemon was killed by a crossbowman while defending Tarth. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
647.name: Character: Aemon Targaryen (son of Jaehaerys I)

648.comment: Character: Baelon Targaryen (son of Jaehaerys I)
648.content: Baelon Targaryen: The second son of Jaehaerys I, known as Baelon the Brave and the Spring Prince. He was a celebrated warrior and dragonrider who flew Vhagar. Baelon served as Hand of the King and was named Prince of Dragonstone following the death of his brother Aemon. He was married to his sister Alyssa, and their union produced kings Viserys I and Prince Daemon. He died of a burst belly in 101 AC. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
648.name: Character: Baelon Targaryen (son of Jaehaerys I)

649.content: Alyssa Targaryen: The daughter of Jaehaerys I and Alysanne, known for her spirited and tomboyish nature. She had a long face, a broken nose, and mismatched eyes of green and purple. A dragonrider who flew Meleys, she was a skilled hunter and joined her brother-husband Baelon in his martial pursuits. She was the mother of Viserys I and Daemon Targaryen and died following a difficult childbirth at the age of twenty-four. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
649.name: Character: Alyssa Targaryen

650.comment: Group: Maegor I's champions in the trial of seven
650.content: Maegor's Seven: The group of champions who fought alongside King Maegor I in a trial of seven against the Faith Militant's Warrior's Sons. The champions included Ser Bernarr Brune, Ser Bramm of Blackhull, Ser Rayford Rosby, Ser Guy Lothston, Lord Lucifer Massey, and Dick Bean. Maegor was the sole survivor of the brutal contest, which resulted in the deaths of all other participants, including the Faith's leader, Ser Damon Morrigen. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, Warrior's Sons.
650.name: Group: Maegor I's champions in the trial of seven

651.comment: Lore: Rebellion of the Faith against the Targaryens
651.content: Faith Militant uprising: A major rebellion by the militant orders of the Faith of the Seven against Targaryen rule. The conflict was triggered by the incestuous and polygamous marriage practices of House Targaryen. It began during the reign of Aenys I, escalated under the brutal suppression of Maegor I, and was finally resolved by Jaehaerys I. The uprising ended with the disarming of the Stars and Swords and the establishment of the Doctrine of Exceptionalism. [Affiliations]: Faith of the Seven, House Targaryen.
651.name: Lore: Rebellion of the Faith against the Targaryens

652.content: Dragonstone: An island fortress located at the mouth of Blackwater Bay. It was built as the westernmost outpost of the Valyrian Freehold and is famous for its unique architecture, featuring towers shaped like dragons created through arcane magic. The castle served as the seat for House Targaryen before the Conquest and later became the traditional seat of the heir apparent to the Iron Throne. It sits beneath the smoking volcano known as the Dragonmont. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
652.name: Location: Ancestral Targaryen seat

653.comment: Location: The first Targaryen fortress in King's Landing
653.content: Aegonfort: The initial wooden and earthen fortress built by Aegon I at the mouth of the Blackwater Rush following his landing in Westeros. It served as the center of Aegon's authority during the early years of his reign and was where the Iron Throne was first forged from the swords of his enemies. The fortress was eventually torn down in 35 AC to make way for the more permanent stone construction of the Red Keep. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
653.name: Location: The first Targaryen fortress in King's Landing

654.comment: Character: Daeron Targaryen (son of Viserys I)
654.content: Daeron Targaryen: The youngest son of King Viserys I and Queen Alicent Hightower, known as Daeron the Daring. [Appearance details]: A handsome youth with the silver hair of his house. [Personality/Traits]: A popular and courageous warrior who rode the blue dragon Tessarion. [Key History]: He was a critical commander for the Greens, winning the Battle of the Honeywine and sacking Bitterbridge in vengeance for the death of Prince Maelor. He perished at the Second Battle of Tumbleton, though the exact manner of his death remains a subject of historical debate. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, Greens.
654.name: Character: Daeron Targaryen (son of Viserys I)

655.content: Rhaena Targaryen: The twin sister of Baela Targaryen and daughter of Prince Daemon. [Appearance details]: A Valyrian beauty with silver-gold hair. [Personality/Traits]: Unlike her twin, she did not ride a dragon during the war, as her hatchling Morning only emerged as the conflict ended. [Key History]: She spent much of the Dance of the Dragons in the Vale of Arryn for her safety. She later married Ser Corwyn Corbray and then Garmund Hightower. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, Blacks.
655.name: Character: Rhaena Targaryen (daughter of Daemon)

656.content: Rhaenys Targaryen: The daughter of Prince Aemon and wife of Corlys Velaryon. [Appearance details]: In her youth, she was a great beauty with black hair that turned to silver in age. [Personality/Traits]: A high-spirited and fearless dragonrider who flew Meleys, the Red Queen. [Key History]: Famously passed over for the throne at the Great Council of 101 AC, earning the title 'The Queen Who Never Was'. She died valiantly during the battle at Rook's Rest, taking on the dragons Vhagar and Sunfyre simultaneously. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, House Velaryon, Blacks.
656.name: Character: Rhaenys Targaryen (daughter of Aemon)

657.content: Roderick Dustin: The Lord of Barrowton and commander of the Winter Wolves. [Appearance details]: A savage veteran warrior often seen blood-drenched in battle. [Personality/Traits]: Famed for his berserker rage and disregard for his own wounds. [Key History]: He led two thousand northerners south to fight for Rhaenyra, scoring major victories at the Butcher's Ball and the First Battle of Tumbleton. He was slain at Tumbleton after mortally wounding Lord Ormund Hightower and Ser Bryndon Hightower. [Affiliations]: House Dustin, Blacks.
657.name: Character: Roderick Dustin

658.content: Kermit Tully: The young Lord of Riverrun and leader of the riverland host known as 'The Lads'. [Appearance details]: A youth with the vibrant red hair of House Tully. [Personality/Traits]: Bold and energetic, he was the most prominent riverlord of his time. [Key History]: He won the decisive Battle of the Kingsroad against Borros Baratheon, effectively ending the Green threat to the capital. He was a key figure in installing Aegon III on the throne. [Affiliations]: House Tully, Blacks.
658.name: Character: Kermit Tully

659.content: Benjicot Blackwood: The boy-lord of Raventree Hall during the Dance of the Dragons. [Appearance details]: He was only eleven years old when he inherited his seat. [Personality/Traits]: Despite his youth, he was a brilliant and courageous battle commander. [Key History]: Known as 'Bloody Ben,' he fought in the major battles of the riverlands and accompanied the host that took King's Landing at the war's end. He remained a close ally to the crown during the early reign of Aegon III. [Affiliations]: House Blackwood, Blacks.
659.name: Character: Benjicot Blackwood

660.content: Unwin Peake: The Lord of Starpike who served as Hand of the King and Regent for Aegon III. [Appearance details]: A stern and calculating lord from the Reach. [Personality/Traits]: A ruthless political player who sought to advance his family's status through intrigue and the elimination of rivals. [Key History]: He was a leader of the Caltrops during the Dance and later seized power in the capital during the chaotic regency years. His attempt to marry his daughter to the King led to his eventual resignation. [Affiliations]: House Peake, Greens.
660.name: Character: Unwin Peake

661.comment: Event: The governance of Cregan Stark
661.content: Hour of the Wolf: A significant six-day period in 131 AC when Cregan Stark governed as Hand of the King in King's Landing. During this time, the Lord of Winterfell administered stern justice to those involved in the poisoning of Aegon II Targaryen. The event concluded with the execution of Lord Larys Strong and Ser Gyles Belgrave, and the mass exile of others to the Night's Watch. It is regarded as the formal end of the Dance of the Dragons.
661.name: Event: The governance of Cregan Stark

662.comment: Lore: The initial war between Daeron II and Daemon I
662.content: First Blackfyre Rebellion: An open civil war breaking out in 196 AC when Daemon I Blackfyre claimed the Iron Throne from his half-brother Daeron II. The war divided the realm as lords joined either the Red or Black Dragon. It culminated in the massive Battle of the Redgrass Field, where ten thousand men perished and the Blackfyre cause was broken by the death of Daemon and his eldest sons. [Affiliations]: House Blackfyre, House Targaryen.
662.name: Lore: The initial war between Daeron II and Daemon I

663.content: Daeron II Targaryen: The twelfth Targaryen king to sit the Iron Throne, known as Daeron the Good. [Appearance]: Spindly with round shoulders and a small wobbly belly. [Personality]: Scholarly and peaceful, he preferred the company of septons and maesters over warriors. [Key History]: He successfully brought Dorne into the realm through marriage, though his Dornish ties and the rumors of his parentage provoked the First Blackfyre Rebellion; he died during the Great Spring Sickness. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, House Martell.
663.name: Character: King Daeron II

664.content: Baelor Targaryen: The eldest son of Daeron II and a celebrated Hand of the King. [Appearance]: He possessed the dark hair and features of his Dornish mother, Myriah Martell. [Personality]: A man of immense honor and the 'soul of chivalry.' [Key History]: He acted as the 'hammer' to Maekar's 'anvil' at the Redgrass Field and later died accidentally at the Ashford tourney after defending Duncan the Tall in a trial of seven. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
664.name: Character: Prince Baelor Targaryen

665.content: Maekar I Targaryen: The fourteenth Targaryen monarch and former Prince of Summerhall. [Appearance]: A powerfully built man with a square jut of jaw. [Personality]: Stern, prickly, and prone to brooding, he often felt overlooked by his father and brothers. [Key History]: He provided the decisive 'anvil' force at the Redgrass Field and later ascended the throne after his brother Aerys I died without issue; he was slain at the storming of Starpike. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen.
665.name: Character: King Maekar I

666.content: Aemon Targaryen: The third son of Maekar I and the long-serving maester of Castle Black. [Appearance]: In extreme age, he was blind, wrinkled, and stooped, though he retained a sharp mind. [Personality]: Wise, humble, and dedicated to his vows, he twice refused the Iron Throne to remain a servant of the realm. [Key History]: He joined the Night's Watch to prevent his presence being used against his brother Aegon V and provided counsel to Lord Commanders for decades. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, Night's Watch, Citadel.
666.name: Character: Maester Aemon

667.content: Duncan the Tall: A legendary Lord Commander of the Kingsguard who originated as a hedge knight from Flea Bottom. [Appearance]: An immense man standing nearly seven feet tall, with shaggy brown hair and powerful shoulders. [Personality]: Humble, slow of wit but courageous, and deeply committed to the true meaning of knighthood. [Key History]: He took Aegon V as his squire and eventually rose to lead the Kingsguard; he died at Summerhall while rescuing members of the royal family. [Affiliations]: Kingsguard, Aegon V Targaryen.
667.name: Character: Ser Duncan the Tall

668.content: Aegon V Targaryen: The fifteenth Targaryen king, known as Aegon the Unlikely. [Appearance]: In his youth, he went bald to hide his identity; as king, he was lean and regal. [Personality]: Willful, kind-hearted toward the smallfolk, and determined to restore dragons to the world. [Key History]: He spent his youth wandering the realm as the squire 'Egg' to Duncan the Tall and perished in the tragedy at Summerhall during an attempt to hatch dragon eggs. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, Duncan the Tall.
668.name: Character: King Aegon V

669.content: Gormon Peake: The Lord of Starpike and a relentless Blackfyre loyalist. [Appearance]: Sour-faced with a well-trimmed grey-black-white beard and flinty eyes. [Personality]: Arrogant and ambitious, driven by the desire to recover his family's lost castles. [Key History]: A survivor of the First Rebellion, he orchestrated the Second Blackfyre Rebellion at Whitewalls but was captured and beheaded by Bloodraven for his treason. [Affiliations]: House Peake, House Blackfyre.
669.name: Character: Lord Gormon Peake

670.content: Daemon II Blackfyre: The third son of Daemon I and the leader of the brief Second Blackfyre Rebellion. [Appearance]: Handsome with dyed hair and classic Targaryen features beneath. [Personality]: Dashing but delusional, he relied heavily on dragon dreams that predicted his eventual rise. [Key History]: He traveled incognito as the hedge knight 'John the Fiddler' to the Whitewalls tourney, where he was exposed and imprisoned by Bloodraven. [Affiliations]: House Blackfyre.
670.name: Character: Daemon II Blackfyre

671.content: Haegon I Blackfyre: The fourth son of Daemon I and leader of the Third Blackfyre Rebellion. [Appearance]: Possessed the traditional Valyrian look of his house. [Key History]: He led an invasion of Westeros in 219 AC alongside Bittersteel but was defeated and slain after surrendering his sword. [Affiliations]: House Blackfyre.
671.name: Character: Haegon I Blackfyre

672.content: Aenys Blackfyre: The fifth son of Daemon I. [Key History]: After the death of Maekar I, he wrote from exile to claim the throne; promised safe conduct to the Great Council of 233 AC by Bloodraven, he was instead seized upon arrival in King's Landing and executed as a warning to loyalists. [Affiliations]: House Blackfyre.
672.name: Character: Aenys Blackfyre

673.comment: Lore: The climactic battle of the First Rebellion
673.content: Battle of the Redgrass Field: The final and most bloody engagement of the First Blackfyre Rebellion in 196 AC. Named for the ten thousand men whose blood turned the grass red, the battle saw the deaths of Daemon I and his twin sons. The loyalist victory was secured by the 'Hammer and Anvil' tactics of Baelor Breakspear and Maekar Targaryen. [Affiliations]: House Targaryen, House Blackfyre.
673.name: Lore: The climactic battle of the First Rebellion

674.content: Golden Company: A famous and highly disciplined sellsword company founded in Essos by Bittersteel in 212 AC. Composed primarily of Westerosi exiles, their motto is 'Our word is good as gold,' and their battle cry is 'Beneath the gold, the bitter steel.' They are unique among mercenaries for never breaking a contract and for their desire to return home to Westeros. [Affiliations]: House Blackfyre, Aegor Rivers.
674.name: Group: The elite sellsword company

675.comment: General Lore: The group of merchants, pirates, and mercenaries
675.content: Band of Nine: A group of nine outlaws, exiles, and merchant princes who formed a pact beneath the Tree of Crowns in 258 AC to carve out kingdoms for themselves. Its members included Maelys the Monstrous, the Old Mother, Samarro Saan, and Alequo Adarys. They successfully conquered Tyrosh and the Stepstones before being defeated by the forces of the Iron Throne. Their alliance shattered following the death of Maelys Blackfyre.
675.name: General Lore: The group of merchants, pirates, and mercenaries

676.content: Brynden Tully: A celebrated knight of House Tully and younger brother to Lord Hoster. He is a craggy-faced man with stiff grey hair and a weathered countenance. He earned the name 'Blackfish' after a lifelong quarrel with his brother regarding his refusal to marry. A hero of the War of the Ninepenny Kings, he later served as the Knight of the Gate in the Vale before becoming a primary military commander for Robb Stark during the War of the Five Kings.
676.name: Character: Brynden Tully

677.comment: Character: Former Lord of Storm's End
677.content: Steffon Baratheon: The former Lord of Storm's End and head of House Baratheon. He was a close friend to Aerys II Targaryen and fought as a squire during the War of the Ninepenny Kings. He perished alongside his wife, Cassana Estermont, in a shipwreck within Shipbreaker Bay while returning from a royal mission to find a bride for Prince Rhaegar. He was the father of Robert, Stannis, and Renly Baratheon.
677.name: Character: Former Lord of Storm's End

678.comment: Character: Eldest son of Lord Rickard Stark
678.content: Brandon Stark: The heir to Winterfell and elder brother of Eddard and Lyanna. Known for his 'wolf blood' and fiery temperament, he was a peerless swordsman and jouster. He was betrothed to Catelyn Tully but was executed by King Aerys II in King's Landing. He died by strangulation from a Tyroshi device while trying to reach a sword to save his burning father.
678.name: Character: Eldest son of Lord Rickard Stark

679.comment: Character: Lord Commander of the Kingsguard under Aerys II
679.content: Gerold Hightower: The Lord Commander of the Kingsguard during the reigns of Jaehaerys II and Aerys II. Known as the White Bull for his immense strength and presence, he was the uncle of Lord Leyton Hightower. He remained loyal to the Targaryens until his death at the Tower of Joy at the conclusion of Robert's Rebellion.
679.name: Character: Lord Commander of the Kingsguard under Aerys II

680.comment: Character: Kingsguard knight of House Whent
680.content: Oswell Whent: A knight of the Kingsguard under Aerys II known for his dark humor. He wore a distinctive helm featuring the black bat of House Whent. He acted as a confidant to Prince Rhaegar and was one of the three knights who guarded the Tower of Joy, where he was ultimately slain by Eddard Stark's party.
680.name: Character: Kingsguard knight of House Whent

681.comment: Lore: The cataclysmic fire in 259 AC
681.content: Tragedy at Summerhall: A mysterious and disastrous fire that occurred at the Targaryen pleasure palace in 259 AC. The blaze occurred during an attempt to hatch dragon eggs and resulted in the deaths of King Aegon V, Prince Duncan, and Lord Commander Duncan the Tall. Prince Rhaegar Targaryen was born during the conflagration, a fact that haunted his later life. The event effectively extinguished the Targaryen dream of restoring dragons for generations.
681.name: Lore: The cataclysmic fire in 259 AC

682.content: Aegon V Targaryen: The fifteenth Targaryen monarch, known as Aegon the Unlikely. He was a lean, kind-hearted king who spent his youth wandering the realm as the squire 'Egg'. His reign was marked by efforts to grant rights to the smallfolk, which earned him the enmity of many lords. He died at Summerhall while attempting to hatch dragon eggs to restore his house's power.
682.name: Character: The fifteenth Targaryen king

683.comment: Character: Eldest son of Aegon V
683.content: Duncan Targaryen: The eldest son of Aegon V and former Prince of Dragonstone. He famously renounced his claim to the Iron Throne and broke a betrothal to House Baratheon to marry the lowborn Jenny of Oldstones. Known as the Prince of Dragonflies, he was a tall and romantic figure. He perished alongside his father and Ser Duncan the Tall in the Tragedy at Summerhall.
683.name: Character: Eldest son of Aegon V

684.content: Ghost of High Heart: An ancient, albino dwarf woods witch inhabiting High Heart in the riverlands. She is tiny, with red eyes and white hair, and subsists on the grief of the past. She was a companion to Jenny of Oldstones and survived the Tragedy at Summerhall. She possesses the gift of greensight and provides cryptic prophecies to the brotherhood without banners in exchange for songs.
684.name: Character: Prophetic dwarf woods witch

685.content: Defiance of Duskendale: A major rebellion in 277 AC led by Lord Denys Darklyn, who imprisoned King Aerys II Targaryen for six months over a tax dispute. The crisis ended when Ser Barristan Selmy successfully infiltrated the Dun Fort and rescued the king. In retaliation, Aerys ordered the complete extermination of House Darklyn and House Hollard, marking the beginning of his descent into madness.
685.name: Lore: The 277 AC hostage crisis

686.comment: Lore: The massive tournament during the False Spring
686.content: Tourney at Harrenhal: A grand tournament held in 281 AC by Lord Walter Whent. It drew nobility from across the realm and featured the crowning of Prince Rhaegar as champion and his controversial selection of Lyanna Stark as Queen of Love and Beauty. It was also notable for the appearance of the Knight of the Laughing Tree and the admission of Jaime Lannister to the Kingsguard. The event is seen as the final moment of peace before Robert's Rebellion.
686.name: Lore: The massive tournament during the False Spring

687.comment: Lore: The fall of the capital in 283 AC
687.content: Sack of King's Landing: The climactic betrayal of Robert's Rebellion in which Lord Tywin Lannister's army entered the capital under the guise of loyalty before pillaging the city. The event resulted in the murder of King Aerys II by Jaime Lannister and the brutal deaths of Princess Elia Martell and her children by Gregor Clegane and Amory Lorch. It effectively ended Targaryen rule and established the Baratheon dynasty.
687.name: Lore: The fall of the capital in 283 AC

688.content: Maesters: An order of scholars, healers, and scientists who serve the nobility of the Seven Kingdoms. Based at the Citadel in Oldtown, they forge chains of various metals to signify their mastery of different fields of knowledge, such as silver for medicine and iron for warcraft. Members take sacred vows of celibacy and service, promising to hold no lands and putting aside their family names to serve the realm.
