They provide council, handle raven communications, and provide medical care to the lords they are assigned to. [Seat]: The Citadel, Oldtown.
688.name: General Lore: Maesters

689.content: Grand Maester: The designated representative of the order of maesters to the Iron Throne. This high official sits on the king's small council and serves as a primary royal adviser in King's Landing. While they are sworn to serve the whole realm, the position is often subject to the political pressures of the court. [Affiliations]: Small Council, The Citadel.
689.name: General Lore: Grand Maester

690.content: Archmaester: The most senior members of the order of maesters, each possessing a mask, ring, and rod made of the metal in which they have demonstrated total mastery. They reside at the Citadel, where they teach students and judge their readiness to earn links for their chains. Collectively, they form the Conclave, the governing body that makes major decisions for the order, such as electing the Grand Maester. [Seat]: The Citadel, Oldtown.
690.name: General Lore: Archmaester

691.comment: General Lore: Hand of the King
691.content: Hand of the King: The chief advisor to the monarch and the second most powerful official in the Seven Kingdoms. The Hand is authorized to speak with the king's voice, lead the small council, and dispense justice from the Iron Throne in the king's absence. The office is symbolized by a badge or necklace of linked hands. [Seat]: Tower of the Hand, Red Keep.
691.name: General Lore: Hand of the King

692.content: Small Council: A cabinet of advisors who assist the King of the Seven Kingdoms in the governance of the realm. The council traditionally consists of the Hand of the King, the Grand Maester, the Lord Commander of the Kingsguard, and the masters of coin, laws, ships, and whisperers. They convene in a private chamber in the Red Keep to manage the treasury, the law, and the defense of the realm. [Seat]: Council Chamber, Red Keep.
692.name: General Lore: Small Council

693.content: Iron Throne: The seat of the monarch of the Seven Kingdoms, located in the Great Hall of the Red Keep. It is a massive, asymmetric monstrosity of jagged metal and twisted blades, forged by Aegon I Targaryen from the swords of his defeated enemies. Legend claims it was hammered together from a thousand blades heated by the breath of the dragon Balerion to remind rulers that a king should never sit easy. [Location]: Great Hall, Red Keep.
693.name: Location: Iron Throne

694.content: Kingsguard: An elite order of seven knights sworn for life to protect the person of the King and the royal family. They wear plain white armor and cloaks, holding no lands, titles, or wives in the service of the Iron Throne. Their history and achievements are recorded in the White Book, kept in the White Sword Tower. [Seat]: White Sword Tower, Red Keep.
694.name: General Lore: Kingsguard

695.comment: Organization: City Watch of King's Landing
695.content: City Watch of King's Landing: The primary law enforcement and defensive force of the capital, commonly known as the gold cloaks. They are responsible for manning the city gates, patrolling the streets, and defending the walls under the command of their appointed leader. While they are sworn only to the Iron Throne, they have a history of being subject to corruption and the influence of the Hand or the master of laws. [Seat]: East, West, and Red Keep Barracks.
695.name: Organization: City Watch of King's Landing

696.content: Master of Coin: The royal official responsible for the finances and treasury of the Seven Kingdoms. This councillor oversees the collection of taxes, manages the crown's debts to institutions like the Iron Bank, and ensures the king's expenses are covered. [Affiliations]: Small Council.
696.name: General Lore: Master of Coin

697.content: Master of Ships: The councillor in charge of the royal fleet and the naval defense of the realm. Historically the office was often held by House Velaryon, but it can be granted to any high-ranking noble with naval expertise. [Affiliations]: Small Council.
697.name: General Lore: Master of Ships

698.content: Master of Whisperers: The crown's spymaster, responsible for gathering intelligence and maintaining a network of informants known as 'little birds'. The office is tasked with monitoring potential threats both within the capital and across the narrow sea. [Affiliations]: Small Council.
698.name: General Lore: Master of Whisperers

699.content: Master of Laws: The councillor responsible for the administration of justice and the legal affairs of the kingdom. The office typically oversees the City Watch and advises the crown on the unified code of law. [Affiliations]: Small Council.
699.name: General Lore: Master of Laws

700.content: High Septon: The supreme leader of the Faith of the Seven, believed to be the avatar of the gods on earth. Upon election, the individual renounces their birth name and identity, assuming only the title of the office. They wear a crystal crown and lead worship from the Great Sept of Baelor. [Seat]: Great Sept of Baelor, King's Landing.
700.name: Character/Title: High Septon

701.content: Most Devout: The highest council of septons and septas within the Faith of the Seven, responsible for electing the High Septon. They represent the elite hierarchy of the clergy and often wear garments of cloth-of-silver as a sign of their rank. [Affiliations]: Faith of the Seven.
701.name: General Lore: Most Devout

702.content: Faith of the Seven: The dominant religion of Westeros, recognizing one god with seven distinct aspects: Father, Mother, Warrior, Smith, Maiden, Crone, and Stranger. Worship is conducted in seven-walled buildings called septs through hymns, incense, and the lighting of candles. It was imported by the Andals and is centered in King's Landing and Oldtown. [Affiliations]: Most Devout, Faith Militant.
702.name: Religion: Faith of the Seven

703.content: Old Gods: The nameless deities of stream, stone, and forest originally worshipped by the children of the forest and later the First Men. They are worshipped in silence within godswoods, specifically before ancient weirwood trees carved with faces, known as heart trees. Their influence is strongest in the North and beyond the Wall.
703.name: Religion: Old Gods

key: He Who Dwells Beneath the Waves
704.content: Drowned God: The sea deity of the ironborn of the Iron Islands, who believe they were made in his likeness to reave and conquer. The faith emphasizes paying the 'iron price' and holds the sea as sacred, with its followers believing they will feast in the god's watery halls after death. [Affiliations]: Ironborn.
keys: He Who Dwells Beneath the Waves
704.name: Religion: Drowned God

705.content: R'hllor: A powerful fire deity from Essos, worshipped as the Lord of Light and the God of Flame and Shadow. Followers believe he is locked in eternal conflict with the Great Other and look for the return of the legendary hero Azor Ahai. Worship involves red temples, nightfires, and visions seen in flames by red priests. [Affiliations]: Red Priests.
705.name: Religion: R'hllor

706.content: Faceless Men: A secretive and highly feared guild of assassins based in the House of Black and White in Braavos. They worship the Many-Faced God and view their killings as a gift, using magical techniques to assume the physical identities of others. They are notoriously expensive, requiring a significant sacrifice or steep price for their services. [Seat]: House of Black and White, Braavos.
706.name: Organization: Faceless Men

707.content: Iron Bank of Braavos: The wealthiest and most powerful financial institution in the known world, famous for its discretion and the mantra 'The Iron Bank will have its due'. Founded in an abandoned iron mine, it is governed by a group of descendants known as keyholders. The bank frequently funds kings and city-states, but it is known to support rivals of those who fail to repay their debts. [Seat]: Braavos.
707.name: Organization: Iron Bank of Braavos

708.content: Valyrian Steel: A rare metal forged with magic and spells in the ancient Valyrian Freehold. It is lighter, stronger, and sharper than any other steel, characterized by distinctive ripples in the blade. Since the Doom of Valyria, the secret of its creation has been lost, making surviving items priceless heirlooms often held by Great Houses. [Origin]: Valyria.
708.name: General Lore: Valyrian Steel

709.content: Wildfire: A volatile, highly flammable liquid that burns with a green flame and cannot be easily extinguished. Produced by the Alchemists' Guild through arcane rituals, it is regarded as a 'close cousin' to dragonflame. It is notoriously dangerous to store and handle, growing more unstable with age. [Affiliations]: Alchemists' Guild.
709.name: General Lore: Wildfire

710.content: Dragonglass: A volcanic glass known to maesters as obsidian and to the ancient Valyrians as 'frozen fire'. It is sharp enough to be used for tools and weapons, and it is the only known substance capable of killing the Others. Large deposits are found on the volcanic island of Dragonstone.
710.name: General Lore: Dragonglass
